ἀμοιβηδίς [ἀμοιβή.] In turns Il. 18.506: Od. 18.310.
ἀμοιβοί οἱ [ἀμοιβή.] A relieving force: ἦλθον ἀμοιβοί (as a . . . ) Il. 13.793.

ἀμολγός Sense unknown. (ἐν) νυκτὸς ἀμολγῷ, gen. rendered, in the depth or gloom of night Il. 11.173, Il. 15.324, Il. 22.28, 317: Od. 4.841. (But Sirius, referred to in Il. 22.27 as shining ὀπώρης, is not then seen in the depth of night; and ἀστὴρ ἕσπερος in Il. 22.317 also causes difficulty.)

ἁμός -ή, -όν. Our ( = ἡμέτερος) Il. 6.414, Il. 8.178, Il. 10.448, Il. 13.96, Il. 16.830: Od. 11.166 = 481. (But the sense my (cf. ἡμέτερος 2) is always admissible, and in Il. 6.414, and perh. in Il. 8.178, is preferable.)
ἄμοτος In neut. ἄμοτον as adv., insatiably, continually, incessantly, without pause or intermission Il. 4.440, Il. 5.518, Il. 13.40, 80, Il. 19.300, Il. 22.36, Il. 23.567: Od. 6.83, Od. 17.520.
†ἀμπείρω [ἀμ-, ἀνα- 6.] Nom. pl. masc. aor. pple. ἀμπείραντες. To transfix, spit Il. 2.426.
ἀμπελόεις -εσσα [ἄμπελος.] Rich in vines. Epithet of places Il. 2.561, Il. 3.184, Il. 9.152 = 294.
ἄμπελος -ον, ἡ. A vine Od. 9.110, 133, Od. 24.246.
ἀμπεπαλών contr. aor. pple. ἀναπάλλω.
ἀμπερές [ἀμπείρω.] Passing through. With διά (cf. διαμπερές): διὰ δʼ ἀ. ἰὸς κατέπηκτο Il. 11.377. Cf. Il. 17.309: Od. 21.422.
ἀμπέχω [ἀμπ-, ἀμφι- 3.] To cover Od. 6.225.
ἀμπηδάω [ἀμ-, ἀνα- 1.] To leap up, start up: ἐκ λόχου ἀμπήδησεν Il. 11.379.
ἀμπνεῦσαι contr. aor. infin. ἀναπνέω.
ἄμπνυε contr. aor. imp. ἀναπνέω.
ἀμπνύνθη (ύθη) ἄμπνυτο See ἐμπνύνθη.
ἄμπυξ -υκος. A diadem of metal worn over the forehead Il. 22.469.

ἄμυδις [ἅμα.] 1 Together, all together, in or into a body or mass: θυνόντων ἀ. Il. 10.524. Cf. Il. 9.6, Il. 10.300, Il. 12.385, Il. 13.336, 343, Il. 20.114, 158, 374, Il. 23.217: Od. 4.659, Od. 12.413. 2 Together, at the same time: ἀ. βρόντησε καὶ ἔμβαλε κεραυνόν Od. 12.415 = Od. 14.305. Cf. Od. 5.467.

ἀμύμων -ονος. 1 An epithet of persons of general commendation, noble, illustrious, goodly, or the like: μάντις Il. 1.92, Αἰθιοπῆας 423. Cf. Il. 2.674, Il. 5.247, Il. 6.155, Il. 11.835, Il. 20.236, etc.: Αἰγίσθοιο (app. as a merely conventional epithet) Od. 1.29, Ὀδυσῆος Od. 2.225. Cf. Od. 4.187, Od. 7.29, Od. 8.117, Od. 19.332, Od. 8.325, etc. Of women: ἄκοιτιν Il. 6.374. Cf. Od. 4.4, Od. 7.303, Od. 13.42, Od. 15.15, etc. Of a nymph Il. 14.444. Of a horse Il. 16.152. 2 Sim. of things or abstractions, indicating excellence or perfection: πομπῇ Il. 6.171, ἔργα Il. 9.128, τόξῳ Il. 15.463. Cf. Il. 9.270, Il. 10.19, Il. 13.637, Il. 16.119, Il. 19.245, Il. 23.263: οἶκος Od. 1.232, μῆτις Od. 9.414. Cf. Od. 10.50, Od. 12.261, Od. 14.508, Od. 16.237, Od. 22.442 = 459, Od. 23.145, Od. 24.80, 278. 3 Absol. in neut. pl.: δς ἂν ἀμύμονα εἰδῇ (is of noble heart) (see εἴδω III.12) Od. 19.332.
ἀμύντωρ -ορος, ὁ [ἀμύνω.] A defender or helper Il. 14.449, Il. 15.540, 610: Od. 2.326, Od. 16.256, 261.

ἀμύνω 3 sing. impf. ἄμυνε Il. 13.678, Il. 14.71, Il. 15.731. 3 sing. aor. ἤμυνε Il. 9.599, Il. 13.783. ἄμυνε Il. 4.129, Il. 5.662, Il. 12.402, Il. 17.615. 3 sing. opt. ἀμύναι Il. 12.334, Il. 15.736. Imp. ἄμυνον Il. 1.456, Il. 15.375: Od. 22.208. Infin. ἀμῦναι Il. 1.67, Il. 9.576, Il. 16.75, Il. 24.489, etc.: Od. 2.59, Od. 17.538. Aor. opt. mid. ἀμυναίμην Od. 2.62, Od. 12.114. (ἀπ-, ἐπ-, προσ-.) 1 To ward off, keep off, avert: λοιγόν Il. 5.603, 662, Il. 18.450, Il. 20.98. Il. 24.489. Cf. Il. 6.463, Il. 9.599, Il. 13.783, Il. 15.375, Il. 17.615: ἀρήν Od. 2.59 = Od. 17.538, Od. 22.208, μνηστῆρας Od. 24.380. To defend oneself against, fight with: δήϊον ἄνδρα Il. 22.84. With dat. of person or thing protected: ἡμῖν λοιγόν Il. 1.67. Cf. Il. 1.341, 398, 456, Il. 4.129, Il. 9.435, 495, Il. 11.277, 588, Il. 12.334, Il. 13.426, Il. 15.736, Il. 16.32, 512, 835, Il. 17.511, Il. 18.129, Il. 20.124: ἄστεϊ νηλεὲς ἦμαρ Od. 8.525. With genit. : κῆρας παιδός Il. 12.402. Cf. Il. 4.11, Il. 15.731, Il. 16.75, 80. 2 To defend, protect, succour, fight for, come to the rescue of. With dat.: ὤρεσσιν Il. 5.486, σοῖσιν ἔτῃσιν Il. 6.262. Cf. Il. 9.518, 602, Il. 11.674, Il. 13.464, 481, Il. 14.71, 362, 369, Il. 15.73, 255, 492 (supplying αὐτοῖς), 688, Il. 16.265, Il. 17.273, 563, 703, Il. 21.215, 231, 414: Ἀργείοισιν Od. 11.500, 518. Cf. Od. 16.257, Od. 21.195, 197, Od. 22.214. With genit.: οὗ παιδός Il. 16.522. Cf. Il. 13.109. 3 Absol. to play the defender, fight, show fight: ἐξελθεῖν καὶ ἀμῦναι Il. 9.576. Cf. Il. 13.312, 678, 814, Il. 17.182: οὐ τοῖοι ἀμυνέμεν Od. 2.60. 4 In mid. a To ward or keep off from oneself: ἀμύνετο νηλεὲς ἦμαρ Il. 11.484, Il. 13.514. Cf. Il. 17.510. Sim. ἄνδρας θηρητῆρας ἀμύνονται πεπρὶ τέκνων Il. 12.170. To defend oneself against, fight with: σκύλλην Od. 12.114. b To defend, protect, fight for. With genit.: Καλυδῶνος Il. 9.531. Cf. Il. 12.155, 179, Il. 16.561. With ablative: ναῦφιν Il. 13.700. c Absol., to play the defender, fight: περὶ νηῶν Il. 12.142. Cf. Il. 12.227, 243, Il. 15.496, Il. 16.556, 622, Il. 18.173, Il. 24.500: ἧός μοι ἀμύνεσθαι πάρʼ ὀϊστοί Od. 22.106. Cf. Od. 2.62, Od. 22.116.
ἀμύσσω 2 sing. fut. ἀμύξεις Il. 1.243. (κατ-.) To tear, lacerate: χερσὶ στήθεα Il. 19.284. Fig.: θυμόν Il. 1.243.
ἀμφαγαπάζω [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 3.] 1 To welcome (with suppressed notion of embracing) Od. 14.381. 2 To show love to, treat with affection. In mid. Il. 16.192.
†ἀμφαγείρω [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 3.] 3 pl. aor. mid. ἀμφαγέροντο. In mid., to come together or gather round. With acc.: θεαί μιν ἀμφαγέροντο Il. 18.37.
ἀμφαδά [ἀμφαίνω = ἀναφαίνω.] Openly, without concealment: μὴ ἀ. ἔργα γένοιτο (disclosure should take place) Od. 19.391.
ἀμφάδιος [as ἀμφαδά.] 1 Open, public: γάμον Od. 6.288. 2 Adv. of acc. fem. form ἀμφαδίην = ἀμφαδά. Il. 7.196, Il. 13.356: Od. 5.120.
ἀμφαδόν [as ἀμφάδιος.] Openly, without concealment or subterfuge: βαλέειν Il. 7.243, ἀγορευέμεν Il. 9.370: ἠὲ δόλῳ ἢ ἀ. Od. 1.296, Od. 11.120, ἢ ἀ. ἦε κρυφηδόν Od. 14.330 = Od. 19.299.
ἀμφαραβέω [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 3.] To rattle or ring about one: τεύχεʼ ἀμφαράβησεν Il. 21.408.
ἀμφασίη ἡ [ἀμ- (= ἀ-1) + φα-, φημί.] Speechlessness: ἀ. μιν λάβεν Il. 17.695: = Od. 4.704.

†ἀμφαφάω [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 3.] Pres. pple. ἀμφαφόων Od. 8.196. Acc. pl. ἀμφαφόωντας Od. 19.586. Fem. ἀμφαφόωσα Od. 4.277. 3 pl. impf. mid. ἀμφαφόωντο Od. 15.462. Infin. ἀμφαφάασθαι Il. 22.373: Od. 8.215, Od. 19.475. 1 To put the hands round, handle. In mid.: [ὅρμον] ἀμφαφόωντο Od. 15.462. Cf. Od. 19.475. So μαλακώτερος ἀμφαφάασθαι (easier to deal with) Il. 22.373. To handle and use: τόξον Od. 19.586. In mid. Od. 8.215. 2 To put the hands on in passing round: κοῖλον λόχον (the wooden horse) Od. 4.277. 3 Absol., to feel about with the hands Od. 8.196.
ἀμφέθετο 3 sing. aor. mid. ἀμφιτίθημι.
ἀμφεκάλυψε 3 sing. aor. ἀμφικαλύπτω.
ἀμφέξεσα aor. ἀμφιξέω.
ἄμφεπε 3 sing. impf. See ἀμφιέπω.
†ἀμφέρχομαι [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 3.] 3 sing. aor. ἀμφήλυθε. To come round, be diffused round. With acc. : ἀϋτή με Od. 6.122, ἀϋτμή με Od. 12.369.
ἀμφέσταν 3 pl. aor. ἀμφίστημι.
ἀμφέχανε 3 sing. aor. ἀμφιχαίνω.
ἀμφεχύθη ἀμφέχυτο 3 sing. aor. pass. ἀμφιχέω.
ἀμφήκης Neut. ἄμφηκες. [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 2 + ἀκή, point, edge.] Two-edged Il. 10.256, Il. 21.118: Od. 16.80, Od. 8.341.
ἀμφήλυθε 3 sing. aor. ἀμφέρχομαι.
ἀμφηρεφής [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 1 + ἐρέφω.] Covering on both sides: φαρέτρην (i.e. enclosing (the arrows)) Il. 1.45.
ἀμφήριστος [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 1 + ἐρίζω.] Disputed on both sides. In neut. qualifying a vague notion the state of things; hence, a dead heat: ἀμφήριστόν κʼ ἔθηκεν Il. 23.382, 527.

ἀμφί I Adv. 1 a On both sides: ἀ. ὀβελοῖσιν ἔπειραν (so that the spits appeared on both sides) Il. 1.465 = Il. 2.428. Cf. Il. 9.210: ξύλα τʼ ἀ. καὶ οἰσέμεν ὕδωρ (i.e. to be set on either side of the altar) Od. 3.429. Cf. Od. 3.462 = Od. 12.365 = Od. 14.430, Od. 14.75. b In reference to the two sides of the body: ἀ. ὄσσε νὺξ ἐκάλυψεν (both eyes) Il. 5.310 = Il. 11.356. Cf. Il. 6.117, Il. 10.535, etc.: δρεψαμένω ἀ. δειράς Od. 2.153. Cf. Od. 9.389. Sim. in reference to the φρένες (see μέλας 1): μένεος φρένες ἀ. μελαιναι πίμπλαντο Il. 1.103: = Od. 4.661. Cf. Il. 17.83, 499, 573. From side to side: ἀ. μοι χεὶρ ὀδύνῃσιν ἐλήλαται Il. 16.517. 2 Round, about, round about: ἔστασαν Il. 4.330. Cf. Il. 4.328, Il. 5.194, Il. 7.449, Il. 11.417, Il. 14.420, etc.: χλαίνας βάλον Od. 4.50. Cf. Od. 3.32, Od. 4.253, Od. 5.72, Od. 7.14, Od. 9.22, etc. Joined with περί Il. 21.10, Il. 23.191. Fig.: ἀ. μάλα φράζεσθε (look at the matter all round, consider well) Il. 18.254. 3 About or concerning something: τάδʼ ἀ. πονησόμεθα Il. 23.159. Cf. Il. 7.316, Il. 11.776: τὸνδέρον ἀ. θʼ ἕπον Od. 8.61, Od. 19.421. II Prep. (sometimes (without anastrophe) following the case). 1 With dat. a On each side of: ἀ. κῦμα στείρῃ ἴαχεν Il. 1.481, ἀ. ὤμοισιν βάλετο ξίθος (i.e. the belt rested on both shoulders) Il. 2.45, θώρηκας ῥήξειν ἀ. στήθεσσιν (i.e. the belt rested on both shoulders) Il. 2.45, θώρηκας ῥήξειν ἀ. στήθεσσιν (i.e. the two γύαλα) 544, ἀ. ὀχέεσσι βάλε κύκλα Il. 5.722, ἀ. σθοῖς ὀχέεσσιν (app., sprawling over them) Il. 18.231, ἀ. πυρίποδα (astraddle over it) 344, etc.: ἀ. ἑνὶ δούρατι βαῖνεν (bestriding it) Od. 5.371, ἀ. πυπὶ χαλκὸν ἰήνατε Od. 8.426, etc. So with locative: ἱδρώσει τελαμὼν ἀ. στήθεσφιν Il. 2.388. In reference to a shield protecting on both sides (cf. ἀμφίβροτος): δῄουν ἀ. στήθεσσι βοείας Il. 5.452. Cf. Il. 10.149 (across the shoulders), Il. 11.527, Il. 16.108, Il. 17.132, etc. For βαίνειν ἀ. τινι see βαίνω I.6.a, and cf. ἀμφιβαίνω 4. Joined with περί Od. 11.609. b Round, about, round about: τυθωέϊ Il. 2.782, εἰδώλῳ Il. 5.451. Cf. Il. 9.654, Il. 13.496, Il. 14.447, Il. 15.608, etc.: πόλει Od. 6.9, γούνασιν Od. 7.142. Cf. Od. 4.245, Od. 10.262, Od. 11.423, Od. 14.23, etc. So with locative: ἀ. κυνέην κεφαλῆφιν ἔθηκεν Il. 10.257. Cf. Il. 10.261: Od. 16.145. In reference to something transfixing: ἀ. σιδήρῳ Il. 23.30. Cf. Od. 12.395. With notion of protection: ἀ. βόεσσιν Il. 15.587. Cf. Il. 17.369. c About, concerning, for, touching, in the matter of: Ἑλένῃ Il. 3.70. Cf. Il. 3.254, Il. 7.408, Il. 11.672, Il. 13.382, Il. 16.647, etc.: τεύχεσιν ἀ. Ἀχιλῆος Od. 11.546. Cf. Od. 1.48, Od. 4.151, Od. 14.338, Od. 17.555, Od. 22.227, etc. 2 With acc. a On each side of : ἀ. κῆρ Il. 16.481. b Round, about, round about: ἀ. ἅλα(i.e. round the bay) Il. 1.409, ἀ. Αἴαντε (with them, under their leadership) Il. 6.436, τὴν ἑτέρην πόλιν ἀ. Il. 18.509. Cf. Il. 2.417, Il. 3.231, Il. 5.314, Il. 13.335, Il. 16.290, Il. 17.290, Il. 22.473, etc.: Ἰαρδάνου ἀ. ῥέεθρα Od. 3.292. Cf. Od. 3.163, Od. 8.502, Od. 11.419, Od. 17.65, Od. 22.281, Od. 24.37, etc. Joined with περί Il. 2.305, Il. 17.760.–οἱ ἀ. τινα, a person and those with him, a group of which the person named is the chief: οἱ δʼ ἀ. Ἀτρεΐωνα ἠγερέθοντο Il. 23.233. With several persons named Il. 3.146. Sim.: οὓς ἑτάρους στέλλοντʼ ἀ. Πελάγοντα Ἀλάστορά τε . . . Il. 4.295 (where P. etc. are included in ὲτάρους). c About, concerning: ἀ. ἔκαστα Od. 19.46.–(/b>3) With genit., about, concerning: μάχεσθον πίδακος ἀ. Il. 16.825. Cf. Od. 8.267.

data.ref: Il. 4.295 (where P. etc. are included in

definition: ἀμφίαλος -ον [ἀμφι- 3 + ἅλς1.] Sea-girt. Epithet of Ithaca Od. 1.386, 395, 401, Od. 2.293, Od. 8.252.
†ἀμφιάχω [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 3 + ϝιϝάχω.] Acc. fem. pf. pple. without redup. ἀμφιαχυῖαν (ἀμφι-ϝακυῖαν). Of a bird, to cry (flying) about: τὴν λάβεν ἀμφιαχυῖαν Il. 2.316.

†ἀμφιβαίνω [ἀμφι- 1, ἀμφι- 3.] 2 sing. pf. ἀμφι-βέβηκας Il. 1.37, 451. 3 sing. -ε Il. 6.355, Il. 16.66: Od. 8.541, Od. 12.74. 3 sing. subj. ἀμφιβεβήκῃ Od. 4.400. 3 sing. plupf. ἀμφιβεβήκει Il. 8.68, Il. 16.777: Od. 9.198. 1 To be round, cover completely, a double (organ) (cf. ἀμφί I.1.b). With acc.: πόνος (ἄχος) φρένας ἀμφιβέβηκεν Il. 7.355: Od. 8.541. 2 To come round, surround. With dat.: Τρώων νέφος νηυσίν Il. 16.66. 3 To be round, envelop, cover up. With acc. Od. 12.74. 4 To have the feet on each side of, bestride (cf. βαίνω I.6.a). With acc. Fig.: ἠέλιος μέσον οὐρανόν (thought of as standing with both feet in the midst of heaven) Il. 8.68, Il. 16.777: Od. 4.400. Hence to protect (a place) as a tutelary power Il. 1.37 = 451: Od. 9.198.

†ἀμφιβάλλω [ἀμφι- 1, ἀμφι- 3.] Aor. pple. ἀμφιβαλών, -όντος Il. 17.742, Il. 23.97: Od. 17.344, Od. 23.192. Fut. mid. ἀμφιβαλεῦμαι Od. 22.103. Aor. infin. ἀμφιβαλέσθαι Od. 6.178. 1 To put round something: [χεῖρας] Od. 17.344. To throw the arms round. With acc.: ἀλλήλους Il. 23.97. To put building materials round. With dat.: θάμνῳ Od. 23.192. 2 Fig., to throw or put (strength) on both sides of something, apply (strength) vigorously: μένοσἀμφιβαλόντες Il. 17.742. 3 In mid., to throw (a garment) round oneself Od. 6.178. To put on a piece of armour Od. 22.103.
ἀμφίβασις ἡ [ἀμφιβαίνω.] Defence of a fallen body (cf. ἀμφιβαίνω 4): Τρώων (by the . . .) Il. 5.623.
ἀμφιβέβηκε 3 sing. pf. ἀμφιβαίνω.
ἀμφίβροτος -η, -ον [ἀμφι- 1 + βροτός.] Protecting on both sides (as well as in front). Epithet of shields Il. 2.389, Il. 11.32, Il. 12.402, Il. 20.281.

ἀμφιγυήεις [prob. ἀμφι- 2 + γυ-, to bend, as in γύαλον, γυρός.] Thus, having a crooked limb on each side. Epithet or a name of Hephaestus Il. 1.607, Il. 14.239, Il. 18.383, 393 = 462, 587, 590, 614: Od. 8.300, 349, 357.

ἀμφίγυος [prob. as ἀμφιγυήεις.] Thus, of spears, (having a head) curved on each side, i.e. leafshaped; or perh., bending to either side, elastic Il. 13.147 = Il. 15.278 = Il. 17.731, Il. 14.26 = Il. 16.637, Il. 15.386, 712: Od. 16.474, Od. 24.527.
†ἀμφιδαίω [ἀμφι- 3 + δαίω1.] 3 sing. pf. ἀμφιδέδηε. To burn or blaze all round. With acc. Fig.: ἀϋτὴ ἄστυ ἀμφιδέδηε Il. 6.329.
ἀμφίδασυς -εια [ἀμφι- 3 + δασύς.] Covered with hair: αἰγίδα Il. 15.309.
ἀμφιδέδηε 3 sing. pf. ἀμφιδαίω.

†ἀμφιδινέω [ἀμφι- 3.] 3 sing. pf. pass. ἀμφιδεδίνηται. (Cf. δινωτός.) To set round in circles, i.e. in strips running round: ᾧ πέρι χεῦμα κασσιτέροιο ἀμφιδεδίνηται Il. 23.562 (the strips on the front plate being app. continued on the back plate and carried round to the front again): κολεὸν ἐλέθαντος ἀμφιδεδίνηται (is surrounded by (a succession of) ivory rings) Od. 8.405.
ἀμφιδρυφής [ἀμφι- 1 + δρυθ-, δρύπτω.] Having both cheeks torn in mourning: ἄλοχος Il. 2.700.
ἀμφίδρυφος -ον [as ἀμφιδρυφής.] Both torn in mourning: παρειαί Il. 11.393.
ἀμφίδυμος [ἀμφι- 2 + -δυμος as in δίδυμος.] Twofold, double: λιμένες Od. 4.847.

ἀμφιέλισσα -ης [ἀμφι- 1 + (V) ἑλίσσω.] Epithet of ships, wheeling both ways; hence, easily directed, handy Il. 2.165 = 181, Il. 9.683, Il. 13.174 = Il. 15.549, Il. 17.612, Il. 18.260: Od. 3.162, Od. 6.264, Od. 7.9, 252, Od. 9.64, Od. 10.91, 156 = Od. 12.368, Od. 14.258 = Od. 17.427, Od. 15.283, Od. 8.390.

†ἀμφιέννυμι [ἀμφι- 3 + (ϝ)έννυμι.] Fut. ἀμφιέσω Od. 5.167. Aor. opt. ἀμφιέσαιμι Od. 18.361. Fem. pple. ἀμφιέσασα Od. 5.264, Od. 15.369. 3 pl. aor. mid. ἀμφιέσαντο Od. 23.142. Imp. pl. ἀμφιέσασθε Od. 23.131. 1 To put (garments) on a person Od. 5.167, 264, Od. 15.369, Od. 18.361. 2 In mid., to put (garments) on oneself Od. 23.131, 142.

ἀμφιέπω [ἀμφι- 3, ἀμφι- 4 + (σ)έπω1.] With elision of the ι (on the loss of the σ) 3 sing. impf. ἄμφεπε Il. 17.124, Il. 18.348: Od. 8.437. 3 pl. -ον Il. 18.559, Il. 23.167, Il. 24.622. 1 To handle, attend to, do what is needful to: ἵππους Il. 19.392. Cf. Il. 5.667, Il. 18.559, Il. 23.167, Il. 24.622. 2 To marshal, draw up in order Il. 2.525. 3 To manage, conduct: τάφον Il. 24.804. 4 In sinister sense, to employ oneself about for evil, work for the destruction of, [Τρῶας] Od. 3.118. 5 Of fire, to bring itself to bear upon, lap round: πρύμνην Il. 16.124. Cf. Il. 18.348: = Od. 8.437.
ἀμφιζάνω [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 3.] To settle about, be deposited upon. With dat. Of ashes: χιτῶνι Il. 18.25.
ἀμφιθαλής [ἀμφι- 2 + θάλλω.] Absol., one who has both parents alive Il. 22.496.
ἀμφίθετος -ον [ἀμφι- 2 + θε-, τίθημι.] Two-handled: φιάλην Il. 23.270, φιάλη 616.
ἀμφιθέω [ἀμφι- 3.] To run about or round. With acc., [πόριες] ἀμφιθέουσι μητέρας Od. 10.413.

ἀμφικαλύπτω [ἀμφι- 1, ἀμφι- 3.] Fut. ἀμφικαλύψω Il. 14.343. Infin. -ειν Od. 8.569, Od. 13.177. 3 sing. aor. ἀμφεκάλυψε Il. 3.442, Il. 5.68, Il. 8.331, Il. 16.350, etc.: Od. 4.180, 618, Od. 15.118. 3 sing. subj. ἀμφικαλύψῃ Od. 8.511, Od. 13.183, Od. 20.86. Pple. ἀμφικαλύψας Od. 5.493, Od. 14.349, Od. 23.17. Infin. ἀμφικαλύψαι Od. 13.152, 158. 1 To cover both of one's . . . (cf. ἀμφί I.1 b ). Of sleep: βλέθαρʼ ἀμφικαλύψας Od. 5.493. Cf. Od. 20.86, Od. 23.17. To cover completely a double (organ) (cf. ἀμφί I 1.b): ἔρως φρένας ἀμφεκάλυψεν Il. 3.442, Il. 14.294. 2 To cover up all round, enfold, conceal, contain Il. 2.262, Il. 23.91. Of a city, to receive within its walls Od. 8.511. Of a house, to receive as a guest Od. 4.618 = Od. 15.118. Fig. of death or fate Il. 5.68, Il. 12.116, Il. 16.350, Il. 20.417: Od. 4.180. 3 To put round, cover or protect with. With dat. of what is covered or protected: σἀκος οἱ Il. 8.331 = Il. 13.420. Cf. Il. 14.343: Od. 14.349. Sim., to put round (something) so as to isolate (it): ὄρος πόλει Od. 8.569, Od. 13.152, 158, 177, 183.
†ἀμφικεάζω [ἀμφτ- 3.] Aor. pple. ἀμφικεάσσας. To split off all round (something). With acc.: τὸ μέλαν δρυὸς ἀμφικεάσσας (splitting off (the outside wood) all round the dark heart) Od. 14.12.
ἀμφίκομος [ἀμφι- 3 + κόμη.] With foliage all round, thick-leafed: θάμνῳ Il. 17.677.

ἀμφικύπελλος [ἀμφι- 2 + (perh.) *κυπέλη, handle, conn. with κώπη.] Two-handled: δέπας Il. 1.584, Il. 6.220, Il. 9.656, Il. 23.219, 656, 663, 667, 699: Od. 3.63, Od. 8.89, Od. 13.57, Od. 15.102, 120, Od. 22.86, δέπα Od. 20.153.
ἀμφιλαχαίνω [ἀμφι- 3 + λαχαίνω, to dig.] To dig round about. With acc.: θυτόν Od. 24.242.
ἀμφιλύκη [ἀμφι- 1 (giving the notion of hesitation between two sides, hence of doubtfulness) + *λύκη = L. lux.] ἀ. νύξ, the(morning) twilight Il. 7.433.
†ἀμφιμαίομαι [ἀμφι- 3.] Aor. imp. pl. ἀμφιμάσασθε. To carry the hands all round or over (the surface of), wipe all round or over: τραπέζας Od. 20.152.

ἀμφιμάχομαι [ἀμφι- 3, ἀμφι- 4.] 1 With acc., in local sense, to fight round or about: Ἴλιον Il. 6.461. Cf. Il. 9.412, Il. 16.73, Il. 18.208. 2 With genit., to fight for the possession of: τείχεος Il. 15.391. Cf. Il. 16.496 = 533, Il. 18.20.
ἀμφιμέλαιναι See μέλας 1.
†ἀμφιμυκάομαι [ἀμφι- 3.] 3 sing. pf. ἀμφιμέμυκε. To resound or echo all round Od. 10.227.
ἀμφινέμω [ἀμφι- 3.] In mid., to have one's lot, dwell, round or about. With acc. With place-names Il. 2.521, 574, 585, 634, 649, 655, 835, 853, Il. 18.186: Od. 19.132.
†ἀμφιξέω [ἀμφι- 3.] Aor. ἀμφέξεσα. To smooth all round: κορμόν Od. 23.196.
ἀμφιπέλω [ἀμφι- 3.] Of sound, to come round (hearers). With dat. In mid.: ἀοιδὴ ἀκουόντεσσιν Od. 1.352.

ἀμφιπένομαι [ἀμφι- 4.] To busy oneself about, attend to Il. 13.656, Il. 19.278. To attend upon Od. 15.467. To treat surgically Il. 4.220, Il. 16.28: Od. 19.455. In sinister sense: Ἀστεροπαῖον ἐγχέλυες ἀμφεπένοντο (made a meal of him) Il. 21.203. Cf. Il. 23.184.
ἀμφιπεριστέφω [ἀμφι- 3 + περι- 1.] To put round. With dat. Fig., in pass., to be put round as a crown, adorn: οὔ οἱ χάρις ἀμφιπεριστέθεται ἐπέεσσιν Od. 8.175.
ἀμφιπεριστρωφάω [ἀμφι- 3 + περι- 2.] To turn about in all directions: ἵππους Il. 8.348.
†ἀμφιπίπτω [ἀμφι- 3.] Aor. pple. fem. ἀμφιπεσοῦσα. To fall (with the arms) round, embrace. With acc.: πόσιν Od. 8.523.

ἀμφιπολεύω [ἀμφίπολος.] To busy oneself about, take care of, tend: ἐμὸν βίον Od. 18.254 = Od. 19.127, ὄρχατον Od. 24.244, 257. In sinister sense: ἔδοσαν ἐρινύσιν ἀμφιπολεύειν (i.e. handed them over to their tender mercies) Od. 20.78.

ἀμφίπολος -ου, ἡ [ἀμφι- 4 + -πολος, conn. with πολεύω.] A handmaid, a female attendant or servant, hardly to be distinguished from δμῳή. (The words are sometimes used indifferently; cf. Od. 6.52 with 307, and 84 with 99. But in Od. 22.483, 484 ἀμφίπολοι seem to be personal attendants and δμῳαί the other servants.) Il. 3.143, 422, Il. 6.286, 324, 372, 399, 491, 499, Il. 18.417 (i.e. representations), Il. 22.442, 461, Il. 24.304: Od. 1.136, Od. 6.18, Od. 7.232, Od. 18.198, Od. 19.90, Od. 23.227, etc. Of Circe's servants Od. 10.348, 368, Od. 12.18. With γυνή. See γυνή 3. With word indicating the servant's country of origin: σικελή Od. 24.366. Her office: ταμίην Il. 24.302: Od. 16.152.
ἀμφιπονέομαι [ἀμφι- 4.] To busy oneself about, attend to: τάθον Od. 20.307. To do the offices of a second to: εὐρύαλον Il. 23.681.
ἀμφιποτάομαι [ἀμφι- 3.] To fly round and round Il. 2.315.
ἀμφίρυτος -η [ἀμφι- 3 + ῥυ-, ῥέω.] Flowed round (by the sea), sea-girt Od. 1.50, 198, Od. 11.325, Od. 12.283.

ἀμφίς [ἀμφί.] I Adv. 1 On both sides: ᾧ ῥόπαλʼ ἀ. ἐάγῃ (i.e. across his back) Il. 11.559, δούρασιν ἀ. [βάλεν] (with spears from both hands, with both spears at once) Il. 21.162. 2 A part, asunder: ἀ. φράζονται (have different views) Il. 2.13 = 30 = 67, ἔχουσα ἀ. (one in each scale) Il. 12.434, τόξων ἀϊκὰς ἀ. μένον (at a safe distance) Il. 15.709, ἀ. ἀρωγοί (partisans, some of one, some of the other) Il. 18.502, ἀ. ἀριζήλω (standing out from the others) 519, ἀ. ἄλλʼ ἀποδάσσεσθαι (in addition) Il. 22.117, ἀ. ὁδοῦ Il. 23.393 (see ὁδός 1). Cf. Il. 13.345, 706: ζυγὸν ἀ. ἔχοντες (supporting it at either end) Od. 3.486 = Od. 15.184, τιμὴν ἀ. ἄγοντες (in addition) Od. 22.57. Cf. Od. 1.54. 3 Absent: ἀ. ἐόντα Od. 24.218. Sim. of separation from a person Od. 19.221. 4 Between: ὀλίγη ἦν ἀ. ἄρουρα (between the heaps or rows) Il. 3.115. 5 Round, about: τάθρος ἀ. ἐοῦσα (surrounding) Il. 7.342, τάρταρος ἀ. [ἐστιν] Il. 8.481. Cf. Il. 9.464, Il. 14.123, Il. 23.330, Il. 24.488: Od. 8.340, 476. II Prep. 1 With genit. a Apart from, at a distance from: διός Il. 8.444. Cf. Od. 14.352, Od. 16.267. b About, concerning: ἅρματος ἀ. ἰδών (seeing to it) Il. 2.384. 2 With dat., round, about: ἄξονι Il. 5.723. 3 With acc. a On each side of: δύο δʼ ἀ. ἕκαστον [δίθρον] (one on each side of each) Il. 11.748. b Round, about: ἕκαστον Il. 11.634. Cf. Il. 14.274, Il. 15.225: Od. 6.266, Od. 7.4, Od. 9.399.

†ἀμφίστημι [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 3.] 3 pl. aor. ἀμφέσταν Il. 18.233, Il. 23.695. 3 sing. impf. mid. ἀμφίστατο Il. 24.712. 3 pl. -αντο Il. 11.733. In aor. and mid., to stand round or about Il. 18.233, Il. 23.695, Il. 24.712. To stand round or about. With acc.: ἄστυ Il. 11.733.
†ἀμφιστρατάομαι [ἀμφι- 3.] 3 pl. impf. ἀμφεστρατόωντο. To be established round, besiege. With acc.: θρυόεσσαν Il. 11.713.
ἀμφιστρεφής [app. ἀμφι- 3 + στρέφω.] Thus, twisted about: κεφαλαὶ τρεῖς δράκοντος ἀμφιστρεφέες Il. 11.40 (i.e. two twisted about the third).

†ἀμφιτίθημι [ἀμφι- 1, ἀμφι- 3.] 3 sing. aor. mid. ἀμφέθετο Od. 8.431. Aor. fem. pple. pass. ἀμφιτεθεῖσα Il. 10.271. 1 To put round or about something Il. 10.271. 2 In mid., to put on, arm oneself with: ξίφος Od. 8.431 (i.e. the belt rested on both shoulders).
ἀμφιτρομέω [ἀμφι- 4.] To tremble for. With genit.: τοῦ Od. 4.820.
ἀμφίφαλος -ον [ἀμφι- 2 + θάλος.] With two θάλοι: κυνέην Il. 5.743 = Il. 11.41.
ἀμφιφορεύς -ῆος, ὁ [ἀμφι- 2 + θορ-, θέρω.] A two-handled jar Il. 23.92, 170: Od. 2.290, 349, 379, Od. 9.164, 204, Od. 13.105 (of natural formations in a cave), Od. 24.74.

data.ref: Od. 13.105 (of natural formations in a cave),

definition: †ἀμφιχαίνω [ἀμφι- 3.] 3 sing. aor. ἀμφέχανε. To gape round. With acc.: ἐμὲ κήρ (gaped for me) Il. 23.79.

ἀμφιχέω [ἀμφι- 3.] 3 sing. aor. pass. ἀμφέχυτο Il. 2.41. ἀμφθεχύθη Od. 4.716. Pple. ἀμφιχυθείς Il. 14.253, Il. 23.63: Od. 16.214. Infin. ἀμφιχυθῆναι Il. 23.764. 1 To pour or shed round or about. Of dust: πάρος κόνιν ἀμφιχυθῆναι (had settled down again) Il. 23.764. 2 Fig., in pass., of sound, to come round. With acc.: ἀμφέχυτό μιν ὀμφή Il. 2.41. Of sleep, to be shed round one, come upon one Il. 14.253 Il. 23.63. Of grief, to come upon. With acc.: τὴν ἄχος ἀμφεχύθη Od. 4.716. So of a bodily action, to embrace (a person): ἀμφιχυθεὶς πατέρα Od. 16.214. Cf. Od. 22.498.
ἀμφίχυτος [ἀμφιχέω.] Poured round or about; hence of heaped-up earth: τεῖχος Il. 20.145.

ἀμφότερος -η, -ον [ἄμφω.] 1 Both. a Of two persons, etc. In dual or (more freq.) in pl. α Absol.: ἐξαίνυτο θυμὸν ἀμφοτέρω Il. 5.156. Cf. Il. 3.208, Il. 4.38, Il. 5.261, Il. 7.3, etc.: ἀμφοτέρους ἱέρευσεν Od. 14.74. Cf. Od. 3.37, Od. 11.212, Od. 18.17, Od. 8.214, etc. β With sb. or pron.: ἀμφοτέρω σθῶϊ Il. 7.280, ἐπʼ ἀμφοτέρους πόδας (one after the other) Il. 13.281. Cf. Il. 4.521, Il. 5.163, Il. 8.115, Il. 12.382, etc.: ἀμφοτέρῃσιν χερσίν Od. 4.116. Cf. Od. 3.136, Od. 4.282, Od. 5.414, Od. 12.239, etc. With sb. to be supplied: ἀμφοτέρῃσι [χερσίν], with both hands Il. 5.416: Od. 10.264, Od. 11.594, Od. 17.356, Od. 18.28. b In pl. of two groups of persons. α Absol.: ἀμφοτέρων βέλεα Il. 8.67. Cf. Il. 3.416, Il. 4.16, Il. 6.120, Il. 13.303, etc.: φιλότητα μετʼ ἀμφοτέροισιν Od. 24.476. Cf. Od. 10.204, Od. 24.546. β With pron.: τοὺς ἀμφοτέρους Il. 20.54. 2 In neut. ἀμφότερον as adv., both. Followed by . . . τε . . . τε Il. 3.179, Il. 4.145. By . . . τε καὶ . . . Il. 4.60 = Il. 18.365, Il. 13.166. By . . . τε . . . δὲ . . . Il. 7.418. By καὶ Od. 14.505. By . . . τε καὶ . . . καὶ . . . Od. 15.78.

ἀμφοτέρωθεν [ἀμφότερος + -θεν 1.] 1 From both sides: ὦρτʼ ἀϋτὴ ἀ. Il. 15.313. Cf. Il. 12.431. Of plainting strands of a rope, across and across Od. 10.167. 2 On both sides, on either side: πλῆμναί εἰσιν ἀ. Il. 5.726. Cf. Il. 12.55, Il. 16.563, Il. 17.440, Il. 20.170, Il. 23.628: Od. 22.404. On both edges: ἀ. ἀκαχμένον Od. 5.235, Od. 22.80. At both ends: ἅψας ἀ. Od. 8.408. Of stating alternatives: ἐρέω ἀ. Od. 12.58. 3 In both directions: θόως γένετʼ ἀ. Il. 15.669. With περί, app., in both directions so as to meet: περὶ ἕρκος ἐλήλαται ἀ. Od. 7.113. Cf. Od. 10.88.
ἀμφοτέρωσε [ἀμφότερος + -σε.] In both directions: γεγωνέμεν ἀ. Il. 8.223 = Il. 11.6, ἀ. λίθοι πωτῶντο Il. 12.287.
ἀμφουδίς [prob. ἀμφι- 3 + an unknown element + advbl. -δις.] App., by the middle: ἀ. ἀείρας Od. 17.237.
†ἀμφράζομαι [ἀμ-, ἀνα- 6.] 3 sing. aor. opt. ἀμφράσσαιτο. To remark, notice: οὐλήν Od. 19.391.

ἄμφω Only in nom. and acc. of same form. Both. Constructed with dual or pl. 1 Of two persons, etc. a Absol.: ἀ. θιλέουσα Il. 1.196. Cf. Il. 1.259, Il. 2.767, Il. 3.148, Il. 5.153, etc.: ἀ. ἱέσθην Od. 3.344. Cf. Od. 8.316, Od. 10.138, Od. 12.424, Od. 13.296, Od. 15.366, Od. 18.65, 372. b With sb. or pron.: ἀ. χεῖρε Il. 4.523. Cf. Il. 5.258, Il. 6.19, Il. 7.255, Il. 11.782, etc.: τοὺς ἀ. Od. 11.301. Cf. Od. 5.453, Od. 8.135, Od. 16.15, Od. 18.89, etc. 2 Of two groups of persons: ἀριθμηθήμεναι ἀ. Il. 2.124.
ἄμφωτος [ἀμφ-, ἀμφι- 2 + ὠτ-, οὖς.] Having two ears (for handles) : ἄλεισον Od. 22.10.
ἀμώμητος [ἀ-1 + μωμάομαι.] Not to be blamed; hence, unerring (in counsel): πουλυδάμαντος Il. 12.109.

ἄν1. Conditional or limiting particle. (Cf. κεν.) For the uses with subj., opt. and fut., aor. and impf. indic. in protasis and apodosis see 6. 1 With subj.: τάχʼ ἂν θυμὸν ὀλέσσῃ Il. 1.205. Cf. Il. 18.192, Il. 22.505: ἐγὼ ἂν ξεῖνος ἔω Od. 9.17. Cf. Od. 4.240, Od. 11.328, 517, Od. 12.81. In Il. 22.50 (ἀπολυσόμεθα) : Od. 4.240, Od. 11.328, 517 (μυθήσομαι), Od. 6.221 (λοέσσομαι) may be aor. subj. or fut. indic. 2 With opt. in potential or fut. sense: τῶν οὐκ ἄν τι θέροις Il. 1.301. Cf. Il. 2.250 (conveying an order), Il. 3.52 (will you not . . .?), 66, Il. 5.32, 362, Il. 6.141, Il. 9.77, Il. 10.204, Il. 13.741, Il. 14.58, Il. 22.108, Il. 24.437, etc.: πῶς ἂν Ὀδυσῆος λαθοίμην; Od. 1.65. Cf. Od. 3.232, Od. 4.78, Od. 6.57, 300, Od. 10.573, Od. 20.135 (do not . . .), Od. 22.325, etc. 3 In potential sense in reference to the past in suppositions contrary to fact. a With impf. or aor. indic.: ἦ τʼ ἂν κέρδιον ἦεν Il. 5.201 = Il. 22.103, οὐκ ἂν θυμὸν ὤρινεν Il. 19.271. Cf. Il. 8.455, Il. 13.676, Il. 16.638: οὐκ ἂν τόσσʼ ἀγόρευες (would not have . . .) Od. 2.184. Cf. Od. 9.211, 228, 334. b With pres. or aor. opt.: ἦ ἄν ὕστατα λωβήσαιο Il. 1.232 = Il. 2.242. Cf. Il. 1.271, Il. 4.223, Il. 5.85 Il. 13.127: οὐκ ἄν ὀχλίσσειαν Od. 9.241. 4 With infin. in indirect discourse: καὶ δʼ ἂν τοῖς ἄλλοισιν ἔθη παραμυθήσασθαι Il. 9.684. 5 Joined with κεν. See κεν 5. 6 For uses in protasis with εἰ and in the corresponding relative sentences see Table at end II.B.a 3 subj., (D) (7) subj., (23) opt., III.B.a 3 subj., (D) (11) fut., (34) (35) (36) (37) (38) (43) (44) subj., (49) (65) opt. For uses in apodosis see II.C.a 3 aor. or impf. indic., (6) opt., c.2 opt., (D) (6) opt., (23) fut., (30) opt., (52) subj., (57) (63) opt. For ὅτʼ ἄν (not in protasis) see ὅτε 1.a.γ, b.α b.δ b.ε, 4. For ὄφρʼ ἅν (not in protasis) see ὄφρα 1.b, ὄφρα 1.c, 5.a b . For ὡς ἄν (not in protasis) see ὡς 7.a, b.β, 8.α 8.γ, b.γ.

data.quote: καὶ δʼ ἂν τοῖς ἄλλοισιν ἔθη παραμυθήσασθαι

definition: ἄν2. See next.

ἀνά Also in form ἄν and in assimilated form ἄμ. I Adv. 1 Up, upwards, in an upward direction, on to something: ἂν Χρυσηΐδα βήσομεν (put her on board) Il. 1.143, ἀνὰ δʼ ἔστη Il. 2.100, ἂν δʼ ἔβη (mounted) Il. 3.261, ἀνʼ ἔντεα λέγοντες (gathering them up) Il. 11.755. Cf. Il. 1.310, Il. 3.268, Il. 5.798, Il. 17.541, Il. 21.361, Il. 22.77, etc.: ἂν δʼ αὐτοὶ βάντες (going on board) Od. 2.419 = Od. 4.579. Cf. Od. 6.253, Od. 8.3, Od. 9.468 (see νεύω 3), Od. 13.56, Od. 17.262 (see βάλλω II.4), etc. 2 Back, reversal of action: ἀνά τʼ ἔδραμʼ ὀπίσσω Il. 5.599, ἀνὰ δὲ σχέο Il. 7.110 (see ἔχω IV.1.b): ἀνὰ πρυμνήσια λῦσαι Od. 9.178 = 562 = Od. 11.637 = Od. 12.145 = Od. 15.548. 3 Indicating extension or diffusion: ἀνʼ ἱστία πέτασσαν Il. 1.480, μέλανες ἀνὰ βότρυες ἦσαν Il. 18.562: ἀνὰ κρητῆρα κέρασσεν Od. 3.390. Cf. Od. 4.41, 783 = Od. 8.54, Od. 10.506, Od. 24.343. II Prep. 1 With dat., on, upon: ἀνὰ σκήπτρῳ Il. 1.15 = 374. Cf. Il. 14.352, Il. 15.152: ἂμ πέτρῃσιν Od. 5.156. Cf. Od. 11.128 = Od. 23.128 = Od. 23.275, Od. 24.8. In pregnant sense: ἅρματʼ ἂμ βωμοῖσι τίθει Il. 8.441. Cf. Il. 18.177. 2 With acc. a On to, on, upon: θῆκεν ἀνὰ μυρίκην Il. 10.466. Cf. Il. 18.278: ἂν δὲ βήσετο δίφρον Od. 3.481. Cf. Od. 3.492 = Od. 15.145 = 190, Od. 22.176, 193, 239. b Through, throughout, along, over, among, in, on: ἀνὰ στρατόν Il. 1.10, ἂμ πεδίον Il. 5.87. Cf. Il. 1.53, Il. 4.251, Il. 5.74, Il. 9.383, Il. 10.339, Il. 13.308, Il. 16.349, Il. 22.452 (in . . .), etc.: ἂν στόμα Od. 5.456, ἀνʼ ὀρσοθύρην Od. 22.132. Cf. Od. 2.430, Od. 7.72, Od. 10.251, Od. 18.246, Od. 22.18, Od. 24.318, etc. In reference to the mouth as the organ of speech: βασιλῆας ἀνὰ στόμʼ ἔχων (having them passing through the mouth, i.e. talking freely of them) Il. 2.250. In reference to immaterial things: ἀνὰ θυμόν (in his mind) Il. 2.36, ἀνʼ ἰθύν Il. 21.303 (see ἰθύς2 2), etc. Cf. Od. 2.116, Od. 4.638, Od. 8.377 (see ἰθύς2 1), etc. In reference to night as a space of darkness: ἀνὰ νύκτα Il. 14.80. Indicating diffusion: ἀνὰ εἴκοσι μέτρα Od. 9.209. In reference to position: ἀνὰ πρόθυρον τετραμμένος (i.e. with his feet pointing outwards through the doorway) Il. 19.212. 3 With genit., on to, upon: ἂν δὲ νηὸς βαῖνεν (went on board) Od. 2.416. Cf. Od. 9.177, Od. 15.284.
ἄνα1 [ἀνά with anastrophe.] Up ! get up ! rouse yourself ! to work ! ἀλλʼ ἄνα Il. 6.331, Il. 9.247, Il. 18.178: Od. 18.13.
ἄνα2 voc. ἄναξ.

ἀναβαίνω [ἀνα- 1, ἀνα- 2 5.] A Contr. 1 pl. subj. ἀμβαίνωμεν Od. 15.219. Contr. infin. ἀμβαίνειν Od. 9.178, Od. 11.637, etc. 3 sing. aor. ἀνέβη Il. 1.497. 3 sing subj. ἀναβῇ Od. 2.358. 3 sing. opt. ἀναβαίη Od. 22.132. Contr. ἀμβαίη Od. 12.77. Pple. ἀναβάς, -άντος Il. 1.312, 611, Il. 14.287, Il. 16.184, etc.: Od. 3.157, Od. 5.470, Od. 14.353, Od. 15.474, etc. Fem. ἀναβᾶσα Od. 1.362, Od. 17.49, Od. 22.428, etc. Infin. ἀναβήμεναι Od. 1.210. 3 sing. aor. mid. ἀνεβήσετο Od. 23.1. B Aor. pple. pl. mid. ἀναβησάμενοι Od. 15.475. I Intrans. in all forms except (B). 1 To go up, ascend, mount: ἐς λέχος Il. 1.611. Cf. Il. 14.287, Il. 16.184, 657, Il. 22.399: εἰς ὑπερῷα Od. 1.362 = Od. 19.602 = Od. 21.356, Od. 2.358, Od. 4.751 = Od. 17.49 = Od. 23.364, Od. 4.760, Od. 23.1. Cf. Od. 3.483, Od. 5.470, Od. 14.353. Absol. Od. 12.77. In reference to leaving a room: ἀνʼ ὀρσοθύρην Od. 22.132, ἀνέβαινεν ἐς θαλάμους (left the μέγαρον and took his way to . . .) Od. 22.142. Of a voyage from Ithaca to Troy Od. 1.210. 2 To go up to, ascend to. With acc.: οὐρανόν Il. 1.497. Cf. Od. 18.302, Od. 19.600, Od. 22.428. 3 To go on board a ship, embark: ἀναβάντες ἐπέπλεον ὑγρὰ κέλευθα Il. 1.312: ἀναβάντες ἐλαύνομεν Od. 3.157. Cf. Od. 4.473, 842, Od. 9.178 = 562 = Od. 11.637 = Od. 12.145 = Od. 15.548, Od. 12.293, 401, Od. 13.285, Od. 14.252, Od. 15.209, 219, 474. 4 Of reputation, to be spread abroad among. With acc.: φάτις ἀνθρώπους ἀναβαίνει Od. 6.29. II Trans. in form (B), to cause to go on board a ship or embark: νὼ ἀναβησάμενοι Od. 15.475.

ἀναβάλλω [ἀνα- 1, ἀνα- 3.] Contr. 1 pl. subj. mid. ἀμβαλλώμεθα Il. 2.436. 1 To put off, delay: ἄεθλον Od. 19.584. In mid.: ἔργον Il. 2.436. 2 In mid., to strike up, begin (to sing) (cf. βάλλω II.4 and ἀμβλήδην): ἀνεβάλλετʼ ἀείδειν Od. 1.155, Od. 8.266.
ἀναβέβροχε 3 sing. pf. ἀναβρέχω. [LSJ ἀναβέβρυχε]
ἀναβησάμενοι aor. pple. pl. mid. ἀναβαίνω.
ἀνάβλησις ἡ [ἀναβάλλω.] 1 Delay: λύσιος νεκροῖο (in . . .) Il. 24.655. 2 Respite: κακοῦ (from . . .) Il. 2.380.
†ἀναβράχω [ἀνα- 6.] 3 sing. aor. ἀνέβραχε. To clash or rattle loudly: τεύχεα Il. 19.13. Of a door, to creak or grate loudly Od. 21.48.
†ἀναβρέχω [ἀνα- 6 + βρέχω, to wet.] 3 sing. pf. ἀναβέβροχε. To wet or moisten abundantly Il. 17.54.
†ἀναβρόχω [ἀνα- 6 + βρόχω, to swallow.] 3 sing. aor. opt. ἀναβρόξειε Od. 12.240. Neut. aor. pple. pass. ἀναβροχέν Od. 11.586. (κατα-.) To swallow down, swallow Od. 11.586, Od. 12.240.

†ἀναγιγνώσκω [ἀνα- 4, ἀνα- 6.] Aor. ἀνέγνων Od. 4.250. 3 sing. ἀνέγνω Il. 13.734: Od. 1.216, Od. 21.205. 3 sing. opt. ἀναγνοίη Od. 11.144. Genit. sing. masc. pple. ἀναγνόντος Od. 24.346. Dat. sing. fem. ἀναγνούσῃ Od. 19.250, Od. 23.206. 1 To know again, recognize Od. 4.250, Od. 11.144, Od. 19.250 = Od. 23.206, Od. 24.346. 2 To know well, know certainly: [νόον ἐσθλόν] Il. 13.734 (i.e. best knows its value; cf. Od. 6.185). Cf. Od. 1.216, Od. 21.205.

ἀναγκαίη -ης, ἡ. Instrumental ἀναγκαίηφι Il. 20.143. = ἀνάγκη Il. 6.85: Od. 19.73. In dat. ἀναγκαίῃ, of necessityIl. 4.300. In instrumental, by the application of force or strength: δαμέντας Il. 20.143.

ἀναγκαῖος -η, -ον [ἀνάγκη.] 1 Compelled, acting under compulsion: πολεμισταί Od. 24.499. Sim. of slaves Od. 24.210. 2 Imposing compulsion: ἦμαρ ἀναγκαῖον (see ἦμαρ 4.b) Il. 16.836, μύθῳ Od. 17.399 = Od. 20.344.–χρειοῖ ἀναγκαίῃ, by compelling necessity, under the compulsion of necessityIl. 8.57.

ἀνάγκη -ης, ἡ. 1 Necessity, compulsion: ἐπικείσετʼ ἀ. Il. 6.458. Cf. Il. 5.633, Il. 10.418, Il. 20.251, Il. 24.667: Od. 10.273.–ὑπʼ ἀνάγκης, under compulsionOd. 2.110 = Od. 24.146, Od. 19.156. 2 In dat. ἀνάγκῃ. a By or under compulsion or constraint: ἀ. οὔ μιν ἄξω Il. 9.429. Cf. Il. 9.692, Il. 15.199: ὃς ἤειδεν ἀ. Od. 1.154. Cf. Od. 4.557, Od. 5.154, Od. 7.217, Od. 9.98, Od. 14.27, etc. b Under compulsion of circumstances, of necessity, perforce: φεύγοντας Il. 11.150. Cf. Il. 12.178, Il. 14.128, Il. 15.133, etc.: ἄγρην ἐφέπεσκον Od. 12.330. Cf. Od. 13.307, Od. 15.311.

†ἀναγνάμπτω [ἀνα- 3.] 3 pl. aor. ἀνέγναμψαν Od. 14.348. 3 sing. aor. pass. ἀνεγνάμφθη Il. 3.348, Il. 7.259, Il. 17.44. 1 To bend back: ἀνεγνάμφθη αἰχμή Il. 3.348 = Il. 7.259 = Il. 17.44. 2 To unloose Od. 14.348.
ἀναγνοίη 3 sing. aor. opt. ἀναγιγνώσκω.

ἀνάγω [ἀν-, ἀνα- 1.] 1 pl. fut. ἀνάξομεν Od. 18.115. Aor. ἀνήγαγον Il. 15.29. 3 sing. -ε Il. 6.292, Il. 9.338: Od. 3.272, Od. 4.534. 1 To cause to go or take inland Od. 14.272 = Od. 17.441. 2 Of bringing to Troy Il. 3.48, Il. 6.292, Il. 9.338, Il. 13.627. To Argos Il. 15.29. Of taking from Ithaca to the mainland Od. 18.115. 3 Of bringing gifts to temples Il. 8.203. 4 Of conducting to a house: ὅνδε δόμονδε Od. 3.272. Without complementary words Od. 4.534. 5 To bring up to the mark in a contest Od. 18.89. 6 In mid., to put to sea, sail Il. 1.478: Od. 19.202.
ἀναδέδρομε 3 sing. pf. ἀνατρέχω.
†ἀναδέρκομαι [ἀνα- 1.] 3 sing. aor. ἀνέδρακε. To look up Il. 14.436.
ἀναδέσμη -ης, ἡ [ἀνα- 6 + δεσ-, δέω.] A woman's head-dress, app. in the form of a plaited band Il. 22.469.
†ἀναδέχομαι [ἀνα- 6.] 3 sing. aor. ἀνεδέξατο Il. 5.619. 1 pl. aor. ἀνεδέγμεθα Od. 17.563. 1 To receive, catch: σάκος πολλὰ [δούρατα] Il. 5.619. 2 To receive as one's portion Od. 17.563.

†ἀναδύω [ἀνα- 1, ἀνα- 3.] 3 sing. aor. ἀνέδυ Il. 1.359: Od. 5.322. 3 sing. opt. ἀναδύη (for ἀναδυίη) Od. 9.377. Infin. ἀναδῦναι Il. 7.217. Contr. 3 sing. mid. ἀνδύεται Il. 13.225. 3 sing. aor. ἀνεδύσετο Il. 1.496: Od. 5.337. 1 To rise up or emerge from out of. With genit.: ἁλός Il. 1.359. Cf. Od. 5.337. So with acc.: κῦμα Il. 1.496. Absol., to come to the surface Od. 5.322. 2 To go back, retire Il. 7.217. To withdraw from: πόλεμον Il. 13.225. Absol., to draw back, flinch Od. 9.377.
ἀνάεδνος ἡ [app. for ἀνέϝεδνος fr. ἀν- 1 + ἔϝεδνα. See ἕδνα, ἔεδνα.] Without bride-price Il. 9.146, 288, Il. 13.366.

ἀναείρω [ἀν-, ἀνα- 1.] 3 sing. aor. ἀνάειρε Il. 23.614, 725, 729, 778. Infin. ἀναεῖραι Od. 8.298. 1 To lift up, raise Od. 8.298. Of a wrestler hoisting his adversary Il. 23.724, 725, 729. 2 To take up, pick up Il. 23.614, 778.
ἀναθηλέω [ἀνά- 4.] To sprout afresh Il. 1.236.
ἀνάθημα -ατος, τό [ἀνατίθημι.] An accompaniment or accessory: δαιτός Od. 1.152, Od. 21.430.
ἀναθήσει 3 sing. fut. ἀνατίθημι.
ἀναθρῴσκω [ἀνα- 1.] To leap or bound up. Of a stone: ἀναθρῴσκων πέτεται Il. 13.140.
ἀναιδείη -ης, ἡ [ἀναιδής.] 1 Shamelessness, effrontery Il. 1.149, Il. 9.372. 2 Immodesty, unchastity Od. 22.424.

ἀναιδής [ἀν- 1 + αἰδώς.] 1 Careless of the good opinion of others, lost to all sense of decency, shameless, reckless Od. 1.254, Od. 13.376, Od. 17.449, Od. 20.29, 39, 386, Od. 23.37. Absol. Il. 1.158. 2 Of a stone or rock, reckless, careless of what mischief or trouble may ensue Il. 4.521. Cf. Il. 13.139 (as if the rock lent itself to the discharge of the stone): Od. 11.598. Of κυδοιμός figured as a symbol: ἀναιδέα δηϊοτῆτος (app., shamelessly insatiate of . . .) Il. 5.593.
ἀναίμων -ονος [ἀν- 1 + αἷμα.] Bloodless Il. 5.342.
ἀναιμωτί [as ἀναίμων.] Without bloodshed Il. 17.363, 497: Od. 18.149, Od. 24.532.

ἀναίνομαι 3 sing. aor. ἀνήνατο Il. 23.204: Od. 10.18. 3 sing. subj. ἀνήνηται Il. 9.510. Infin. ἀνήνασθαι Il. 7.93: Od. 4.651, Od. 14.239, Od. 18.287. (ἀπ-.) 1 To refuse: δόσιν (i.e. to give it) Od. 4.651, Od. 18.287. To refuse to do something. With infin.: λοιγὸν ἀμῦναι Il. 18.450. Cf. Il. 18.500, Il. 23.204. Absol. Il. 7.93, Il. 9.510, 585, Il. 11.647: Od. 10.18, Od. 14.239. 2 To reject, spurn Il. 9.679. So in reference to a course proposed: ἔργον ἀεικές Od. 3.265. To refuse to have to do with (a person) Od. 8.212. 3 To refuse to entertain an idea; hence, to deny: ἀασάμην, οὐδʼ ἀναίνομαι Il. 9.116. To refuse to entertain expectation Od. 14.149.
ἀναΐξας aor. pple. ἀναΐσσω.

†ἀναιρέω [ἀν-, ἀνα- 1.] Aor. pple. ἀνελών, -όντος Il. 1.301, Il. 23.551, 736: Od. 3.453, Od. 18.16. Mid. Fut. infin. ἀναιρήσεσθαι Od. 21.261, Od. 22.9. 3 sing. aor. ἀνείλετο Il. 13.296. 3 pl. ἀνέλοντο Il. 1.449, Il. 2.410: Od. 20.66. 3 sing. subj. ἀνέληται Il. 16.10. Opt. ἀνελοίμην Od. 18.357. 2 sing. ἀνέλοιο Od. 19.22. Infin. ἀνελέσθαι Il. 16.8, Il. 23.823: Od. 21.117. 1 To take or pick up Il. 23.551: Od. 18.16. 2 To take up into the hands or arms. In mid.: οὐλοχύτας ἀνέλοντο Il. 1.449, Il. 2.410. Cf. Il. 16.8, 10. 3 To take up and, or in order to, carry off or appropriate: τῶν οὐκ ἄν τι φέροις ἀνελών Il. 1.301. In mid.: [πελέκεας] Od. 21.261. To take up and carry off (prizes) Il. 23.736. In mid. Il. 23.823. To seize and carry off. In mid.: ὅτε κούρας ἀνέλοντο Od. 20.66. 4 To lift up or raise: ἀπὸ χθονός (i.e. the victim's head) Od. 3.453. In mid.: ἄλεισον ἀναιρήσεσθαι Od. 22.9. 5 In mid., to take for one's use: ἀνείλετʼ ἔγχος Il. 13.296. To take into service Od. 18.357. To take upon oneself, undertake: πατρὸς ἀέθλια Od. 21.117. To take into one's mind: ἐπιφροσύνας Od. 19.22.

data.quote: τῶν οὐκ ἄν τι φέροις ἀνελών

definition: ἀναΐσσω [ἀν-, ἀνα- 1.] 3 pl. aor. ἀνήϊξαν Il. 15.86, Il. 23.203: Od. 18.40, Od. 24.463. 3 sing. opt. ὰναΐξειε Il. 3.216. 3 pl. -ειαν Il. 4.114. Pple. ἀναΐξας, -αντος Il. 1.584, Il. 15.6, Il. 23.733, etc.: Od. 1.410, Od. 8.186, Od. 21.300, etc. Fem. ἀναΐξασα Od. 22.240. 1 To start, spring or dart up, rise quickly or suddenly: πάντες ἀνήϊξαν Il. 15.86, Il. 23.203. Cf. Il. 1.584, Il. 4.114, Il. 7.106, Il. 15.6, Il. 23.733, Il. 24.621: ἀναΐξας οἴχεται Od. 1.410. Cf. Od. 8.186, 361, Od. 9.288, Od. 13.197, Od. 18.40, Od. 19.31, Od. 21.119, 300, Od. 22.240, Od. 24.50, 463. 2 To rush or spring on to. With acc.: ἅρμα Il. 24.440. 3 Of springs, to gush forth Il. 22.148. 4 To rise to speak Il. 3.216 (the notion of quickness not here to be pressed).
ἀναίτιος [ἀν- 1 + αἴτιος.] Not blameworthy, blameless Il. 20.297: Od. 20.135, Od. 22.356. Absol. Il. 11.654, Il. 13.775.
ἀνακαίω [ἀνα- 6.] To light, kindle: πῦρ Od. 7.13, Od. 9.251, 308, Od. 10.358, Od. 20.123, Od. 21.181.
ἀνακηκίω [ἀνα- 1.] To gush up, ooze forth: αἷμα Il. 7.262, ἱδρώς Il. 13.705, Il. 23.507.

†ἀνακλίνω [ἀνα- 3.] Aor. pple. ἀνακλίνας Od. 18.103. Contr. ἀγκλίνας Il. 4.113: Od. 22.156. Infin. ἀνακλῖναι Il. 5.751, Il. 8.395: Od. 11.525. Aor. pple. pass. ἀνακλινθείς Od. 9.371. Pl. ἀνακλινθέντες Od. 13.78. Fem. ἀνακλινθεῖσα Od. 4.794, Od. 18.189. 1 To push back, open (a door) Od. 22.156. To remove (something covering): νέφος Il. 5.751 = Il. 8.395. App. (perh. in imitation of these lines), to suspend or delay the action of (an ambush): ἀνακλῖναι λόχον Od. 11.525. 2 To cause to lean (against something): ποτὶ ἑρκίον αὐλῆς Od. 18.103. To place or rest in a specified position Il. 4.113. 3 In aor. pple. pass., leaning or bending back Od. 9.371. Reclining Od. 4.794 = Od. 18.189. Of rowers swinging back to their work Od. 13.78.
ἀνακοντίζω [ἀνα-, ἀνα- 1.] To spirt up Il. 5.113.
ἀνακόπτω [ἀνα- 3] To thrust back Od. 21.47.
†ἀνακράζω [ἀνα- 6 + κράζω in sim. sense.] Aor. ἀνέκραγον. To lift up one's voice, speak Od. 14.467.
ἀνακτόριος -η, -ον [ἀνακτ-, ἄναξ.] Of a king or chief Od. 15.397.
ἀνακυμβαλιάζω [app. ἀνα- 6 + *κυμβαλιάζω in sim. sense fr. κύμβαλον, cymbal.] Thus, of chariots, to rattle (in upsetting) Il. 16.379.
ἀναλκείη -ης, ἡ [ἄναλκις.] Lack of spirit, cowardice. In pl. Il. 6.74 = Il. 17.320, Il. 17.337.

ἄναλκις -ιδος, ὁ, ἡ [ἀν- 1 + ἀλκή.] Acc. masc. ἄναλκιν Od. 3.375. Incapable of offering defence or resistance, spiritless, cowardly Il. 2.201, Il. 5.331, 349, Il. 8.153, Il. 11.390, Il. 13.104, Il. 16.355, Il. 21.555, etc.: Od. 3.310, 375, Od. 4.334 = Od. 17.125, Od. 9.475. As epithet of φύζα Il. 15.62.
ἄναλτος -ον [prob. for ἄναλδτος fr. ἀν- 1 + ἀλδ-, ἀλδαίνω, ἀλδήσκω.] Thus, not to be filled out, insatiable, greedy: γαστέρα Od. 17.228, Od. 18.364. Absol. Od. 18.114.

ἀναλύω ἀλλύω [ἀνα- 6, ἀλ-, ἀνα- 6.] Pa. iterative ἀλλύεσκον Od. 19.150. 3 sing. -ε Od. 2.105, Od. 24.140. 1 To loose, set free: ἐκ δεσμῶν (from . . .) Od. 12.200. 2 To undo, take down (a web) Od. 2.105 = Od. 24.140, Od. 2.109 = Od. 24.145, Od. 19.150.
ἀναμαιμάω [ἀνα- 5.] Of fire, to rage through. With acc.: βαθέʼ ἄγκεα Il. 20.490.
†ἀναμάσσω [ἀνα- 6 + μάσσω, to handle, conn. with μαίομαι.] 2 sing. fut. ἀναμάξεις. To wipe away the stain of (a crime) Od. 19.92.
†ἀναμένω [ἀνά- 6.] Aor. ἀνέμεινα. To wait for, await: Ἠῶ Od. 19.342.
ἀναμετρέω [ἀνα- 4.] To measure one's way again, retrace one's course. With acc. of terminus ad quem: χάρυβδιν Od. 12.428.
†ἀναμιμνήσκω [ἀνα- 6.] 2 sing. aor. ἀνέμνησας. To remind (a person of a thing). With double acc. Od. 3.211.
ἀναμίμνω [ἀνα- 6.] To wait for, await: ἀλλήλους Il. 11.171. Absol., to stand one's ground Il. 16.363.
ἀναμίσγω [ἀνα- 5.] Contr. aor. pple. ἀμμείξας, ἀμμίξας Il. 24.529. 1 To mix up ingredients Il. 24.529. 2 To mix up or mingle: σίτῳ φάρμακα (with . . .) Od. 10.235.
ἀναμορμύρω [ἀνα- 6.] 3 sing. pa. iterative ἀναμορμύρεσκε. To seethe or boil up Od. 12.238.

ἀνανεύω [ἀνα- 1.] 1 To throw up the chin in token of refusal (cf. κατανεύω) Il. 6.311 (app. the statue is supposed to move its head). 2 With infin. of what is refused: σόον ἀπονέεσθαι Il. 16.252. With acc. ἕτερον Il. 16.250. 3 To make the motion in prohibition Il. 22.205: Od. 21.129.
ἄναντα [app. a nonce-word formed fr. ἀνά by adding a termination fr. ἔναντα, ἐσάντα.] Uphill Il. 23.116.

ἄναξ -ακτος, ὁ (ϝ)άναξ Voc. (besides ἄναξ) ἄνα Il. 3.351, Il. 16.233: Od. 17.354. Dat. pl. ἀνάκτεσι Od. 15.557. 1 A king (the main notion being app. that of a protecting chief rather than that of a ruler; cf. the name Ἀστυάναξ Il. 6.403, and the reason for it there given. But βουληφόρος ἀ. occurs Il. 12.414). a ἀ. ἀνδρῶν (app. much like ποιμὴν λαῶν) applied to Agamemnon, gen. as a title, but sometimes as a descriptive term Il. 1.7, 172, 442, 506, Il. 2.402, 434, etc.: Od. 8.77, Od. 11.397 = Od. 24.121. Sim.: πολλῶν λαῶν ἀ. Il. 9.98. So ἀ. alone Il. 2.284, 360, Il. 9.33.–ἀ. ἀνδρῶν applied also to Anchises Il. 5.268. To Aeneas Il. 5.311. To Augeas Il. 11.701. To Euphetes Il. 15.532. To Eumelus Il. 23.288. Sim. πολέεσσʼ ἄνδρεσσιν ἄνακτα of Ortilochus Il. 5.546. And applied by Idomeneus to himself Il. 13.452. b ἀ. applied to Priam Il. 2.373, Il. 4.18, Il. 6.451, etc.: Od. 3.107. To Idomeneus Il. 2.405, Il. 10.112, Il. 15.301: Od. 19.181. To Philoctetes Il. 2.725. To Diomedes Il. 4.420, Il. 5.794. To Proetus Il. 6.166. To Achilles Il. 9.164, 276 = Il. 19.177, Il. 23.35, 173, Il. 24.449, 452. To Peleus Il. 9.480. To Asius Il. 12.139. To Sarpedon Il. 12.413, 414, Il. 16.464. To Helenus Il. 13.582, 758, 770, 781. To Nestor Il. 23.302: Od. 3.388. To Menelaus Il. 23.588. To Teucrus Il. 23.859. To Odysseus Od. 3.163, Od. 13.194, etc. To Teiresias Od. 11.144, 151. To Aias Od. 11.561. To Minos Od. 11.570. To minor heroes and personages Il. 2.566 = Il. 23.678, Il. 2.624, 672, 679, 693, Il. 7.8, 137, Il. 11.322, Il. 14.489, Il. 15.639: Od. 16.395 = Od. 18.413, Od. 18.299, Od. 19.523, Od. 24.305. Applied to kings or chiefs generally: ἅρματα ἀνάκτων Il. 2.777: ἀνάκτων παῖδες Od. 13.223. To the leader of a ship's company Od. 11.71. With a local word: πύλοιο Il. 2.77. Cf. Il. 6.173. Sim. Τρώεσσιν Il. 20.230. Joined with βασιλεύς Od. 20.194. c ἀ. applied to gods. To Apollo Il. 1.36, 75, 390, etc.: Od. 8.323, 334, 339. To Zeus Il. 1.502, 529, Il. 2.102, Il. 3.351, Il. 7.194, 200, Il. 16.233, Il. 18.118: Od. 17.354. To Hermes Il. 2.104. To Sleep Il. 14.233. To Poseidon Il. 15.8, 57, 158, Il. 20.67, 404: Od. 3.43, 54, Od. 9.412, 526, Od. 11.130, Od. 13.185, Od. 23.277. To Hephaestus Il. 15.214, Il. 18.137: Od. 8.270. To Hades Il. 20.61. To a river Od. 5.445, 450. To the sun Od. 12.176. To the gods generally Od. 12.290. 2 A lord, master, owner: οὐδʼ ἠγνοίησαν ἄνακτα Il. 13.28, τί δόμεν πηλῆϊ ἄνακτι (to P. as your master) Il. 17.443. Cf. Il. 10.559, Il. 13.38, Il. 15.453, Il. 16.371, 507, Il. 18.417, 421, Il. 23.417 = 446, 517, Il. 24.734: οἴκοιο ἀ. Od. 1.397, οὔτε ἀ. οὔτε ποιμήν Od. 4.87. Cf. Od. 9.440, Od. 10.216, Od. 14.8, 139, 170, Od. 17.186, 320, etc.
ἀνάξει 3 sing. fut. ἀνάσσω.
ἀνάξομεν 1 pl. fut. ἀνάγω.

†ἀναοίγω [ἀνα- 6 + οἴγω = οἴγνυμι.] 3 sing. impf. ἀνέῳγε Il. 16.221, Il. 24.228. Cont. ἀνῷγε Il. 14.168. 3 pl. pa. iterative ἀναοίγεσκον Il. 24.455. 3 sing. aor. ἀνέῳξε Od. 10.389. 1 To open (a door) Od. 10.389. 2 To draw back (a bar in order to open a door) κληῗδα Il. 14.168, Il. 24.455. 3 To remove (a cover) Il. 16.221, Il. 24.228.

ἀναπάλλω [ἀνα- 1.] Contr. aor. pple. ἀμπεπαλών Il. 3.355, Il. 5.280, Il. 7.244, Il. 11.349, Il. 17.516, Il. 20.438, Il. 22.273, 289: Od. 24.519, 522. 3 sing. aor. pass. ἀνέπαλτο Il. 8.85, Il. 23.694. 1 To poise and sway (a spear before throwing) Il. 3.355 = Il. 5.280 = Il. 7.244 = Il. 11.349 = Il. 17.516 = Il. 22.273 = 289, Il. 20.438: Od. 24.519 = 522. 2 In pass., to leap or spring up: ἀναπάλλεται ἰχθύς Il. 23.692. Cf. Il. 8.85, Il. 23.694.
ἀναπαύω [ἀνα- 6.] To cause to cease: ἔργων ἀνθρώπους ἀνέπαυσεν (from . . .) Il. 17.550.
†ἀναπετάννυμι [ἀνα- 6.] Acc. fem. pf. pple. pass. ἀναπεπταμένας. To open wide (a gate) Il. 12.122.

†ἀναπίμπλημι [ἀνα- 6.] Fut. infin. ἀναπλήσειν Od. 5.302. 2 sing. aor. subj. ἀναπλήσῃς Il. 4.170. Pple. ἀναπλήσας, -αντος Il. 8.34, 354, 465, Il. 11.263, Il. 15.132. Infin. ἀναπλῆσαι Od. 5.207. To fulfil (one's destiny), have full measure of (misery etc.): πότμον Il. 4.170, Il. 11.263. Cf. Il. 8.34 = 354 = 465, Il. 15.132: κήδεα Od. 5.207. Cf. Od. 5.302.
ἀναπλέω [ἀνα- 1, ἀνα- 5.] Fut. infin. in mid. form ἀναπλεύσεσθαι Il. 11.22. 1 To sail upwards. Of a voyage from Greece to Troy Il. 11.22. 2 To sail through, traverse. With acc.: στεινωπόν Od. 12.234.

ἀνάπνευσις ἡ [ἀναπνέω.] A breathing-space, a respite: ὀλίγη δέ τʼ ἀ. πολέμοιο (a little (space of time) serves as a respite from . . .) Il. 11.801 = Il. 16.43 = Il. 18.201 (ὀλίγη assimilated in gender to the predicate; cf. Il. 13.237 under ἀρετή 1).

ἀναπνέω [ἀνα- 4.] 3 pl. aor. ἀνέπνευσαν Il. 11.382, Il. 16.302. 3 pl. subj. ἀναπνεύσωσι Il. 11.800, Il. 15.235, Il. 16.42, Il. 18.200, Il. 21.534. 3 sing. opt. ἀναπνεύσειε Il. 19.227. Contr. infin. ἀμπνεῦσαι Il. 16.111. Contr. aor. imp. ἄμπνυε Il. 22.222. To breathe again, recover breath, draw breath, find a breathing-space or respite Il. 11.327, 800 = Il. 16.42 = Il. 18.200, Il. 16.111, 302, Il. 21.534, Il. 22.222. With genit.: κακότητος (from . . .) Il. 11.382. Cf. Il. 15.235, Il. 19.227.
ἀνάποινος [ἀν- 1 + ἄποινα.] In neut. ἀνάποινον as adv., without ransom Il. 1.99.
†ἀναπρήθω [ἀνα- 1.] Aor. pple. ἀναπρήσας. To cause (tears) to well up Il. 9.433: Od. 2.81.

ἀνάπτω [ἀν-, ἀνα- 1, ἀνα- 6.] 3 sing. aor. ἀνῆψε Od. 3.274. Infin. ἀνάψαι Od. 2.86, Od. 9.137. Pf. imp. pass. ἀνήφθω Od. 12.51, 162. 1 To fasten up (as an offering in a temple) Od. 3.274. 2 To tie, make fast (a rope): πρυμνήσια Od. 9.137. Cf. Od. 12.51 = 162, 179. 3 To fasten (blame) upon a person Od. 2.86.
ἀνάπυστος [ἀνα- 6 + πυσ-, πεύθομαι.] Discovered, revealed. Absol. in neut. pl.: ἀνάπυστα θεοὶ θέσαν (caused discovery to be made) Od. 11.274.
ἀναροιβδέω See ἀναρροιβδέω.

†ἀναρπάζω [ἀν-, ἀνα- 1.] 3 sing. aor. ἀνήρπασε Il. 9.564. 3 pl. ἀνήρπαξαν Od. 15.427. Pple. ἀναρπάξας Il. 16.437. Fem. -ασα Od. 4.515, Od. 5.419, Od. 20.63, Od. 23.316. Pl. -ασαι Od. 8.409. 1 To snatch up and carry off Il. 9.564, Il. 16.437. Of winds Od. 4.515, Od. 5.419, Od. 8.409, Od. 20.63, Od. 23.316. 2 To carry off as a slave Od. 15.427.

†ἀναρρήγνυμι [ἀνα- 6.] 3 sing. aor. opt. ἀναρρήξειε Il. 20.63. Pple. ἀναρρήξας Il. 7.461. Nom. dual masc. -αντε Il. 18.582. 1 To split, cause to open: γαῖαν Il. 20.63. To tear open, rend: βοείην Il. 18.582. 2 To tear down, demolish Il. 7.461.

ἀναρρίπτω [ἀνα- 1.] 3 pl. aor. ἀνέρριψαν Od. 10.130. From ἀναρριπτέω 3 pl. impf. ἀνερρίπτουν Od. 13.78. To throw up (the sea with the oar): ἅλα πηδῷ Od. 7.328, Od. 13.78. Absol., to row vigorously Od. 10.130.
ἀναρροιβδέω also ἀναροιβδέω, Od. 12.105. [ἀνα- 6.] To swallow down, swallow Od. 12.104, 105, 236, 431.
ἀνάρσιος [ἀν- 1 + ἀρ-, ἀραρίσκω. Not fitted, ill-fitted, ill-assorted.] Unfriendly, hostile Il. 24.365: Od. 10.459, Od. 11.401, 408, Od. 24.111. Absol.: δυσμενέες καὶ ἀνάρσιοι Od. 14.85.
ἄναρχος [ἀν- 1 + ἀρχός.] Leaderless Il. 2.703 = 726.
†ἀνασεύω [ἀνα- 1.] 3 sing. aor. mid. ἀνέσσυτο. In mid., to spirt up: αἷμα Il. 11.458.
†ἀνασπάω [ἀνα- 3.] 3 sing. aor. mid. ἀνεσπάσατο. To draw forth again: ἔγχος Il. 13.574.
ἄνασσα -ης, ἡ (ϝάνασσα) [fem. of ἄναξ.] Queen, protectress. Applied to Demeter Il. 14.326. In voc. addressed to Athene Od. 3.380. To Nausicaa Od. 6.149, 175.

ἀνάσσω (ϝανάσσω) [ἄναξ.] 3 sing. fut. ἀνάξει Il. 19.104, 122, Il. 20.307. Infin. -ειν Il. 19.109, Il. 20.180. Aor. infin. mid. -ασθαι Od. 3.245 (in mid. only here). 1 To protect, be patron of. With genit.: τενέδοιο Il. 1.38 = 452. 2 To be king, chief or ruler: μετὰ τριτάτοισιν Il. 1.252. Cf. Il. 4.61 = Il. 18.366, Il. 16.172, Il. 23.471: Od. 7.23, 62, Od. 19.110. In mid.: τρὶς ἀνάξασθαι γένεʼ ἀνδρῶν (app., during three generations) Od. 3.245. With local words: ἐν Βουδείῳ Il. 16.572. Cf. Od. 11.276, 284, Od. 24.26. 3 To be king or chief of or ruler over. a With genit.: Ἀργείων Il. 10.33. Cf. Od. 11.276. With local words: Ἰλίου Il. 6.478. Cf. Od. 3.304, Od. 4.602, Od. 17.443. b With dat.: Μυρμιδόνεσσιν Il. 1.180. Cf. Il. 1.231, Il. 2.643, Il. 6.397, Il. 14.85, 94, Il. 19.104, Il. 24.202, etc.: Od. 1.181, 419, Od. 2.234 = Od. 5.12, Od. 4.9, Od. 7.11, Od. 9.552 = Od. 13.25, Od. 10.110, Od. 11.349, 491, Od. 15.240, Od. 20.112, Od. 24.26, 378. With local words: πολλῇσιν νήσοισιν Il. 2.108. 4 In pass., to be ruled by, be under the sway of. With dat.: ἀνάσσονται ἐμοὶ αὐτῷ Od. 4.177. 5 To be lord or master of, possess, enjoy. a With genit.: τιμῆς Il. 20.180: Od. 24.30. b With dat.: κτήμασιν οἶσιν Od. 1.117. Cf. Od. 1.402, Od. 4.93.
ἀνασταδόν [ἀνα- 1 + στα-, ἵστημι.] Standing up: δειδέχατʼ ἀ. Il. 9.671, ἴδεσθʼ ἀ. Il. 23.469.
ἀναστάς aor. pple. ἀνίστημι B.
ἀναστεναχίζω [ἀνα- 6.] To groan aloud Il. 10.9.
ἀναστενάχω [ἀνα- 6.] To groan aloud over, lament, bewail Il. 23.211. In mid. Il. 18.315, 355.
ἀναστήσας aor. pple. ἀνίστημι A.

ἀναστρέφω [ἀνα- 5, ἀνα- 6.] Contr. 3 pl. aor. opt. ἀνστρέψειαν Il. 23.436. 1 To upset: δίφρους Il. 23.436. 2 In mid., to go about over, find oneself in. With acc.: ἄλλην τινὰ γαῖαν ἀναστρέφομαι Od. 13.326.
ἀναστρωφάω [ἀνα- 6.] To keep turning about: τόξον ἐνώμα ἀναστρωφῶν Od. 21.394.
ἀνασχέμεν ἀνασχεῖν aor. infin. ἀνέχω.
†ἀνατέλλω [ἀνα- 1.] 3 sing. aor. ἀνέτειλε. To cause to spring up or be produced: ἀμβροσίην Il. 5.777.
†ἀνατίθημι [ἀνα- 1.] 3 sing. fut. ἀναθήσει. To lay (reproach) upon. With dat.: ἐλεγχείην μοι Il. 22.100.
†ἀνατλάω [ἀνα- 6.] 2 sing. aor. ἀνέτλης Od. 14.47. 3 sing. -η Od. 10.327. 1 pl. -ημεν Od. 3.104. To endure, suffer Od. 3.104, Od. 14.47. To withstand the operation of Od. 10.327.
†ἀνατρέπω [ἀνα- 3.] 3 sing. aor. mid. ἀνετράπετο. In mid., to fall supine Il. 6.64, Il. 14.447.

†ἀνατρέχω [ἀνα- 1, ἀνα- 3.] 3 sing. aor. ἀνέδραμε Il. 11.354, Il. 16.813, Il. 17.297, Il. 18.56, 437. 3 pl. -ον Il. 23.717. 3 sing. pf. ἀναδέδρομε Od. 5.412, Od. 10.4. 1 To spirt up Il. 17.297. 2 To run up, shoot up (like a quickly growing plant) Il. 18.56 = 437. Of welts, to start up Il. 23.717. 3 To run, stretch, extend up: πέτρη Od. 5.412, Od. 10.4. 4 To run back, retire Il. 11.354, Il. 16.813.
ἄναυδος [ἀν- 1 + αὐδή.] Speechless Od. 5.456. Absol.: ἷσος ἀναύδῳ (like a dumb man) Od. 10.378.

ἀναφαίνω [ἀνα- 6.] Aor. infin. ἀναφῆναι Od. 4.254. 1 To reveal, make known Il. 1.87. To betray, denounce Od. 4.254. To display: ἐπεσβολίας Od. 4.159. To make a display of: ἀρετήν Il. 20.411. 2 To afford light Od. 18.310. 3 In pass., to appear, be seen: οἷος ἀναφαίνεται ἀστήρ Il. 11.62. Cf. Od. 10.29. Of destruction, to be manifested, come upon one Il. 11.174, Il. 17.244.
ἀναφανδά [ἀναφαν-, ἀναφαίνω.] Openly, without concealment: ἀ. φιλεῦντας Od. 3.221. Cf. Od. 3.222, Od. 11.455.
ἀναφανδόν [as ἀναφανδά.] = ἀναφανδά.: ἀ. ὄπυιεν (as her avowed husband) Il. 16.178.
†ἀναφέρω [ἀνα- 1.] Aor. ἀνένεικα Od. 11.625. 3 sing. aor. mid. ἀνενείκατο Il. 19.314. 1 To bring or fetch up Od. 11.625. 2 In mid., to fetch a sigh Il. 19.314.

ἀναχωρέω [ἀνα- 3.] 1 To go back, return Il. 10.210 = 411, Il. 13.457. 2 To withdraw, retire Od. 17.453, 461. To draw back from danger Il. 3.35. Of hounds retreating from a boar Il. 17.729. To draw back or retire in fight Il. 4.305, Il. 5.107, Il. 11.189, 440, Il. 17.30, Il. 20.196, 335: Od. 22.270.
ἀνάψαι aor. infin. ἀνάπτω.
ἀναψύχω [ἀνα- 6.] 3 pl. aor. pass. ἀνέψυχθεν Il. 10.575. To cool, refresh Od. 4.568. Fig.: ἐπεὶ ἀνέψυχθεν ἦτορ Il. 10.575. Cf. Il. 13.84. To cool or soothe (a wound) Il. 5.795.

†ἁνδάνω ((σ)ϝανδάνω) [(σ)ϝαδ-. Cf. ἡδύς, L. suavis.] 3 sing. ἁνδάνει Od. 2.114. 3 sing. impf. ἑήνδανε (ἐϝάνδανε) Il. 24.25: Od. 3.143. ἥνδανε (ϝάνδανε) Il. 1.24, 378, Il. 15.674, Il. 18.510: Od. 5.153, Od. 8.506, Od. 10.373, Od. 14.337, 525, Od. 16.398, Od. 17.173. ἅνδανε Od. 3.150. 3 sing. aor. εὔαδε (ἔϝαδε) Il. 14.340, Il. 17.647: Od. 16.28. ἅδε (ϝάδε) Il. 12.80, Il. 13.748: Od. 24.465. 3 sing. opt. ἅδοι Od. 6.245, Od. 20.327. Infin. ἁδεῖν Il. 3.173. Acc. sing. masc. pf. pple. ἑαδότα (ϝεϝαδότα) Il. 9.173: Od. 18.422. (ἀφ-, ἐπι-.) 1 To please, be pleasing or acceptable, find favour or acceptance Od. 5.153, Od. 17.173. With dat.: Ἕκτορι Il. 12.80 = Il. 13.748. Cf. Il. 3.173, Il. 14.340, Il. 18.510: Od. 2.114, Od. 3.150, Od. 8.506, Od. 14.337, 525, Od. 16.398, Od. 20.327, Od. 24.465. 2 Impers. With dat.: ἐπεί τοι εὔαδεν οὕτως Il. 17.647. Cf. Il. 1.24 = 378, Il. 24.25: Od. 3.143, Od. 10.373. With dat. and infin.: Αἴαντι ἑστάμεν Il. 15.674. Cf. Od. 6.245. So ὥς τοι εὔαδε, . . . ἐσορᾶν . . . Od. 16.28. 3 In pf. pple., pleasing, agreeable Il. 9.173: = Od. 18.422.
ἄνδιχα [ἀν-, ἀνα- 6 + δίχα.] 1 In two, asunder: κεάσθη Il. 16.412 = Il. 20.387, Il. 16.578. 2 In halves, equally: δάσασθαι Il. 18.511, Il. 22.120.
ἀνδράγρια τά [ἀνδρ-, ἀνήρ + ἄγρη. Cf. βοάγρια.] Spoils of a man, i.e. of a fallen foe Il. 14.509.
ἀνδρακάς [ἀνδρ-, ἀνήρ.] Each man, each Od. 13.14.
ἀνδράποδον Dat. pl. -πόδεσσι. A slave Il. 7.475.
ἀνδραχθής [ἀνδρ-, ἀνήρ + ἄχθος.] That is a load for a man, as heavy as a man can carry Od. 10.121.
ἀνδρειφόντης [prob. rather ἆδριφόντης, fr. ἀδρ-, ἀνδρ-, ἀνήρ + φον-, *φένω. Cf. ἀνδροτής.] Slayer of men. Epithet of Enyalius Il. 2.651, Il. 7.166 = Il. 8.264 = Il. 17.259.
ἀνδρόκμητος [ἀνδρ-, ἀνήρ + κμη-, κάμνω.] Made by the hands of man, the work of men's hands Il. 11.371.

ἀνδροκτασίη -ης, ἡ [ἀνδρ-, ἀνήρ + κτα-, κτείνω.] 1 Slaughter of men, slaughter in battle. In pl.: παύσασαι ἀνδροκτασιάων Il. 5.909. Cf. Il. 7.237, Il. 24.548: Od. 11.612. In concrete sense: ὕπαγʼ ἐξ ἀνδροκτασίης Il. 11.164. 2 Homicide Il. 23.86.
ἀνδρόμεος [ἀνδρ-, ἀνήρ.] Of man, human Il. 11.538 (the throng of men), Il. 17.571, Il. 20.100, Il. 21.70: Od. 9.297 (of man's flesh), Od. 9.347, Od. 9.374, Od. 22.19.
ἀνδροτής -ῆτος, ἡ [prob. rather ἆδροτής, fr. ἀδρ-, ἀνδρ-, ἀνήρ. Cf. ἀνδρειφόντης.] 1 Manhood Il. 16.857 = Il. 22.363. 2 Manliness Il. 24.6.
ἀνδροφάγος [ἀνδρ-, ἀνήρ + φάγον.] Man-eating Od. 10.200.

ἀνδροφόνος -ον [ἀνδρ-, ἀνήρ + φον-, *φένω.] 1 Slayer of men. Epithet of Hector Il. 1.242, Il. 6.498, Il. 9.351, Il. 16.77, 840, Il. 17.428, 616, 638, Il. 18.149, Il. 24.509, 724. Of Ares Il. 4.441. Of Lycurgus Il. 6.134. 2 Manslaying, fatal: χεῖρας Il. 18.317 = Il. 23.18, Il. 24.479. Of a poisonous application, deadly Od. 1.261.
ἀνδύεται contr. 3 sing. pres. mid. ἀναδύω.
ἀνέβη 3 sing. aor. ἀναβαίνω.
ἀνεβήσετο 3 sing. aor. mid. ἀναβαίνω.

ἀνεγείρω [ἀν-, ἀνα- 6.] Aor. ἀνέγειρα Od. 10.172. 3 sing. -ε Il. 10.138, 157: Od. 23.22. Infin. ἀνεγεῖραι Od. 4.730. To wake up, cause to rise, rouse Il. 10.138, 157: Od. 4.730, Od. 10.172, Od. 23.16, 22.
ἀνέγναμψαν 3 pl. aor. ἀναγνάμπτω.
ἀνέγνων aor. ἀναγιγνώσκω.
ἀνεδέγμεθα 1 pl. aor. ἀναδέχομαι.
ἀνεδέξατο 3 sing. aor. ἀναδέχομαι.
ἀνέδρακε 3 sing. aor. ἀναδέρκομαι.
ἀνέδραμε 3 sing. aor. ἀνατρέχω.
ἀνέδυ 3 sing. aor. ἀναδύω.
ἀνεδύσετο 3 sing. aor. mid. ἀναδύω.
ἀνεέργω [ἀν-, ἀνα- 6.] To keep back, restrain: φάλαγγας Il. 3.77 = Il. 7.55, μάχην Τρώων Il. 17.752.

†ἀνέζομαι [ἀν-, ἀνα- 1, ἀνα- 4.] 3 sing. fut. ἀνέσει Od. 18.265. Aor. opt. ἀνέσαιμι Il. 14.209. Pl. pple. ἀνέσαντες Il. 13.657. In the forms cited 1 To set or place upon something: ἐς δίφρον Il. 13.657. Sim.: εἰς εὐνήν Il. 14.209. 2 To restore to one's place Od. 18.265.
ἀνέηκε 3 sing. aor. ἀνίημι.
ἀνείη 3 sing. aor. opt. ἀνίημι.
ἀνείλετο 3 sing. aor. mid. ἀναιρέω.

†ἄνειμι [ἀν-, ἀνα- 1, ἀνα- 3 + εἶμι.] 3 sing. ἄνεισι Il. 22.492, 499. Pple. ἀνιών, -όντος Il. 6.480, Il. 8.538, Il. 14.28, Il. 18.136, Il. 22.135: Od. 1.24, 259, Od. 5.282, Od. 10.332, Od. 12.429, Od. 23.362. Fem. ἀνιοῦσα Il. 19.290. Acc. ἀνιοῦσαν Od. 8.568, Od. 13.150, 176. Impf. ἀνήϊον Od. 10.146, 274. 3 pl. ἀνήϊον Od. 10.446. 1 To go up Od. 10.146. Of the sun, to rise: ἠελίου ἀνιόντος Il. 8.538. Cf. Il. 18.136, Il. 22.135: Αἰθίοπες ἀνιόντος Ὑπερίονος (dwelling in the east) Od. 1.24. Cf. Od. 12.429, Od. 23.362. 2 To go inland Od. 10.274, 446. 3 To go up (to a person) as a suppliant: ἐς πατρὸς ἑταίρους Il. 22.492. 4 To go or come back, return: ἐκ πολέμου Il. 6.480. Cf. Il. 14.28, Il. 19.290, Il. 22.499: Od. 1.259, Od. 5.282, Od. 8.568 = Od. 13.150 = 176, Od. 10.332.
ἀνείμων -ονος [ἀ-1 + εἷμα.] Without (store of) raiment. Absol.: ἀνείμονος ἠὲ πενιχροῦ Od. 3.348.

ἀνείρομαι [ἀν-, ἀνα- (6)]. 1 To ask, inquire, make inquiry Il. 21.508: Od. 7.21, Od. 23.99. 2 To inquire, about: τήνδε γαῖαν Od. 13.238. 3 To question (a person): σε Od. 4.420. Cf. Od. 4.461, 631. 4 With double acc.: ὅ μʼ ἀνείρεαι Il. 3.177: = Od. 7.243 = Od. 15.402, Od. 19.171. Cf. Od. 1.231 = Od. 15.390.
ἀνέκραγον aor. ἀνακράζω.

ἀνεκτός -ον [vbl. adj. fr. ἀνέχω.] Bearable, endurable, to be endured Il. 1.573, Il. 10.118, Il. 11.610: Od. 20.83. Absol. in neut. pl.: οὐκέτʼ ἀνεκτὰ πέλονται (my case is now unendurable) Od. 20.223.
ἀνεκτῶς [adv. fr. ἀνεκτός.] In such wise as may be endured: μαίνεται οὐκέτʼ ἀ. Il. 8.355. Cf. Od. 9.350.
ἀνελθών aor. pple. ἀνέρχομαι.

ἀνέλκω [ἀν-, ἀνα- 1, ἀνα- 3.] 1 To draw up Il. 12.434. 2 To draw back (i.e. away from one): τόξου πῆχυν Il. 11.375, Il. 13.583. To draw back (a spear in order to recover it). In mid. Od. 22.97. To bend a bow Od. 21.128, 150.
ἀνέλοντο 3 pl. aor. mid. ἀναιρέω.
ἀνέμεινα aor. ἀναμένω.
ἀνέμνησας 2 sing. aor. ἀναμιμνήσκω.
ἀνεμοσκεπής [ἄνεμος + σκέπας.] Protecting from the wind: χλαινάων Il. 16.224.
ἀνεμοτρεφής -ές [ἄνεμος + τρέφω.] Of a wave, fed (i. e. raised) by the wind Il. 15.625. Of a spear, (made of wood) toughened by (the buffeting of) the wind Il. 11.256.

ἀνεμώλιος [app. fr. ἄνεμος.] Thus 1 Like the idle blowing of the wind, idle, vain: ταῦτʼ ἀνεμώλια βάζεις (what you say is idle) Il. 4.355.– Absol.: ἀνεμώλια βάζειν Od. 4.837 = Od. 11.464. 2 Useless, idle: τόξα Il. 5.216. Cf. Il. 21.474. Useless, effecting nothing Il. 20.123.
ἀνένεικα aor. ἀναφέρω.
ἀνέντες aor. pple. pl. ἀνίημι.
ἀνέξομαι fut. mid. ἀνέχω.
ἀνέπαλτο 3 sing. aor. pass. ἀναπάλλω.
ἀνεπᾶλτο 3 sing. aor. ἀνεφάλλομαι.
ἀνέπνευσαν 3 pl. aor. ἀναπνέω.
ἀνερρίπτουν 3 pl. impf. See ἀναρρίπτω.
ἀνέρριψαν 3 pl. aor. ἀναρρίπτω.

ἀνέρχομαι [ἀν-, ἀνα- 1, ἀνα- 3.] 3 sing. aor. ἀνήλυθε Od. 6.167. Pple. ἀνελθών Od. 10.97, 148, 194, Od. 19.190. 1 To go up Od. 10.97 = 148, 194. To go up (to a city): ἄστυδε Od. 19.190. –Of a plant, to shoot up Od. 6.163, 167. 2 To come back, return Il. 4.392, Il. 6.187: Od. 1.317.
ἀνερωτάω [ἀν-, ἀνα- 6 + ἐρωτάω = εἰρωτάω.] To question (a person): ἀνηρώτων μιν Od. 4.251.
ἄνεσαν 3 pl. aor. ἀνίημι.
ἀνέσει 3 sing. fut. ἀνέζομαι.
ἀνεσπάσατο 3 sing. aor. mid. ἀνασπάω.
ἀνέσσυτο 3 sing. aor. mid. ἀνασεύω.
ἀνέστη 3 sing. aor. ἀνίστημι B.
ἀνέστησε 3 sing. aor. ἀνίστημι A.
ἀνέστιος [ἀ-1 + ἑστίη = ἱστίη.] Unworthy to have a home: ἀφρήτωρ ἀθέμιστος ἀ. Il. 9.63.
ἀνέσχε 3 sing. aor. ἀνέχω.
ἀνέσχεθε 3 sing. aor. ἀνέχω.
ἀνέτειλε 3 sing. aor. ἀνατλάω.
ἀνέτλη 3 sing. aor. ἀνατλάω.
ἀνετράπετο 3 sing. aor. mid. ἀνατρέπω.

ἄνευ With genit. 1 Away from, aloof from: δηΐων Il. 13.556. 2 Lacking: κέντροιο Il. 23.387. Cf. Od. 24.247. Without need of: δεσμοῖο Od. 13.100. 3 Without the help of: ἕθεν Il. 17.407. Without the good will or permission of: ἐμέθεν Il. 15.213. Cf. Od. 2.372, Od. 15.531.

ἄνευθε (-θεν) [ἄνευ.] 1 Adv. a Far away: ἀ. ἐών Il. 2.27 = 64 = Il. 24.174. Cf. Il. 4.277, Il. 22.300, Il. 23.452, 474. b Away, removed: πολλὸν ἀ. Il. 23.378. Cf. Od. 4.356, Od. 19.575. c Apart, aside, aloof: ἀ. ἔθηκεν Il. 22.368. Cf. Il. 23.241, Il. 24.208: Od. 9.26, Od. 11.82. 2 Prep. with genit. a Far from: πατρός Il. 21.78. b Away from: νῶϊν Il. 22.88. c Apart or aloof from: ἄλλων Il. 22.39. Cf. Od. 10.554. d Without, free from: πόνου Od. 7.192. e Without the help of: ἐμεῖο Il. 16.89. Cf. Il. 16.239. Without the good will or permission of: θεοῦ Il. 5.185. f App., in the background as regards, ready to take the place of: τοῖο ἀ. λελείμμην Il. 22.333.
†ἀνεφάλλομαι [ἀν-, ἀνα- 1, ἐφ-, ἐπι- 11.] 3 sing. aor. ἀνεπᾶλτο. To spring up against a person Il. 20.424.
ἀνέφελος -ον [ἀ-1 + νεφέλη.] Cloudless Od. 6.45.

ἀνέχω [ἀν-, ἀνα- 1, ἀνα- 3.] 3 sing. aor. ἀνέσχε Il. 17.310, Il. 20.278, Il. 22.80: Od. 22.297. 3 pl. -ον Il. 3.318, Il. 6.301, Il. 7.177: Od. 18.89. Pple. ἀνασχών Il. 1.450, Il. 3.275, Il. 5.174, etc. : Od. 4.115, 154, Od. 13.355, Od. 17.239, Od. 20.97. Infin. ἀνασχέμεν Il. 24.301. ἀνασχεῖν Il. 6.257. 3 sing. aor. ἀνασχέμεν Il. 24.301. ἀνασχεῖν Il. 6.257. 3 sing. aor. ἀνέσχεθε Il. 7.412, Il. 10.461. 1 pl. -ομεν Od. 9.294. Contr. infin. ἀνσχεθέειν Od. 5.320. Mid. Fut. ἀνέξομαι Il. 5.895: Od. 19.27. Contr. infin. ἀνσχήσεσθαι Il. 5.104, 285. 3 sing. aor. ἀνέσχετο Il. 5.655, Il. 18.430, Il. 21.67, 161: Od. 23.302. Contr. 2 sing. ἄνσχεο Il. 24.518. Opt. ἀνασχοίμην Od. 11.375. Imp. ἀνάσχεο Il. 1.586, Il. 5.382, Il. 10.321. Contr. ἄνσχεο Il. 23.587, Il. 24.549. Pple. ἀνασχόμενος, -ου Il. 3.362, Il. 11.594, Il. 12.138, etc.: Od. 14.425, Od. 18.95, 100, Od. 19.448. Infin. ἀνασχέσθαι Il. 4.511: Od. 13.307. I In act. 1 To hold up, lift up: σκῆπτρον (to the gods in testimony) Il. 7.412, ὑψόσε (as an offering) Il. 10.461. Cf. Il. 14.499, Il. 20.278, Il. 22.80: χεῖρας Od. 18.89. Cf. Od. 4.115 = 154, Od. 22.297. To lift up (the hands) in prayer Il. 1.450, Il. 11.275, 318 = Il. 7.177, Il. 5.174, Il. 6.257, 301, Il. 18.75, Il. 19.254, Il. 24.301: Od. 9.294, Od. 13.355, Od. 17.239, Od. 20.97. 2 To maintain, uphold: εὐδικίας Od. 19.111. 3 To restrain, check: ἵππους Il. 23.426. 4 To project, appear: αἰχμὴ παρʼ ὦμον Il. 17.310. To come to the surface, emerge Od. 5.320. II In mid. 1 To hold up, lift up: σκῆπτρον ἀνάσχεο (in testimony) Il. 10.321. Cf. Il. 12.138: Od. 18.100. To raise (a spear) for action Il. 5.655, Il. 11.594, Il. 15.298, Il. 17.234, Il. 21.67, 161: Od. 19.448. 2 To lift the hand Il. 3.362, Il. 22.34: Od. 14.425. Of boxers, to square up Il. 23.660, 686: Od. 18.95. 3 To endure, have laid upon one, suffer: κήδεα Il. 18.430. Cf. Il. 24.518: Od. 13.307, Od. 23.302. 4 To endure, stand, withstand the action of: χαλκόν Il. 4.511. Cf. Il. 5.104, Il. 15.470. 5 To endure, submit to: δουλοσύνην Od. 22.423. To suffer the presence or company of, bear with: ξείνους Od. 7.32. Cf. Od. 17.13. 6 To endure, suffer, permit. With acc. in complementary ppl. clause: οὔ σʼ ἀνέξομαι ἄλγεʼ ἔχοντα Il. 5.895. Cf. Od. 19.27. 7 To endure, hold up, hold out: δηρόν Il. 5.285. Cf. Od. 11.375. With complementary ppl. clause: καί κʼ εἰς ἐνιαυτὸν παρὰ σοί γʼ ἀνεχοίμην ἥμενος Od. 4.595. 8 To accept what happens, submit with patience: ἀνάσχεο Il. 1.586. Cf. Il. 5.382, Il. 24.549. With complementary pple.: εἰσορόων ἀνέχεσθαι Od. 16.277. To restrain oneself, be placated: ἄνσχεο Il. 23.587.

data.quote: καί κʼ εἰς ἐνιαυτὸν παρὰ σοί γʼ ἀνεχοίμην ἥμενος

definition: ἀνέψυχθεν 3 pl. aor. pass. ἀναψύχω.

ἄνεῳ ἄνεω [the former app a nom. pl. masc. fr. an adj. ἄνεως. The latter (only in Od. 23.93 of a woman) app. to be taken as an adv. .] Silent: ἐγένεσθε Il. 2.323. Cf. Il. 3.84, Il. 9.30 = 695: ἧσθε Od. 2.240. Cf. Od. 7.144, Od. 10.71, Od. 23.93.

data.ref: Od. 23.93 of a woman) app. to be taken as an adv. .]

definition: ἀνέῳξε 3 sing. aor. ἀναοίγω.
ἀνήγαγον aor. ἀνάγω.
ἀνήῃ 3 sing. aor. subj. ἀνίημι.
ἀνήϊξαν 3 pl. aor. ἀναΐσσω.
ἀνήϊον impf. ἄνειμι.
ἀνῆκε 3 sing. aor. ἀνίημι.
ἀνήκεστος [ἀ-1 + ἀκεσ-, ἀκέομαι.] Not to be cured or soothed Il. 5.394. Not to be appeased Il. 15.217.
ἀνηκουστέω [ἀ-1 + ἀκούω.] To fail to hearken to, disobey. With genit.: πατρός Il. 15.236 = Il. 16.676.
ἀνήλυθε 3 sing. aor. ἀνέρχομαι.
ἀνήμελκτος -ον [ἀ-1 + ἀμέλγω.] Not milked Od. 9.439.
ἀνήνατο 3 sing. aor. ἀναίνομαι.

†ἀνήνοθε [3 sing., in the first passage of a plupf. (with secondary person-ending), in the second of a pf., fr. ἀνεθ- = ἀνθ-, ἄνθος. (Cf. ἐνήνοθε).] (ἐπ-.) To come to the surface, come forth: αἷμʼ ἀ. Il. 11.266. To rise up, spread upwards: κνίση ἀ. Od. 17.270.
ἀνήνυστος [ἀ-1 + ἀνυσ-, ἀνύω.] Not accomplished or brought to an end: ἔργῳ Od. 16.111.
ἀνήνωρ -ορος [ἀ-1 + ἀνήρ.] Deprived of virility; or perh. merely, unmanly Od. 10.301, 341.

ἀνήρ (ᾶ), ἀνδρός, ὁ. Genit. ἀνέρος Il. 3.61, Il. 5.649, etc.: Od. 1.161, 218, etc. Dat. ἀνέρι Il. 16.516, 716, etc.: Od. 1.292, Od. 2.223, etc. Acc. ἀνέρα Il. 13.131, Il. 16.215, etc. Voc. ἆνερ Il. 24.725. Nom. dual ἀνέρε Il. 12.421, 447, etc. Acc. ἀνέρε Il. 11.328. Nom. pl. ἀνέρες Il. 2.1, 604, etc. : Od. 1.176, Od. 3.471, etc. Dat. ἄνδρεσσι Il. 5.546, 874, etc.: Od. 1.358, Od. 10.120, etc. Acc. ἀνέρας Il. 1.262, Il. 2.554, etc.: Od. 11.630, Od. 13.261, etc. 1 a A man in general: ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Il. 1.7, περὶ ἀνδρῶν (beyond all men) Il. 21.215. Cf. Il. 2.198, Il. 3.429, Il. 5.37, Il. 9.197, etc.: ἄνδρα μοι ἔννεπε Od. 1.1, ἄνδρες ἂψ ἐγένοντο Od. 10.395. Cf. Od. 2.91, Od. 4.363, Od. 8.223, Od. 9.494, etc. b Mankind, man: ὀϊζυρώτερον ἀνδρός Il. 17.446. c Quasi-pronominal = one, anyone: ὅσσον ἀ. ἴδεν Il. 5.770. Cf. Il. 4.539, Il. 19.183, Il. 20.97, etc.: νεμεσσήσαιτό κεν ἀ. Od. 1.228. Cf. Od. 3.231, Od. 8.139, Od. 15.400, etc. d With a qualifying sb.: ἀ. βουληφόρος (a councillor) Il. 1.144, αἰπόλοι ἄνδρες (goatherds) Il. 2.474. Cf. Il. 3.170, Il. 4.187, Il. 6.315, Il. 9.524, etc.: ἀοιδὸς ἀ. Il. 20.267. Cf. Od. 8.584, Od. 9.126, Od. 14.102, Od. 15.427, etc. e With a proper name (cf. φώς 2): ἀνέρος λαομέδοντος Il. 5.649. Cf. Il. 11.92: Od. 7.22. f With ethnic words: Σίντιες ἄνδρες (the Sintians) Il. 1.594. Cf. Il. 3.6, Il. 5.779, Il. 10.487, etc.: Φοῖνιξ ἀ. (a Phoenician) Od. 14.288. Cf. Od. 3.31, Od. 6.3, Od. 14.263, etc. 2 Specifically. a A man as distinguished from a woman: πόλεμος ἄνδρεσσι μελήσει Il. 6.492. Cf. Il. 7.139, Il. 9.134, Il. 24.707, etc.: Od. 1.358, Od. 4.142, Od. 7.74, etc. b A husband Il. 3.140, Il. 14.504, Il. 19.295, etc.: Od. 1.292, Od. 6.181, Od. 7.68, etc. c A man as distigusihed from a god: Διὸς ἄγγελοι ἠδὲ καὶ ἀνδρῶν Il. 1.334. Cf. Il. 1.544, Il. 5.128, Il. 13.632, etc.: Ἀθήνη ἀνδρὶ ἐϊκυῖα Od. 8.194. Cf. Od. 1.28, Od. 13.112, Od. 16.265, etc. Sim. ἡμιθέων ἀνδρῶν Il. 12.22. With words indicative of mortality: βροτός Il. 5.361, Il. 18.85, etc.: Od. 4.397, Od. 5.129, etc.– θνητός Il. 10.403, Il. 16.441, etc.: Od. 10.306, Od. 16.196.– καταθνητός Il. 10.441. d A man as distinguished from a youth: ἤδη ἀ. [ἐστιν] Od. 19.160. Cf. Od. 11.449. e With words indicative of youthfulness, a youth: νέου ἀνδρός Il. 23.589. Cf. Il. 3.108: Od. 2.188, Od. 3.24, Od. 14.524, Od. 21.310, etc. f A man in the full sense of the term: ἀνέρες ἔστε (quit you like men) Il. 5.529, Il. 6.112, Od. 8.174, Il. 15.561, etc.

ἀνηρέψαντο 3 sing. pl. aor. mid. [No doubt for ἀνηρέψαντο, fr. ἀν-, ἀνα- 1 + ἁρεπ- = ἁρπ-, ἁρπάζω. Cf. ἅρπη, Ἅρπυια.] Thus, to snatch up: Γανυμήδεα ἀ. θεοί Il. 20.234. Cf. Od. 1.241 = Od. 14.371, Od. 4.727, Od. 20.77.
ἀνήροτος -ον [ἀ-1 + ἀρόω.] 1 Unploughed, untilled Od. 9.123. 2 Not growing as the result of tillage Od. 9.109.
ἀνήρπαξαν 3 pl. aor. ἀναρπάζω.
ἀνήρπασε 3 sing. aor. ἀναρπάζω.
ἀνήσει 3 sing. fut. ἀνίημι.
ἀνήφθω pf. imp. pass. ἀνάπτω.
ἀνῆψε 3 sing. aor. ἀνάπτω.
ἀνθεμόεις -εντος [ἄνθος.] 1 Flowery: λειμῶνι Il. 2.467. Cf. Il. 2.695: Od. 12.159. 2 Adorned with flower-like ornaments Il. 23.885: Od. 3.440, Od. 24.275.
ἀνθερεών -ῶνος, ὁ [ἀνθέω. The part on which the beard grows.] The chin Il. 1.501, Il. 3.372, Il. 5.293, Il. 13.388.
ἀνθέριξ -ικος. App., the stalk of corn: ἐπʼ ἀνθερίκων καρπὸν θέον (the ears of the corn) Il. 20.227.
ἀνθέω [ἄνθος.] Of hair on the face, to sprout, grow: πρὶν ἰούλους ἀνθῆσαι Od. 11.320.
ἄνθινος [ἄνθος.] The product of flowers, consisting of fruit: εἶδαρ Od. 9.84.

†ἀνθίστημι [ἀνθ-, ἀντι- 2.] 3 sing. aor. ἀντέστη Il. 20.70, 72. 3 pl. impf. mid. ἀνθίσταντο Il. 16.305. In aor. and mid., to face in fight. With dat.: Ἥρῃ Il. 20.70, Λητοῖ 72. Absol., to make a stand Il. 16.305.

ἄνθος τό. 1 A flower Il. 2.89, 468, Il. 9.542: Od. 6.231 = Od. 23.158, Od. 9.51, 449. 2 The characteristic flower of a plant: φάρμακον γάλακτι εἴκελον ἀ. (having a milk-white flower) Od. 10.304. 3 In collective sense, flowers, blossom: βρύει ἄνθεϊ λευκῷ Il. 17.56. Cf. Od. 7.126. 4 Fig.: ἔχει ἥβης ἀ. (is in the flower of his youth) Il. 13.484.
ἀνθρακιή -ῆς, ἡ. Hot embers Il. 9.213.

ἄνθρωπος -ου, ὁ 1 a A human being, a man (seldom in sing. and never of a particular man): ἐσσομένοισι μετʼ ἀνθρώποισιν Il. 3.287, μυὼν ἀνθρώπου Il. 16.315. Cf. Il. 6.14, Il. 9.134, Il. 10.213, Il. 13.733, etc.: πολλῶν ἀνθρώπων ἄστεα Od. 1.3, ὃς ἀνθρώπους ἐκέκαστο (all men) Od. 19.395. Cf. Od. 19.395. Cf. Od. 1.183, Od. 3.48, Od. 6.259, Od. 7.23, etc. For μεροπες ἄνθρωποι see μέροπες. b Mankind, man: οὐδὲν ἀκιδνότερον ἀνθρώπου Od. 18.130. c Quasi-pronominal = one, anyone: ὅ κε στυγέῃσιν ἰδὼν ἀ. ἔχοντά [σε] Od. 13.400. d With a qualifying sb.: ἀ. ὁδίτης Il. 16.263. Cf. Il. 24.202: Od. 7.32, Od. 13.123. 2 Specifically, a man as distinguished from a god: οὔτε θεῶν οὔτʼ ἀνθρώπων Il. 1.548. Cf. Il. 2.669, Il. 5.442, Il. 6.180, Il. 8.27, etc.: νέμεσις ἐξ ἀνθρώπων ἔσσεται Od. 2.136. Cf. Od. 13.110, Od. 14.179, Od. 20.112, Od. 22.346, etc. With words indicative of mortality: θνητός Il. 1.339, Il. 14.199, etc.: Od. 1.219, Od. 5.32, etc.– καταθνητός Il. 6.123: Od. 3.114, Od. 9.502, etc.

data.quote: ὅ κε στυγέῃσιν ἰδὼν ἀ. ἔχοντά [σε]

definition: ἀνιάζω [ἀνίη.] 1 To molest, annoy Od. 19.323. To weary, tire Il. 23.721. 2 To be overcome by distress or pain Il. 21.270: Od. 22.87. To weary, become tired Od. 4.460. To become impatient Od. 4.598. To be oppressed, feel hampered (by the possession of something): κτεάτεσσιν Il. 18.300.

ἀνιάω [ἀνίη.] 1 To trouble, vex Od. 2.115. 2 To make oneself a nuisance Od. 19.66, Od. 20.178. 3 In pass., to become disgusted or disheartened: ἀνιηθέντα νέεσθαι Il. 2.291. To become disgusted or wearied: ὀρυμαγδῷ Od. 1.133. To become wearied or impatient Od. 3.117. To be wearied or annoyed: οὔτις ἀνιᾶται παρεόντι (by your being here) Od. 15.335.
ἀνιδρωτί [ἀ-1 + ἱδρώς.] Without sweat, i.e. without conflict: οὔ κεν ἀ. γε τελέσθη Il. 15.228.
ἀνίη -ης, ἡ. 1 Trouble, inconvenience Od. 7.192. 2 A source of danger Od. 12.223. A bad thing for one Od. 15.394, Od. 20.52. A kill-joy: δαιτὸς ἀνίην Od. 17.446.

†ἀνίημι [ἀν-, ἀνα- 1, ἀνα- 3 + ἵημι1.] 3 sing. ἀνίησι Od. 4.568, Od. 12.105. 2 sing. opt. ἀνιείης Od. 2.185. Fem. pple. ἀνιεῖσα Il. 5.422. 3 sing. fut. ἀνήσει Il. 2.276. 3 sing. aor. ἀνέηκε Il. 5.882. 2 sing. ἀνῆκας Il. 21.396. 3 sing. ἀνῆκε Il. 2.71, Il. 5.405, Il. 6.256, Il. 7.25, etc.: Od. 7.289, Od. 8.73, Od. 14.465, Od. 17.425, Od. 18.199, Od. 19.551, Od. 24.440. 3 pl. aor. ἄνεσαν Il. 21.537. 3 sing. subj. ἀνήῃ Il. 2.34. 3 sing. opt. ἀνείη Il. 22.346. Pl. pple. ἀνέντες Il. 5.761. From ἀνιέω 2 sing. ἀνιεῖς Il. 5.880. 3 sing. impf. ἀνίει Il. 15.24. ἀνί̄ει Od. 8.359. Fem. pres. pple. mid. ἀνιεμένη Il. 22.80. Acc. masc. pl. ἀνιεμένους Od. 2.300. 1 To send up, cause to ascend: καπνόν Il. 21.523. To cause to flow up: [ὕδωρ] Od. 12.105. 2 To stir up, set on, urge, incite, impel: σοὶ ἔπι τοῦτον Il. 5.405. Cf. Il. 5.761, Il. 7.25, Il. 10.389, Il. 16.691, Il. 17.705, Il. 21.395, 545: Od. 2.185. With infin.: νεικείειν βασιλῆας Il. 2.276. Cf. Il. 5.422, 882, Il. 6.256, Il. 7.152, Il. 12.307, Il. 14.362, Il. 21.396, Il. 22.252, 346: ἀειδέμεναι Od. 8.73. Cf. Od. 14.465, Od. 17.425. Absol. Il. 5.880, Il. 20.118. To cause (a wind) to blow Od. 4.568. 3 To loose (a bond) Od. 8.359.– To loose the fastenings of: πύλας Il. 21.537. To relax hold upon, leave in peace: θυμὸν ὀδύνη Il. 15.24.– Of sleep, to leave, depart from Il. 2.34, 71: Od. 7.289, Od. 18.199, Od. 19.551, Od. 24.440. 4 In mid., to loose, allow to fall away (a part of one's dress): κόλπον Il. 22.80. App. by development of this sense, to take off the skin of, flay: αἶγας Od. 2.300.

data.ref: Od. 8.359.– To loose the fastenings of:

definition: ἀνιηρός [ἀνίη.] Troublesome, tiresome: πτωχόν Od. 17.220. Cf. Od. 17.377. In comp. in impers. construction: αὐτῷ οἱ ἀνιηρέστερον ἔσται (the worse for him) Od. 2.190.
ἀνιπτόπους -ποδος [ἀ-1 + νιπ-, νίζω + πούς.] With unwashen feet: ὑποφῆται Il. 16.235.
ἄνιπτος -ον [ἀ-1 + νιπ-, νίζω.] Unwashen Il. 6.266.

†ἀνίστημι [ἀν-, ἀνα- 1.] A 3 sing. impf. ἀνίστη Il. 24.515, 689. 3 pl. fut. ἀναστήσουσι Il. 7.116. Contr. 2 sing. ἀνστήσεις Il. 24.551. 3 pl. -ει Il. 15.64. Contr. pple. ἀνστήσων Il. 10.32. 3 sing. aor. ἀνέστησε Il. 24.756. 3 sing. opt. ἀναστήσειε Il. 1.191. Contr. imp. ἄνστησον Il. 10.176. Pple. ἀναστήσας Il. 10.179: Od. 6.7, Od. 7.163, 170, Od. 14.319. Contr. fem. ἀνστήσασα Il. 18.358. B 3 sing. aor. ἀνέστη Il. 1.68, 101, Il. 2.76, Il. 7.354, 365, Il. 9.195, Il. 15.287, Il. 18.305, 410, Il. 23.635, Il. 24.597: Od. 2.224, Od. 5.195, Od. 12.439, Od. 18.157, Od. 20.380, Od. 21.139, 166, 243, 392, Od. 23.164. 3 pl. ἀνέσταν Il. 1.533, Il. 7.161, Il. 23.886: Od. 8.258, Od. 10.215. Contr. 3 dual ἀνστήτην Il. 1.305. 3 sing. subj. ἀναστῇ Od. 18.334. Pple. ἀναστάς, -άντος Il. 1.387, Il. 19.77, 175, Il. 23.542, Il. 24.11: Od. 4.343, 776, Od. 16.378, Od. 17.134, Od. 18.47. Contr. ἀνστάς, -άντος Il. 2.398, Il. 19.269, Il. 23.848: Od. 4.674, Od. 12.170, 195, Od. 15.58, 96, Od. 16.358, 407, Od. 17.177. Fem. ἀνστᾶσα Il. 14.336: Od. 19.357. Contr. infin. ἀνστήμεναι Il. 10.55. Mid. 3 sing. impf. ἀνίστατο Il. 7.94, 123, Il. 23.491, 566, 677, 709, 734: Od. 20.124, Od. 21.144. Pple. ἀνιστάμενος, -ου Il. 1.58, Il. 9.52, Il. 19.55: Od. 3.341. 3 pl. fut. ἀναστήσονται Od. 21.56. Contr. infin. ἀνστήσεσθαι Il. 2.694. I In impf. act. and the other forms (A) 1 To cause to rise or stand up: γέροντʼ ἀνίστη Il. 24.515. Cf. Od. 7.163, 170, Od. 14.319. To break up (an assembly) Il. 1.191. To cause (a people) to migrate Od. 6.7. 2 To rouse from sleep Il. 10.32, 176, 179, Il. 24.689. 3 To raise from the dead Il. 24.551, 756. 4 To cause to take action, rouse to action Il. 15.64, Il. 18.358. To put forward (a champion) Il. 7.116. II In mid. and the other forms (B) 1 To rise or stand up: πάτροκλος ἀνέστη Il. 9.195. Cf. Il. 18.410, Il. 24.597: Od. 5.195, Od. 18.157 = Od. 21.139 = 166 = Od. 23.164, Od. 21.243 = 392. To rise up in token of respect Il. 1.533. Of a beast, to stand on its hind legs Od. 10.215. 2 To rise up with a view to action: ἀνστάντες ἔφερον Il. 23.848. Cf. Od. 3.341, Od. 4.674 = Od. 16.407, Od. 4.776, Od. 8.258, Od. 12.170, 195, Od. 16.358, Od. 17.177, Od. 18.47, Od. 19.357. 3 To rise to speak: ἀνιστάμενος μετέφη Il. 1.58 = Il. 19.55. Cf. Il. 1.68 = 101 = Il. 2.76 = Il. 7.354 = 365, Il. 1.387, Il. 7.94, 123, Il. 9.52, Il. 19.77, 175, 269, Il. 23.491, 542, 566, 734: ἀνέστη μαντεύεσθαι Od. 20.380. Cf. Od. 2.224, Od. 16.378. 4 To rise at the close of an assembly Il. 1.305, Il. 2.398. At the close of judicial business Od. 12.439. 5 To rise from bed or from sleep Il. 10.55, Il. 14.336, Il. 24.11: Od. 15.58, 96, Od. 20.124. 6 To rise from the dead Il. 21.56. As if from the dead Il. 15.287. 7 To rouse oneself to action Il. 2.694, Il. 18.305. To stand up to take part in a contest Il. 23.709, 886: Od. 4.343 = Od. 17.134, Od. 21.144. To stand up as a volunteer champion Il. 7.161. 8 To stand up (to another) in a fight, etc. Il. 23.635, 677: Od. 18.334.
ἀνίσχω [ἀ-1, ἀνα- 1.] To lift up (the hands) in prayer: χεῖρας ἀνίσχοντες Od. 8.347 = Il. 15.369.
ἀνιχνέυω [ἀν-, ἀνα- 6 + ἰχνεύω, to trace, fr. ἴχνος.] To trace or hunt out Il. 22.192.
ἀνιών pres. pple. ἄνειμι.
ἀννέομαι [ἀν-, ἀνα- 1.] Of the sun, to rise Od. 10.192.
ἀνοήμων [ἀ-1 + νοήμων.] Lacking understanding Od. 2.270, 278, Od. 17.273.
ἀνόλεθρος [ἀ-1 + ὄλεθρος.] Unscathed Il. 13.761.
ἄνοος -ον [ἀ-1 + νόος.] Senseless, foolish Il. 21.441.

ἀνοπαῖα [app. neut. pl. as adv. of an adj. ἀνοπαῖος fr. ἄνω2; or poss. of such an adj. fr. ἀ-1 + ὀπ-. See ὁράω.] Thus, upwards, or unseen Od. 1.320. (Others write ἀνόπαια, explained as a kind of eagle.)

ἀνορούω [ἀν-, ἀνα- 1.] 1 To rise or start up, spring up: ταφὼν ἀνόρουσεν Il. 9.193. Cf. Il. 1.248, Il. 10.162, 519, Il. 11.273 = 399, 777, Il. 17.130, Il. 19.396, Il. 21.246, Il. 23.101: Od. 3.149, Od. 4.839, Od. 10.557, Od. 14.518, Od. 16.12, Od. 22.23. 2 Of the sun, to rise Od. 3.1.
ἀνόστιμος [ἀ-1 + νόστιμος.] Cut off from return home: κεῖνον ἀνόστιμον ἔθηκεν Od. 4.182.
ἄνοστος [ἀ-1 + νόστος.] = ἀνόστιμος. Od. 24.528.
ἄνοστος [ἀ-1 + νοῦσος.] Afflicted by no disease: ἀσκηθέες καὶ ἄνουσοι Od. 14.255.
ἀνούτατος [ἀ-1 οὐτάω.] Not wounded (by thrust): ἄβλητος καὶ ἀνούτατος Il. 4.540.
ἀνουτητί [as ἀνούτατος.] Without inflicting a wound: οὐδέ οἵ τις ἀνουτητὶ παρέστη Il. 22.371.
ἀνστάς contr. aor. pple. ἀνίστημι B.
ἀνστήσει contr. 3 sing. fut. ἀνίστημι A.
ἀνστήτην contr. 3 dual aor. ἀνίστημι B.
ἀνστρέψειαν contr. 3 pl. aor. opt. ἀναστρέφω.
ἀνσχεθέειν contr. aor. infin. ἀνέχω.
ἄνσχεο contr. 2 sing. and imp. aor. mid. ἀνέχω.
ἀνσχετός [ἀν(α)σχε-, ἀνέχω.] To be endured, sufferable: ἀνσχετὰ ἔργα Od. 2.63.
ἀνσχήσεσθαι contr. fut. infin. mid. ἀνέχω.
