Il. 2.21, 404, Il. 4.323, 344, Il. 6.113, Il. 9.70, 89, 422, 574, Il. 15.721, Il. 18.448, Il. 19.303, 338 (here including Agamemnon, the king): γέροντας πλέονας καλέσαντες Od. 7.189. Cf. Od. 2.14, Od. 21.21, Od. 24.255. 5 An elder acting as one of a body of judges Il. 18.503.

γεύομαι With genit., to taste of, take a taste of. Fig.: δουρὸς ἀκωκῆς Il. 21.61. Cf. Od. 21.98. Also, fig., to make trial of, try one's fortune with: ἀλλήλων Il. 20.258: Ἀχαιῶν Od. 17.413, χειρῶν Od. 20.181.

γέφυρα ἡ. 1 A dike or embankment to confine a river: ποταμὸς ἐκέδασσε γεφύρας Il. 5.88. Cf. Il. 5.89. 2 π(τ)ολέμοιο γέφυραι, app., ranks of men thought of as stemming the tide of warIl. 4.371, Il. 8.378, Il. 11.160, Il. 20.427. In Il. 8.553 (ἐπὶ πτολέμοιο γεφύρας ἥατο) app., preserving (more or less) the stations in which they had fought.
γεφυρόω [γέφυρα.] 1 To dam (a river) Il. 21.245. 2 To make (a way) by forming an embankment: γεφύρωσε κέλευθον Il. 15.357.

γῆ γῆς, ἡ [cf. γαῖα.] 1 The earth = γαῖα 1: ὄφρʼ ἂν ἵκηται γῆν Il. 15.24, φυσίζοος Il. 21.63. Personified Il. 3.104, Il. 19.259. 2 The earth as distinguished from the sea, the land = γαῖα 2..b: ἢ ἁλὸς ἢ ἐπὶ γῆς Od. 12.27. Cf. Od. 21.233. 3 A particular land or country = γαῖα 4: τίς γῆ; Od. 13.233. One's native land: ἁμῆς γῆς Od. 11.167, 482. 4 The surface of the earth, the ground = γαῖα 5: νέρθεν γῆς Od. 11.302, ἦ πρὸς γῆν ἐλάσειε κάρη Od. 17.237.

γηθέω 3 sing. pf. (in pres. sense) γέγηθε Il. 8.559: Od. 6.106. 3 sing. plupf. (in impf. sense) γεγήθει Il. 11.683, Il. 13.494. 1 To rejoice, be glad Il. 1.255, Il. 6.212, Il. 7.189, Il. 8.559, Il. 11.683, Il. 13.416, 494, Il. 16.530, Il. 17.567, Il. 24.424: Od. 6.106, Od. 7.269, 329 = Od. 8.199 = Od. 13.250 = Od. 18.281, Od. 8.385, Od. 13.353 = Od. 21.414, Od. 20.104, Od. 24.382. With complementary pple.: οὐδὲ τὼ ἰδὼν γήθησεν Il. 1.330. Cf. Il. 4.255, 283, 311, Il. 7.214, Il. 8.278, Il. 10.190, Il. 13.344, Il. 14.140, Il. 24.321: Od. 5.486 = Od. 24.504, Od. 12.88, Od. 13.226, Od. 15.165, Od. 22.207. With acc. of what is rejoiced at: νῶϊ προφανέντε Il. 8.378, τάδε Il. 9.77. 2 To take pleasure or delight in doing something. With pple.: Ἀργείων ἐρέων γενεήν Il. 7.127.
γηθοσύνη -ης, ἡ [γηθέω.] Joy, delight: ἐγέλασσέ οἱ ἦτορ γηθοσύνῃ Il. 21.390. Of the sea Il. 13.29.
γηθόσυνος -η [as γηθοσύνη.] Joyful, glad, rejoicing Il. 4.272 = 326, Il. 7.122, Il. 13.82, Il. 18.557: Od. 5.269, Od. 11.540.
γῆμε 3 sing. aor. γαμέω.

γηράσκω [γῆρας.] From γηράω 3 sing. impf. ἐγήρα Il. 7.148, Il. 17.197. γήρα Od. 14.67. Also non-thematic pres. pple. γηράς Il. 17.197. (κατα-.) To grow old: ἤδη γηράσκοντα Il. 2.663. Cf. Il. 7.148, Il. 17.197 (twice), 325, Il. 24.541: Od. 4.210, Od. 14.67, Od. 15.409. Of fruit, to mellow Od. 7.120.
γῆρυς ἡ. Voice Il. 4.437.

γίγνομαι [redup. fr. γ(ε)ν-.] A 3 sing. pa. iterative γενέσκετο Od. 11.208. Aor. γενόμην Il. 18.102, Il. 19.219, Il. 21.440: Od. 8.311, Od. 14.141. 2 sing. γένευ Il. 5.897. 3 sing. γένετο Il. 1.49, Il. 6.153, Il. 13.417, Il. 23.526, etc.: Od. 2.26, Od. 4.11, Od. 24.292, etc. 3 dual γενέσθην Il. 5.548: Od. 11.255, 307, 312. 1 pl. γενόμεσθα Il. 21.89. With metrical lengthening of the first syllable γεινόμεθα Il. 22.477 (v.l. γιγνόμεθα). 2 pl. ἐγένεσθε Il. 2.323. 3 pl. (ἐ)γένοντο Il. 3.84, Il. 4.382, Il. 5.63, Il. 7.313, etc.: Od. 7.144, Od. 8.234, Od. 18.345, Od. 21.24, etc. Subj. γένωμαι Il. 8.180, Il. 16.39, Il. 22.358: Od. 5.473, Od. 11.73, Od. 22.167. 2 sing. -ηαι Il. 8.282, Il. 11.797: Od. 10.486. 3 sing. -ηται Il. 1.341, Il. 6.489, Il. 19.201, etc.: Od. 2.374, Od. 8.553, Od. 17.23, etc. 1 pl. -ώμεθα Il. 10.193, Il. 13.236, Il. 17.636. 2 pl. -ησθε Il. 5.488. 3 pl. -ωνται Il. 2.397, Il. 20.308. Opt. γενοίμην Il. 17.38: Od. 14.338, Od. 16.103. 2 sing. -οιο Od. 9.456, Od. 14.440, Od. 15.341, Od. 18.79. 3 sing. -οιτο Il. 4.17, Il. 8.26, Il. 13.233, etc.: Od. 3.129, Od. 8.414, Od. 18.161, etc. 1 pl. -οίμεθα Il. 13.485. 2 pl. -οισθε Il. 7.99. 3 pl. -οίατο Il. 2.340: Od. 1.266, Od. 4.346, Od. 17.137. 3 sing. imp. γενέσθω Il. 8.181: Od. 5.224, Od. 17.285, Od. 22.491. Pple. (with metrical lengthening of the first syllable) γεινόμενος, -ου (vv. ll. γιγνόμενος, -ου) Il. 10.71, Il. 20.128, Il. 23.79, Il. 24.210: Od. 4.208, Od. 7.198. Infin. γενέσθαι Il. 3.323, Il. 7.199, Il. 17.151, etc.: Od. 1.220, Od. 4.173, Od. 15.480, etc. 3 sing. pf. γέγονε Il. 19.122. 3 pl. γεγάασι Il. 4.325: Od. 5.35, Od. 6.62, Od. 9.118, Od. 10.5, Od. 13.160, Od. 19.279, Od. 24.84. 3 sing. plupf. γεγόνει Il. 13.355. Acc. sing. masc. pple. γεγαῶτα Il. 9.456: Od. 4.112, 144, Od. 19.400. Acc. pl. γεγαῶτας Il. 2.866. (For these pf. forms cf. μάω, μέμονα under μάω.) B 2 sing. aor. ἐγείναο Il. 5.880. 3 sing. (ἐ)γείνατο Il. 1.280, Il. 4.476, Il. 5.800, Il. 13.777, Il. 15.526, Il. 21.85, etc.: Od. 1.223, Od. 4.13, Od. 6.25, Od. 7.57, 61, Od. 11.268, 299, Od. 15.242, Od. 21.172. 2 sing. subj. γείνεαι Od. 20.202. Infin. γείνασθαι Il. 21.160: Od. 8.312. (ἐγ-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, παρα-, περι-, προ-.) I In pres. and impf. and forms (A), to come into being. 1 To be born, take one's being: τράφεν ἠδʼ ἐγένοντο Il. 1.251, τῶν ἓξ ἐγένοντο Il. 5.270, πρότερος γενόμην (am the elder) Il. 19.219, Il. 21.440. Cf. Il. 5.548, 897, Il. 6.206, 489, Il. 10.71, etc.: τοῦ μʼ ἔκ φασι γενέσθαι Od. 1.220, γαμέοντί τε γεινομένῳ τε Od. 4.208. Cf. Od. 3.28, Od. 4.723, Od. 7.198, Od. 8.311, Od. 10.350, etc. 2 In pf., to be in the condition of having been born; hence simply, to exist, live, be: οἳ ὁπλότεροι γεγάασιν Il. 4.325: ἐν αἶγες γεγάασιν Od. 9.118, οἳ νῦν γεγάασιν Od. 24.84. Cf. Od. 5.35 = Od. 19.279, Od. 6.62, Od. 10.5, Od. 13.160. In more strict pf. sense: ἤδη ἀνὴρ γέγονʼ ἐσθλός (has been born, is born) Il. 19.122. Sim. in plupf.: Ζεὺς πρότερος γεγόνει (had been born earlier, was the elder) Il. 13.355. In pple., born Il. 9.456: Od. 4.112, 144, Od. 19.400. So ὑπὸ τμώλῳ γεγαῶτας (born (and dwelling) there) Il. 2.866. 3 To come into view or notice, be seen, heard, etc.: κλαγγή Il. 1.49, ὀδμή Il. 14.415, σέλας Il. 19.374. Cf. Il. 4.456, Il. 10.375, Il. 11.50, Il. 15.607, Il. 22.150, etc.: Od. 12.87, 396, Od. 22.77, 133, Od. 23.137. 4 Of natural phenomena, natural products, etc., to come into being, rise, grow, be: φύλλα καὶ ἄνθεα Il. 2.468. Cf. Il. 2.397: ἐκ νυκτῶν ἄνεμοι γίγνονται Od. 12.287, ἐν οἶνος γίγνεται Od. 13.245, χιὼν γένετο (fell) Od. 14.476. Cf. Od. 9.51, Od. 12.326, Od. 17.23, Od. 22.491. 5 To come to or upon, fall to, befall, be the lot of, affect (a person). With dat.: Πηλεΐωνι ἄχος Il. 1.188, αἰδώς οἱ Il. 24.45. Cf. Il. 3.323, Il. 4.245, 289, Il. 9.125, Il. 14.98, Il. 19.274, etc.: παντα οἱ γένοιτο Od. 17.355, μὴ νῶϊν ἔρις γένηται Od. 18.13. Cf. Od. 8.414, Od. 11.208, Od. 18.122 = Od. 20.199, Od. 18.366, Od. 19.569, Od. 21.412. For ἐμὲ χρεὼ γίγνεται Od. 4.634 see χρειώ 1.a. Without case: ποινὴ οὔ τις ἐγίγνετο Il. 13.659. Cf. Il. 1.341, Il. 9.380, Il. 21.529: Od. 22.306. 6 To be manifested or shown, to be, come into play, take effect: οὔ τις φειδὼ γίγνεται (there is no . . .) Il. 7.410, μνημοσύνη τις γενέσθω (let there be . . .) Il. 8.181. Cf. Il. 15.359, Il. 23.505: εἰ γὰρ ἐπʼ ἀρῇσιν τέλος γένοιτο Od. 17.496. Cf. Od. 10.202 = 568. 7 To happen, occur, come round, come to pass, take place: ἠώς Il. 1.493, τάδε ἔργα Il. 6.348, ἀγορή Il. 7.345. Cf. Il. 3.110, 176, Il. 8.130, Il. 17.686, Il. 24.436, etc.: νόστον γενέσθαι Od. 4.173. Cf. Od. 1.379, Od. 2.26, 374, Od. 3.129, 228, Od. 4.747, Od. 5.299, Od. 11.537, Od. 12.191, Od. 24.455, 461, etc. 8 To become, come to be, prove to be so and so: ὁμηγερέες Il. 1.57, ἄνεῳ Il. 2.323, ἐν πυρὶ βουλαὶ γενοίατο (be cast) 340, κλισίῃσιν ἐν Ἀτρεΐδαο γένοντο (reached the . . .) Il. 7.313. Cf. Il. 2.453, Il. 3.71, Il. 4.17, 466, Il. 8.180, Il. 20.497, Il. 22.421, etc.: λέων γένετο Od. 4.456, ὄφρʼ ἔτι δύης ἐπὶ πῆμα γενοίμην (be brought into . . .) Od. 14.338, φόνος οἱ γένοντο Od. 21.24. Cf. Od. 1.266, Od. 3.271, Od. 7.154, 316, Od. 15.446, Od. 16.175, etc. 9 Passes from this last sense into that, practically, of the copula, to be so and so: οὔ πώ τις ὁμοῖος γένετʼ ἀνήρ (was) Il. 2.553, ὃν κάρτιστον Ἀχαιῶν φημὶ γενέσθαι (that he is) Il. 6.98, ζαχρηεῖς γίγνοντο (were wont to be) Il. 13.684, ἀρίγνωτος Διὸς γίγνεται ἀλκή Il. 15.490. Cf. Il. 4.375, Il. 6.153, 210, Il. 13.569, Il. 16.746, Il. 20.220, etc.: οὐ νηὸς ἐπήβολος γίγνομαι Od. 2.320, τηλύγετος Od. 4.11 (after ἐκ δούλης in 12 supply γεγαώς). Cf. Od. 4.201, 362, Od. 5.224, Od. 8.586, Od. 9.35, Od. 17.223, Od. 19.344, Od. 22.130, etc. II In forms (B), to give (a person) being. 1 Of the father, to beget: παῖδα γείνατο τυδεύς Il. 5.800. Cf. Il. 4.400, Il. 5.880, Il. 15.526, Il. 21.160: υἷε κραταιώ Od. 15.242. Cf. Od. 7.61, Od. 20.202. 2 Of the mother, to bear: θεά σε γείνατο μήτηρ Il. 1.280. Cf. Il. 3.238, Il. 4.476, Il. 5.896, Il. 6.24, 26, Il. 24.608, etc.: ἥ ῥʼ Ἡρακλῆα γείνατο Od. 11.268. Cf. Od. 1.223, Od. 4.13, Od. 6.25, Od. 11.299, Od. 21.172. 3 Of both parents Il. 7.10, Il. 21.142: Od. 7.57, Od. 8.312.

data.quote: εἰ γὰρ ἐπʼ ἀρῇσιν τέλος γένοιτο
ὄφρʼ ἔτι δύης ἐπὶ πῆμα γενοίμην
οὔ πώ τις ὁμοῖος γένετʼ ἀνήρ

definition: γιγνώσκω [redup. fr. γνω-.] 2 sing. fut. in mid. form γνώσεαι Il. 2.367, Il. 10.88: Od. 16.310. γνώσῃ Il. 2.365. 3 sing. -εται Il. 8.17, Il. 18.270. 1 pl. -όμεθα Od. 23.109. 2 pl. -εσθε Il. 23.497, Il. 24.242. Aor. ἔγνων Il. 11.526, Il. 13.72: Od. 15.532, Od. 19.475. 2 sing. ἔγνως Il. 20.20, Il. 22.10: Od. 13.299, Od. 17.273. 3 sing. ἔγνω Il. 1.199, Il. 13.66, Il. 16.530, Il. 17.32, etc.: Od. 1.3, Od. 5.444, Od. 7.234, Od. 11.91, etc. γνῶ Il. 4.357, Il. 7.189, Il. 10.358, Il. 11.439, Il. 16.119, 658: Od. 19.468. 3 dual γνώτην Od. 21.36. 3 pl. ἔγνωσαν Od. 10.397. Subj. γνώω Od. 14.118, Od. 17.549. 2 sing. γνώῃς Il. 23.487. γνῷς Od. 22.373. 3 sing. γνώῃ Il. 24.688: Od. 17.556. γνῷ Il. 1.411, Il. 16.273. 2 dual γνῶτον Od. 21.218. 1 pl. γνώομεν Od. 16.304. γνῶμεν Il. 22.382. 3 pl. γνώωσι Il. 1.302, Il. 23.610, 661, Il. 24.688. γνῶσι Il. 6.231. Opt. γνοίην Il. 3.235. 2 sing. γνοίης Il. 3.53, Il. 5.85, Il. 14.58: Od. 15.537, Od. 17.164, Od. 19.310, Od. 20.237, Od. 21.202. 3 sing. γνοίη Il. 17.630: Od. 13.192, Od. 16.458, Od. 17.363. 3 pl. γνοῖεν Il. 18.125. Imp. pl. γνῶτε Il. 19.84. Infin. γνώμεναι Il. 2.349, Il. 21.266, 609: Od. 1.411. γνῶναι Od. 2.159, Od. 13.312, Od. 24.159. (ἀνα-, δια-, ἐπι-.) 1 a To perceive, mark, remark, note, find, see, know: ἣν ἄτην Il. 1.411 = Il. 16.273, Διὸς τάλαντα Il. 16.658. Cf. Il. 12.272, Il. 16.119, 362, Il. 19.84. b With acc. and complementary pple.: γιγνώσκω Ἄρηα κοιρανέοντα Il. 5.824. Cf. Il. 14.154, Il. 17.84: Od. 15.532, Od. 17.549, 556. With pple. alone: ὅτε γίγνωσκε θεοῦ γόνον ἐόντα Il. 6.191: γνῶναι τὸν ἐόντα (that it was he) Od. 24.159. With a sim. pple. in genit.: ὡς γνῶ χωομένοιο Il. 4.357. With adj.: γνῶ. ἄνδρας δηΐους (that they were . . .) Il. 10.358. c With acc. and dependent clause: γιγνώσκω σε, ὅττι . . . Il. 24.563. Cf. Il. 5.85. With clause only: γνώμεναι εἰ . . . Il. 2.349. Cf. Il. 2.365, Il. 3.53, Il. 6.231, Il. 8.17, Il. 14.58, Il. 18.125, Il. 21.609, etc.: γνοίης χʼ οἵη ἐμὴ δύναμίς [ἐστιν] Od. 20.237. Cf. Od. 3.166, Od. 8.299, Od. 17.269, 363, Od. 22.373, etc. d Absol.: ἵνα γνώωσι καὶ οἵδε Il. 1.302. Cf. Il. 1.333 = Il. 8.446, Il. 13.66, Il. 22.296, Il. 23.487, Il. 24.242: γιγνώσκω, φρονέω Od. 16.136 = Od. 17.193 = 281, Od. 17.273, Od. 19.160. 2 To gain knowledge of, get to know, learn: Τρώων νόον Il. 22.382. Cf. Od. 1.3, Od. 16.304. To get to know, make the acquaintance of (a person) Od. 1.411. So with genit.: ἀλλήλων Od. 21.36. To become aware of the presence of, discover (a person) Il. 24.688 (twice), 691. To experience, find: φιλότητα Od. 15.537 = Od. 17.164 = Od. 19.310. 3 a To have knowledge, know: ὅσσον ἔγωγε γιγνώσκω Il. 13.223. With dependent clause: γιγνώσκων ὅ τʼ ἄναλκις ἔην θεός Il. 5.331. Cf. Il. 5.433: Od. 21.209. b In aor., to know: ἔγνως ἐμὴν βουλήν (knowest) Il. 20.20. To know (a person): αἴ κέ ποθι γνώω τοιοῦτον ἐόντα (in case I may find that I know him, seeing he was such a one, i.e. such as to be likely to be known) Od. 14.118. 4 To distinguish, discern: ἠμὲν θεὸν ἠδὲ καὶ ἄνδρα Il. 5.128. Cf. Il. 13.72. With acc. and dependent clause: ἵππους οἳ δεύτεροι οἵ τε πάροιθεν Il. 23.497. 5 To know (a person or thing) for what he or it is, know the nature of, know: εὖ σε γιγνώσκων Il. 22.356. Cf. Il. 17.32 = Il. 20.198, Il. 18.270: ἔγνω [ποταμόν] (i.e. recognized him for a god) Od. 5.444, καλάμην γιγνώσκειν (i.e. can judge from that what I was) Od. 14.215. Cf. Od. 2.159, Od. 16.310. Sim.: θεὸν ἔγνω (knew that it was a god) Od. 1.420. Absol., to recognize one's claim, hold it good Il. 23.661. 6 To know again, recognize, know: Ἀθηναίην Il. 1.199. Cf. Il. 3.235, Il. 5.182, 815, Il. 7.189, Il. 10.88, Il. 11.111, 526, 651, Il. 14.475, Il. 15.241, Il. 16.639, Il. 17.334, Il. 24.698: φᾶρος Od. 7.234. Cf. Od. 10.397, Od. 11.91, 153, 390, 471, 615, Od. 13.188, 192, 299, 312, Od. 16.458, Od. 19.392, 468, 475, Od. 21.218, Od. 22.501, Od. 24.102. Absol. Il. 7.185, Il. 23.453: Od. 20.94. To find means of recognizing. With genit.: ἀλλήλων Od. 23.109.

data.quote: γιγνώσκων ὅ τʼ ἄναλκις ἔην θεός
ἵππους οἳ δεύτεροι οἵ τε πάροιθεν

definition: γλάγος τό [cf. γάλα.] Milk Il. 2.471 = Il. 16.643.
γλακτοφάγος [γαλακτοφάγος, fr. γαλακτ-, γάλα + φάγον.] Living on (mare's) milk Il. 13.6.
†γλαυκιάω [γλαυκός.] Pres. pple. γλαυκιόων. To have the eyes bright or glaring. Of a lion Il. 20.172.
γλαυκός -ή. Bright, shining, gleaming (prob. without any notion of colour). Of the sea Il. 16.34.

γλαυκῶπις -ιδος [γλαυκός + ὦπα.] Acc. γλαυκώπιδα Il. 8.373. γλαυκῶπιν Od. 1.156. (The) bright-eyed (maid) (prob. without any notion of colour). Epithet or a name of Athene Il. 1.206, Il. 2.166, Il. 5.29, Il. 6.88, Il. 8.373, etc.: Od. 1.44, 156, Od. 2.433, Od. 3.13, 135, etc.

γλαφυρός -ή, -όν [γλάφω = γλύφω. See γλυφίς, and cf. διαγλάφω.] Hollow, hollowed (for the most part as a conventional epithet). Of caves Il. 18.402, Il. 24.83: Od. 1.15 = Od. 9.30, Od. 1.73, Od. 2.20, Od. 4.403, Od. 5.68, 155, 194, 226, Od. 9.114, 476, Od. 12.210, Od. 23.335. Of rocks, having a cavity or cavities Il. 2.88: Od. 14.533. Of the lyre Od. 8.257, Od. 17.262, Od. 22.340, Od. 23.144. Of a harbour (referring to the curved outline) Od. 12.305. Elsewhere epithet of ships Il. 2.454, 516, Il. 3.119, Il. 5.327, Il. 8.180, etc.: Od. 3.287, Od. 4.356, 513, Od. 9.99, Od. 10.23, etc.
γλήνη -ης, ἡ [app. something bright. Cf. γλῆνος.] 1 The eye, the eyeball Il. 14.494: Od. 9.390. 2 A plaything, a doll or puppet: ἔρρε, κακὴ γλήνη Il. 8.164.
γλῆνος τό [cf. γλήνη.] In pl. γλήνεα, trinketsIl. 24.192.
γλουτός -οῦ, ὁ. One of the buttocks: δεξιόν Il. 5.66, Il. 13.651. In pl., the buttocks, the rump Il. 8.340.

γλυκερός -ή, -όν [cf. γλυκύς.] 1 Sweet or pleasant to the taste: σίτου Il. 11.89: συκέαι Od. 7.116 = Od. 11.590 (the tree for the fruit). Cf. Od. 4.88, Od. 14.194, Od. 20.69, Od. 24.68. Of water, sweet, fit for drinking Od. 12.306. 2 Generally, sweet, pleasant, giving delight or joy: ὕπνος Il. 10.4, μολπῆς Il. 13.637. Cf. Il. 24.3, 636: Od. 4.295, Od. 5.472, Od. 16.23 = Od. 17.41, Od. 19.511, Od. 22.323, Od. 23.145, 255. In comp.: ἧς γαίης γλυκερώτερον ἄλλο Od. 9.28.
γλυκύθυμος [γλυκύς + θυμός.] Of gentle or kindly mind: ἀνήρ Il. 20.467.

γλυκύς -ύ. Comp. γλυκίων, γλύκιον Il. 1.249, Il. 2.453, Il. 11.13, Il. 18.109: Od. 9.34. 1 Sweet or pleasant to the taste: νέκταρ Il. 1.598. 2 Generally, sweet, pleasant: ὕπνος Il. 1.610, ἵμερον Il. 3.139. Cf. Il. 2.71, Il. 3.446, Il. 14.328, Il. 23.232: αἰών Od. 5.152. Cf. Od. 2.395, Od. 7.289, Od. 8.445, Od. 9.333, Od. 10.31 = Od. 13.282, Od. 10.548, Od. 12.338, Od. 15.7, Od. 18.188, 199, Od. 19.49, Od. 22.500, Od. 23.342. In comp. Il. 1.249, Il. 2.453 = Il. 11.13, Il. 18.109: Od. 9.34.

γλυφίς -ίδος, ἡ [γλύφω, to cut out, carve. Cf. γλαφυρός.] App., the notch in an arrow to receive the string. In pl. (poss. referring to a double notch (i.e. two notches at right angles)) Il. 4.122: Od. 21.419.

γλῶσσα -ης, ἡ. 1 The tongue Il. 1.249, Il. 2.489, Il. 5.74, 292, Il. 16.161, Il. 17.618, Il. 20.248. Of the tongues of sacrificial victims Od. 3.332, 341. 2 A tongue or language Il. 2.804: Od. 19.175. Language, speech: γ. ἐμέμικτο Il. 4.438.

γλωχίς -ῖνος [cf. τανυγλώχις.] App., a tongue forming one of the ends of the ζυγόδεσμον or yoke-fastening, the ζ. being wound round the pole criss-cross, keeping the portion with the tongue the longer, and the tongue being tucked in under its portion after that portion had been wound over, and had so secured, the end of the other and shorter portion: ὑπὸ γλωχῖνα δʼ ἔκαμψαν Il. 24.274 (ὑπό advbl.).
γναθμός -οῦ, ὁ. The lower jaw Il. 13.671 = Il. 16.606, Il. 16.405, Il. 17.617. In pl., the jaws Od. 16.175, Od. 18.29, Od. 20.347.

γναμπτός -ή, -όν [γνάμπτω.] 1 Bent, curved: ἕλικας Il. 18.401: ἀγκίστροισιν Od. 4.369 = Od. 12.332. 2 Fig., that can be bent or influenced: νόημα Il. 24.41. 3 As epithet of the limbs, flexible, lissom Il. 11.669, Il. 24.359: Od. 11.394, Od. 13.398, 430, Od. 21.283. Sim. of jaws, moving freely in their sockets Il. 11.416.
†γνάμπτω [ = κνάμπτω.] 3 sing. aor. γνάμψε. (ἀνα-, ἐπι-, περι-) To bend: ἐν γόνυ γνάμψεν (app., crooked his knee round the other's leg) Il. 23.731.
γνήσιος [γ(ε)ν-, γίγνομαι.] (Lawfully) begotten, born in wedlock, legitimate Il. 11.102: Od. 14.202.
γνοίην aor. opt. γιγνώσκω.
γνύξ [γόνυ.] On the knee or the knees: ἔριπεν Il. 5.68. Cf. Il. 5.309, 357, Il. 8.329, Il. 11.355, Il. 20.417.
γνῶ 3 sing. aor. γιγνώσκω.
γνώῃ γνῷ 3 sing. aor. subj. γιγνώσκω.
γνώμεναι γνῶναι aor. infin. γιγνώσκω.
γνώριμος [γνω-, γιγνώσκω.] (Well-) known. Absol., a friend or acquaintance Od. 16.9.
γνώσεται 3 sing. fut. γιγνώσκω.

γνωτός -ή, -όν [γνω-, γιγνώσκω.] 1 Easy to be known, evident: γνωτόν [ἐστιν] ὡς . . . Il. 7.401 Cf. Od. 24.182. 2 As sb. a A kinsman or kinswoman: γνωτοὺς λιποῦσα Il. 3.174, γνωτοί τε γνωταί τε Il. 15.350. Cf. Il. 13.697 = Il. 15.336. b More specifically, a brother (and the word may bear this sense in the passages under a) Il. 14.485, Il. 17.35, Il. 22.234.
γνώω aor. subj. γιγνώσκω.

†γοάω [γόος.] 1 pl. opt. γοάοιμεν Il. 24.664. γοάοιεν Od. 24.190. Pple. γοόων, -ωντος Od. 10.209, Od. 12.234, Od. 19.119. Contr. pl. γοῶντες Il. 18.315, 355: Od. 9.467. Fem. γοόωσα, -ης Il. 5.413, Il. 6.373, Il. 16.857, Il. 22.363, 476, Il. 23.106: Od. 4.721, 800, Od. 19.210, 264, 513. Non-thematic infin. γοήμεναι Il. 14.502. 3 pl. impf. γόων Od. 10.567. 3 sing. pa. iterative γοάασκε Od. 8.92. 3 sing. fut. in mid. form γοήσεται Il. 21.124, Il. 22.353. 3 pl. aor. γόον (perh. formed fr. γόος) Il. 6.500. 1 To weep, wail, show signs of grief: μὴ γοόωσα οἰκῆας ἐγείρῃ Il. 5.413. Cf. Il. 6.373, Il. 18.315, 355, Il. 22.476, Il. 23.106: ἑζόμενοι γόων Od. 10.567. Cf. Od. 4.721, 800, Od. 8.92, Od. 9.467, Od. 10.209, Od. 12.234, Od. 19.119, 210, 513. 2 To weep for, bewail, lament, mourn for the loss of: Ἕκτορα Il. 6.500, ὃν πότμον Il. 16.857 = Il. 22.363: πόσιν Od. 19.264. 3 To pay mourning rites to: αὐτόν Il. 24.664. Cf. Il. 14.502, Il. 21.124, Il. 22.353: Od. 24.190.
γόμφος -ου, ὁ. A wooden peg, a treenail Od. 5.248.
γονή -ῆς, ἡ [γον-, γεν-, γίγνομαι.] 1 Offspring Il. 24.539. 2 Progeny, descendants: Ἀρκεισιάδαο Od. 4.755.

γόνος -ου, ὁ [as γονή.] 1 One sprung or born. a The offspring, a child: διός Il. 5.635. Cf. Il. 24.59: Od. 2.274, Od. 4.207, Od. 18.218. b A remoter descendant Il. 6.191, Il. 13.449. c In both these senses: ὃν (i.e. Λαέρταο) καὶ Ὀδυσσῆος Od. 4.741. 2 The race: ἀτρέος Od. 11.436. 3 Offspring Il. 9.493: Od. 4.12, Od. 12.130. One's children or family: νεώτατος γόνοιο Il. 20.409. 4 One's parentage: ὃν γόνον ἐξαγόρευεν Od. 11.234. Cf. Od. 1.216, Od. 19.166.

γόνυ τό. Genit. γουνός (for γονϝ-ός) Il. 11.547: Od. 19.450. γούνατος Il. 21.591. Nom. pl. γούνατα Il. 4.314, Il. 9.610, Il. 19.166, Il. 21.114, etc.: Od. 4.703, Od. 5.297, Od. 13.34, Od. 23.3, etc. γοῦνα Il. 6.511, Il. 14.468, Il. 21.611, etc.: Od. 20.352. Genit. γούνων Il. 1.407, Il. 6.45, Il. 21.65, Il. 22.338, etc.: Od. 6.142, Od. 10.264, Od. 22.310, 339, etc. Dat. γούνασι Il. 5.370, Il. 6.92, Il. 17.514, Il. 22.500, etc.: Od. 1.267, Od. 7.142, Od. 16.443, Od. 21.55, etc. γούνεσσι Il. 9.488, Il. 17.451, 569. Acc. γούνατα Il. 5.176, Il. 11.609, Il. 21.52, Il. 24.478, etc.: Od. 3.92, Od. 5.453, Od. 14.236, Od. 24.381, etc. γοῦνα Il. 14.437, Il. 20.93, Il. 22.204: Od. 6.147, Od. 9.266, Od. 18.395. 1 The knee of men or animals: ῥίμφα ἑ γοῦνα φέρει Il. 6.511 = Il. 15.268. Cf. Il. 7.118, Il. 10.358, Il. 11.547, Il. 14.437, 468, Il. 15.269, Il. 17.386, Il. 19.72, Il. 20.458, Il. 21.302, 591, 611, Il. 22.24, 144, 452, Il. 23.731: ἔλασε γουνὸς ὕπερ Od. 19.450. Cf. Od. 5.453, Od. 20.352, Od. 23.3. 2 In pl., the knees regarded as the seat of strength, as symbolizing the strength (cf. γυῖα 3): βλάψε οἱ γούνατα Il. 7.271. Cf. Il. 4.314, Il. 5.176 = Il. 16.425, Il. 9.610 = Il. 10.90, Il. 11.477, 578 = Il. 13.412 = Il. 17.349, Il. 13.360, 711, Il. 15.291, Il. 17.451, 569, Il. 19.166, 354, Il. 20.93, Il. 21.52, 114, 270, 425, Il. 22.204, 335, 388, Il. 23.444, Il. 24.498: τῆς λύτο γούνατα Od. 4.703 = Od. 23.205. Cf. Od. 5.297 = 406 = Od. 22.147, Od. 13.34, Od. 14.69, 236, Od. 18.133, 212, Od. 20.118, Od. 22.68, Od. 24.345, 381. 3 Of clasping the knees in supplication: λαβέ [μιν] γούνων (by the knees) Il. 1.407. Cf. Il. 1.500, 512, 557, Il. 6.45, Il. 15.76, Il. 20.468, Il. 21.65, 68, 71, Il. 22.345, Il. 24.357, 465, 478: μητρὸς ποτὶ γούνασι χεῖρας βάλλειν Od. 6.310. Cf. Od. 6.142, 147, 169, Od. 7.142, Od. 10.264, 323, Od. 22.310, 339, 342, 365. So with a word of seizing to be supplied: λισσέσκετο γούνων Il. 9.451. Cf. Od. 10.481, Od. 22.337. Sim.: περὶ γούνατʼ ἐμὰ στήσεσθαι λισσομένους Il. 11.609. Cf. Il. 18.457, Il. 20.463: σὰ γούναθʼ ἱκάνω Od. 5.449, Od. 7.147, Ἀμφινόμου πρὸς γοῦνα καθέζετο (as putting himself under his protection) Od. 18.395. Cf. Od. 3.92 = Od. 4.322, Od. 9.266, Od. 13.231. Also λίσσομʼ ὑπὲρ γούνων Il. 22.338. Of kissing the knees in supplication: ἥ οἱ γούνατʼ ἔκυσσε Il. 8.371. Cf. Od. 14.279. 4 By extension, in pl., the knee(s) and thigh(s) of a sitting person: ἐν γούνασι πῖπτε διώνης (on her knee) Il. 5.370, Ἀθηναίης ἐπὶ γούνασιν (on the lap, i.e., app., of a seated statue) Il. 6.92, 273, 303. Cf. Il. 5.408, Il. 9.455, 488, Il. 21.506, Il. 22.500: ἐμὲ γούνασιν οἷσιν ἐφεσσάμενος Od. 16.443. Cf. Od. 19.401, Od. 21.55.–ταῦτα θεῶν ἐν γούνασι κεῖται, the issue lies with the gods(perh. referring to the custom of placing gifts on the lap of a statue (cf. Il. 6.92, 273, 303 cited above), the gifts being irrevocably dedicated, and symbolizing complete submission to divine governance) Il. 17.514 = Il. 20.435: = Od. 1.267 = Od. 16.129, Od. 1.400.

data.ref: 303 cited above), the gifts being irrevocably dedicated, and symbolizing complete submission to divine governance)

definition: γόον 3 pl. aor. γοάω.

γόος -ου, ὁ. 1 Weeping, wailing, lamentation, mourning Il. 5.156, Il. 6.499, Il. 17.37, Il. 18.51, Il. 23.10, 14, etc.: Od. 4.102, 113, Od. 8.540, Od. 16.144, Od. 19.268, Od. 21.228, etc. In pl.: ὀδύνας τε γόους τε Od. 1.242. 2 Inclination to weep: πᾶσιν ὑπέδυ γ. Od. 10.398. 3 Mourning rites, formal mourning or lamentation: ἦρχε γόοιο Il. 24.723. Cf. Il. 24.747, 761.
γοόων γοόωσα pres. pple. γοάω.

γουνάζομαι [γουν-, γόνυ. To clasp the knees, clasp by the knees, in supplication. Cf. γόνυ 3.] Fut. γουνάσομαι Il. 1.427. To supplicate, entreat. Retaining the genitival construction of a vb. of taking hold, and with the construction extended to something appealed to: μή με γούνων γουνάζεο μηδὲ τοκήων Il. 22.345. With this latter construction alone: τῶν ὄπιθέν σε γουνάζομαι Od. 11.66. With prepositional clauses indicating what is appealed to: τῶν ὕπερ Il. 15.665. Cf. Od. 11.66, Od. 13.324. With simple acc. of the person entreated: γουνάσομαί μιν Il. 1.427. Absol. Il. 11.130.

data.quote: μή με γούνων γουνάζεο μηδὲ τοκήων

definition: γούνατος γουνός genit. γόνυ.

γουνός [perh. fr. γονϝ-, γόνυ, in sense swell, knoll, and, in reference to a vineyard, etc., the part best catching the sun, and therefore the most fruitful.] γουνῷ (γουνὸν) ἀλωῆς Il. 9.534, Il. 18.57 = 438: Od. 1.193, Od. 11.193, ἐς γουνὸν Ἀθηνάων Od. 11.323 (here perh. the reference is to the citadel).

γουνοῦμαι = γουνάζομαι. To supplicate, entreat: υἱόν Il. 9.583. Cf. Il. 15.660, Il. 21.74, Il. 22.240: Od. 4.433, Od. 6.149, Od. 22.312, 344. App., to supplicate (and at the same time to vow to do something): νεκύων κάρηνα ῥέξειν . . . Od. 10.521, Od. 11.29.
γοῶντες contr. nom. pl. masc. pres. pple. γοάω.
γραίη -ης, ἡ. = γρηΰς: πυκιμηδέος Od. 1.438.
γραπτύς ἡ [γραπ-, γράφω.] Acc. pl. γραπτῦς. A scratch: γραπτῦς ἀλεείνων Od. 24.229.
†γράφω 3 sing. aor. γράψε Il. 17.599. Pple. γράψας Il. 6.169. (ἐπι-.) 1 To scratch, cut into, incise: δ'στέον Il. 17.599. 2 To form by scratching or incision: θυμοφθόρα Il. 6.169.

γρηΰς γρηῦς ἡ. Dat. γρηΐ Il. 3.386: Od. 1.191, Od. 18.27, Od. 23.33. Voc. γρηΰ Od. 22.395, 481. γρηῦ Od. 19.383, Od. 22.411. An old woman Il. 3.386: Od. 2.377, Od. 7.8, Od. 18.185, Od. 19.346, Od. 23.1, etc. In apposition: γρηΐ ἀμφιπόλῳ Od. 1.191. Cf. Od. 18.27, Od. 24.211.

γύαλον -ου, τό [cf. γυρός.] (ἐγγυαλίζω). One of the two curved plates, front and back, of which the θώρηξ was formed. The front plate Il. 5.99, 189, Il. 13.507 = Il. 17.314, Il. 13.587. In pl. of the two plates Il. 15.530.

γυῖα τά [γυ-, to bend. Cf. γύαλον, γυρός.] 1 A joint: γ. ποδῶν Il. 13.512. 2 The limbs: γ. ἔθηκεν ἐλαφρά Il. 5.122 = Il. 13.61 = Il. 23.772. Cf. Il. 19.385, Il. 22.448, Il. 23.691. 3 The limbs regarded as the seat of strength, as symbolizing the strength (cf. γόνυ 2): λῦσε γ. Il. 4.469 = Il. 11.260, Il. 11.240, Il. 16.312 = 400, 465, Il. 21.406. Cf. Il. 4.230, Il. 5.811, Il. 6.27, Il. 7.6, 12, 16, Il. 13.85 435, Il. 15.435, 581, Il. 16.341, 805, Il. 17.524, Il. 18.31, Il. 19.165, 169, Il. 23.63, 627, 726: ἐκ κάματον εἵλετο γυίων Od. 10.363. Cf. Od. 1.192, Od. 8.233, Od. 12.279, Od. 18.238, 242, 341. As that upon which fear takes hold or which it affects: τρόμος ἔλλαβε γ. Il. 3.34, Il. 8.452, Il. 14.506, Il. 24.170. Cf. Il. 7.215 = Il. 20.44, Il. 10.95, 390: Od. 6.140, Od. 11.527, Od. 18.88. App. as the seat of yearning: ἦλθʼ ἵμερος [γόοιο] ἀπὸ γυίων Il. 24.514.
γυιόω [γυιός, lame.] (ἀπο-.) To lame, cripple: γυιώσω σθωῒν ἵππους Il. 8.402. Cf. Il. 8.416.

γυμνός 1 Without clothes, naked: σὲ εὐλαὶ ἔδονται γυμνόν Il. 22.510. Cf. Od. 6.136. 2 Without armour, unarmed: κτενέει με γυμνὸν ἐόντα Il. 22.124. Cf. Il. 16.815, Il. 17.122 = 693, 711, Il. 18.21, Il. 21.50. 3 Of a bow, out of its case Od. 11.607. Of an arrow, out of the quiver Od. 21.417.

γυμνόω [γυμνός.] (ἀπο-) To make naked. In pass. 1 To become naked, strip oneself: αἰδέομαι γυμνοῦσθαι Od. 6.222. Cf. Od. 10.341. To strip oneself of. With genit.: γυμνώθη ῥακέων Od. 22.1. 2 To be left unprotected by armour or shield: οὖτα γυμνωθέντα Il. 16.312 = 400. Cf. Il. 12.389, 428. Of a wall, to be left bare of defence Il. 12.399.
γυναικεῖος -η, -ον [γυναικ-, γυνή.] Of a woman: βουλάς Od. 11.437.
γυναιμανής [γυναι-, γυνή + μαν-, μαίνομαι.] Mad for women Il. 3.39 = Il. 13.769.
γύναιος [γυνή.] Of a woman: δώρων (given to a woman) Od. 11.521, Od. 15.247.

γυνή γυναικός, ἡ. Voc. γύναι (see 5 below). 1 A woman in gen. Il. 1.348, Il. 2.226, Il. 3.72, Il. 4.141, Il. 5.349, Il. 9.128, Il. 11.269, Il. 12.433, etc.: Od. 1.332, Od. 3.154, Od. 7.57, Od. 11.258, Od. 13.288, Od. 15.20, Od. 18.248, Od. 19.235, etc. 2 The mistress of a house Od. 16.334, Od. 21.86. 3 In pl., the female servants in a house: τετυγμένα χερσὶ γυναικῶν Il. 22.511. Cf. Il. 18.559: εἰς ὅ κʼ εἴπω γυναιξὶ δεῖπνον τετυκεῖν Od. 15.76. Cf. Od. 2.108, Od. 16.304, Od. 17.75, Od. 18.186, Od. 19.16, Od. 22.437, etc. With ἀμφίπολος Od. 1.362, Od. 6.52, Od. 7.235, Od. 16.413, Od. 21.8, etc. With δμῳή Il. 6.323, Il. 9.477: Od. 7.103, Od. 13.66, Od. 16.108 = Od. 20.318, Od. 17.505, Od. 19.490, Od. 22.37, etc. In sing., one of the servants Od. 15.417, 434, 439, Od. 19.344, etc. With words indicating the servant's country of origin: Φοίνισσα Od. 15.417, Σικελή Od. 24.211. Her office: ταμίη Il. 6.390: Od. 2.345, Od. 3.479, ἀλετρίς Od. 20.105. 4 Specifically. a A woman as distinguished from a man: γυναικὸς ἀντὶ τέτυξο Il. 8.163. Cf. Il. 7.139, 236, Il. 9.134, Il. 15.683, etc.: οὔτʼ ἄνδρʼ οὔτε γυναῖκα Od. 4.142, Od. 6.161. Cf. Od. 7.109, Od. 13.308, Od. 15.163, Od. 19.408, etc. b A wife: σὺν γυναιξί τε καὶ τεκέεσσιν Il. 4.162. Cf. Il. 3.48, Il. 6.160, Il. 8.57, Il. 9.394, Il. 17.36, etc.: ἀνὴρ ἠδὲ γ. Od. 6.184. Cf. Od. 1.13, 433, Od. 2.249, Od. 7.347, Od. 14.211, Od. 17.152, Od. 21.72, etc. c A concubine as opposed to a wife Il. 24.497. d A woman as distinguished from a goddess: θεᾶς οὐδὲ γυναικός Il. 14.315. Cf. Il. 16.176, Il. 24.58: ἢ θεὸς ἠὲ γ. Od. 10.228, 255. With words indicative of mortality: θνητάων Il. 20.305: θνητήν Od. 11.244. 5 In voc. as a term of courteous or respectful address, lady Il. 3.204, 438, Il. 6.441, Il. 24.300: Od. 4.148, Od. 6.168, Od. 8.424, Od. 11.248, etc.

data.quote: εἰς ὅ κʼ εἴπω γυναιξὶ δεῖπνον τετυκεῖν

definition: γυρός [cf. γυῖα, γύαλον.] Bent, rounded Od. 19.246.
γύψ γυπός, ὁ. A vulture (except in Od. 11.578 always preying on carrion. Cf. αἰγυπιός) Il. 4.237, Il. 11.162, Il. 16.836, Il. 18.271, Il. 22.42: Od. 11.578, Od. 22.30.

data.ref: Od. 11.578 always preying on carrion. Cf.

definition: γωρυτός -οῦ, ὁ. A case for a bow Od. 21.54.
δαείω aor. subj. δάω.
δαήμεναι δαῆναι aor. infin. δάω.
δαήμων -ονος [δάω.] Skilled, experienced Il. 15.411, Il. 23.671. With genit.: ἄθλων (in . . .) Od. 8.159. Cf. Od. 8.263, Od. 16.253.
δαήρ -έρος, ὁ (δαϝήρ). Voc. δᾶερ (see below). Genit. pl. δαέρων as spondee Il. 24.762, 769. A brother-in-law Il. 3.180, Il. 14.156, Il. 24.762, 769. In voc. Il. 6.344, 355.
δαήσεαι 2 sing. fut. δάω.
δάηται 3 sing. aor. subj. pass. δαίω1.
δαί Emphasizing particle used after interrogatives: τίς δ. ὅμιλος; Od. 1.225. Cf. Il. 10.408 (v.l. δʼ αἱ): Od. 24.299.
δαιδάλλω [δαίδαλον.] To ornament curiously: σάκος Il. 18.479: χρυσῷ τε καὶ ἀργύρῳ Od. 23.200.

δαίδαλον -ου, τό. Something curiously wrought, an ornament Od. 19.227. In pl., things curiously wrought, pieces of cunning workmanship, ornaments: χάλκευον δαίδαλα πολλά Il. 18.400. Cf. Il. 5.60, Il. 14.179, Il. 18.482, Il. 19.13, 19.

δαΐζω [δαίω2.] Aor. infin. δαΐξαι Il. 2.416, Il. 16.841. Pf. pple. pass. δεδαϊγμένος, -ου Il. 17.535, Il. 18.236, Il. 19.203, 211, 283, 292, 319, Il. 22.72: Od. 13.320. 1 To rend, tear: Ἑκτόρεον χιτῶνα Il. 2.416. Cf. Il. 7.247, Il. 16.841. To tear (the hair) Il. 18.27. 2 To rend the flesh of, wound, slay: δεδαϊγμένον ἦτορ (app., with the life killed in him) Il. 17.535, δαΐζων χαλκᾠ Il. 24.393. Cf. Il. 11.497, Il. 18.236, Il. 19.203, 211, 283, 292, 319, Il. 21.147, Il. 22.72. Absol., to do execution Il. 21.33. 3 To divide (meat) into portions Od. 14.434. 4 Fig., in pass., to be in two minds, be in doubt: δαϊζόμενος ἢ . . . ἦε . . . Il. 14.20 Of the mind, etc., to be troubled or distressed: ἐδαΐζετο θυμός Il. 9.8 = Il. 15.629. Cf. Od. 13.320.
δαϊκτάμενος [δαΐ, dat. of δάϊς + κτάμενος. See κτείνω.] Slain in battle: αἰζηῶν Il. 21.146, 301.

δαιμόνιος -η [δαίμων.] Under superhuman influence, possessed, whose actions are unaccountable or ill-omened. In voc. 1 In stern reproof Il. 1.561, Il. 6.326, Il. 9.40. More gently Il. 6.521. 2 In more or less stern remonstrance Il. 2.190, Il. 3.399, Il. 4.31: Od. 18.15, Od. 19.71. In tender or gentle remonstrance Il. 6.407, 486: Od. 10.472, Od. 23.166, 174, 264. 3 Conveying an implication of folly or senselessness Il. 2.200, Il. 13.448, 810: Od. 4.774, Od. 18.406. 4 App. indicating a degree of wonder, the person addressed showing himself superior to what his outward man would indicate: δαιμόνιε ξείνων Od. 14.443. 5 App., with orig. sense lost sight of, merely in affectionate address Il. 24.194.

δαίμων -ονος, ὁ, ἡ. 1 A superhuman power, with little notion of personality (sometimes difficult to distinguish from the next sense). a Represented as evil or maleficent: μάχης ἐπὶ μήδεα κείρει δ. ἡμετέρης Il. 15.468. Cf. Il. 9.600, Il. 11.480, Il. 15.418, Il. 21.93: στυγερός οἱ ἔχραε δ. Od. 5.396. Cf. Od. 4.275, Od. 5.421, Od. 6.172 (cf. θεοί 174), Od. 7.248, Od. 10.64, Od. 11.587, Od. 12.169, 295, Od. 14.488, Od. 16.194, 370 (evil to the speaker), Od. 17.446, Od. 19.201, Od. 24.149. b As beneficent: ἄλλα δ. ὑποθήσεται Od. 3.27. Cf. Od. 9.381, Od. 17.243 = Od. 21.201 (cf. θεός τις Od. 21.196), Od. 19.10, 138. c With neither notion prominent Od. 14.386. 2 In generalized sense, superhuman power, heaven, fate, the gods (sometimes difficult to distinguish from the δαιμόνιος. sense): σὺν δαίμονι (if heaven so wills it) Il. 11.792, Il. 15.403, πρὸς δαίμονα φωτὶ μάχεσθαι (against the will of the gods) Il. 17.98. Cf. Il. 7.291, 377 = 396, Il. 17.104: δαίμονος αἶσα Od. 11.61. Cf. Od. 2.134, Od. 16.64, Od. 18.146, 256 = Od. 19.129, Od. 19.512, Od. 20.87, Od. 24.306.–δαίμονά τοι δώσω (I will deal thee fate, i.e. death) Il. 8.166. 3 With more marked notion of personality: ἐπέσσυτο δαίμονι ἶσος Il. 5.438 = Il. 16.705 = 786 = Il. 20.447. Cf. Il. 5.459 = 884, Il. 20.493, Il. 21.18, 227. 4 a In pl. = θεοί in gen.: βεβήκει μετὰ δαίμονας ἄλλους Il. 1.222. Cf. Il. 6.115, Il. 23.595. b In sing., of a particular god: οὐδʼ ἐπιορκήσω πρὸς δαίμονος (i.e. the god, or, as in the sequel, the gods, by whom he was to swear) Il. 19.188: λίσσομʼ ὑπὲρ θυέων καὶ δαίμονος (i.e. whatever god the sacrifice was being made to) Od. 15.261. More definitely: γίγνωσκον ὃ δὴ κακὰ μήδετο δ. Od. 3.166 (the context app. showing that the reference is exclusively to Zeus). c Of a definite goddess present in her own person: ἦρχε δ. (i.e. Aphrodite) Il. 3.420.

data.quote: μάχης ἐπὶ μήδεα κείρει δ. ἡμετέρης
γίγνωσκον ὃ δὴ κακὰ μήδετο δ.

definition: δαίνυμι [δαίω2.] Fut. infin. δαίσειν Il. 19.299. 2 sing. subj. mid. δαινύῃ Od. 8.243. δαινύ̆ῃ Od. 19.328. 3 sing. opt. δαινῦτο Il. 24.665. 3 pl. δαινύατο Od. 18.248. 2 sing. impf. δαίνυο Il. 24.63. Nom. pl. masc. aor. pple. δαισάμενοι Od. 7.188, Od. 18.408. (μετα-.) 1 a To give (a meal): δαίνυ δαῖτα γέρουσιν Il. 9.70. b To give (a wedding-feast): δαινύντα γάμον Od. 4.3. Sim. δαίσειν γάμον (app., to bring it about) Il. 19.299. c To give (a funeral-feast) Il. 23.29: Od. 3.309. 2 In mid. α To take a meal (often with the notion of faring well or revelling): εἴ τις δαίνυται εὔφρων Il. 15.99. Cf. Il. 1.468 = 602 = Il. 2.431 = Il. 7.320 = Il. 23.56, Il. 4.386, Il. 5.805, Il. 7.477, Il. 9.228: δαινύμενοι τερπώμεθα Od. 1.369. Cf. Od. 1.228, Od. 2.247, 311, Od. 3.471, Od. 7.188, 203, Od. 8.243, Od. 10.9, 61, 452, Od. 12.398, Od. 14.195, 250, Od. 15.398, Od. 16.479 = Od. 19.425, Od. 17.332, Od. 18.248, 408, Od. 19.328, Od. 21.89, 290, 319. β Of a wedding-feast Il. 24.63: Od. 4.15, 238. γ Of a funeral-feast Il. 24.665. δ With cognate acc. As (α): εἰλαπίνην δαίνυντο Il. 23.201. Cf. Od. 3.66 = Od. 20.280, Od. 7.50, Od. 11.186, Od. 13.26. As (γ) Il. 24.802. b To partake of: ἑκατόμβας Il. 9.535 (i.e. of the god's share thereof): κρέα τε καὶ μέθυ Od. 9.162 = 557 = Od. 10.184 = Od. 10.468 = Od. 10.477= Od. 12.30.

δαίς1 δαιτός, ἡ [δαίω2.] 1 A meal (often with the notion of faring well or revelling): δαίνυ δαῖτα Il. 9.70, δαῖτα πένοντο Il. 18.558 (app. a meal for the King and his retainers, that for the ἔριθοι being mentioned below), πειθώμεθα δαιτί (i.e. to hunger) Il. 23.48. Cf. Il. 1.467, 468, 575, 579, Il. 4.259, 343, etc.: ὄφρʼ ἂν δαῖτα πτωχεύῃ (i.e. beg his bread) Od. 17.11, δαιτῶν ἀπολυμαντῆρα 220. Cf. Od. 1.152, 374, Od. 2.322, Od. 3.33, Od. 7.232, Od. 10.124, etc. Of the god's share of a sacrifice: Ζεὺς ἔβη κατὰ δαῖτα Il. 1.424. Cf. Il. 4.48 = Il. 24.69: τέρπετο δαιτὶ παρήμενος Od. 1.26 (of Poseidon). Cf. Od. 3.336, 420, Od. 8.76. Of what a beast devours Il. 24.43. 2 A wedding-feast Od. 18.279. 3 A funeral-feast Il. 24.802.
δάϊς ἡ. Dat. δαΐ (for δαϊ-ι). War, battle: ἐν δαΐ λυγρῇ (λευγαλέῃ) Il. 13.286, Il. 14.387, Il. 24.739.
δαίσειν fut. infin. δαίνυμι.
δαίτη -ης, ἡ = δαίς1 Il. 10.217: Od. 7.50. Of a god's share of a sacrifice Od. 3.44.
δαίτηθεν [δαίτη + -θεν 1.] From, leaving, a meal: δαίτηθεν ἰόντα Od. 10.216.
δαιτρεύω [δαιτρός.] 1 To carve meat Od. 14.433, Od. 15.323. 2 To make an apportionment of spoil Il. 11.688, 705.
δαιτρόν τό [δαίω2.] One's portion Il. 4.262.
δαιτρός ὁ [δαίω2.] One who carves meat, a carver Od. 1.141 = Od. 4.57, Od. 17.331.
δαιτροσύνη -ης, ἡ [δαιτρός.] The art of carving meat. In pl.: θεράποντε δαήμονε δαιτροσυνάων Od. 16.253.

δαιτυμών -όνος, ὁ [δαιτύς.] Dat. δαιτυμόνεσσι Od. 7.102, Od. 22.12. A guest at or partaker of a meal or feast Od. 4.621, Od. 7.102, 148, Od. 8.66 = 473, Od. 9.7, Od. 15.467, Od. 17.605, Od. 22.12 (in the last two passages of the self-invited guests, the suitors).

data.ref: Od. 22.12 (in the last two passages of the self-invited guests, the suitors).

definition: δαιτύς -ύος, ἡ = δαίς 1 Il. 22.496.

δαΐφρων -ονος [δάω + φρήν.] Skilled, whether in war or in the arts of peace. Epithet of heroes, etc. Il. 2.23, Il. 4.252, Il. 6.162, Il. 9.651, Il. 11.123, Il. 14.459, etc.: Od. 1.48, Od. 4.687, Od. 6.256, Od. 8.8, Od. 15.519, Od. 21.16, etc. Absol. in voc. Il. 5.277. Applied to Anticleia Od. 15.356.

δαίω1 [δαϝ-, δηϝ-, δαυ-.] 3 sing. pf. (in pres. sense) δέδηε Il. 13.736, Il. 17.253, Il. 20.18: Od. 20.353. 3 sing. plupf. (in impf. sense) δεδήει Il. 2.93, Il. 12.35, 466. 3 sing. aor. subj. pass. δάηται Il. 20.316, Il. 21.375. (ἀμφι-.) 1 To set on fire, kindle: ξύλα Il. 18.347: Od. 8.436. To light (a fire) Il. 9.211: Od. 7.7. To cause (fire) to appear or blaze Il. 5.4, 7, Il. 18.206, 227. 2 In pf. and plupf. and in pass., to burn or blaze: πῦρ δαιετο Il. 21.343. Cf. Il. 8.75, Il. 18.227 Il. 20.316 = Il. 21.375: Od. 5.61. Of the eyes, to blaze Il. 12.466. So of a lion's eyes Od. 6.132. Fig.: Ὄσσα δεδήει (spread like wild-fire) Il. 2.93, νῦν ἄγχιστα μάχη δέδηε (app., now most nearly blazes up, i.e. is on the point of blazing up) Il. 20.18. Cf. Il. 12.35, Il. 13.736, Il. 17.253: οἰμωγὴ δέδηε (is bursting forth) Od. 20.353.

δαίω2 [cf. δαΐζω, δατέομαι.] 3 pl. pf. pass. δεδαίαται Od. 1.23. To divide or apportion. 1 In mid.: κρέα δαίετο Od. 15.140. Cf. Od. 17.332. 2 In pass.: Αἰθίοπας, τοὶ διχθὰ δεδαίαται (are divided) Od. 1.23, μήλων δαιομένων (in the division of the . . .) Od. 9.551. Fig., to be troubled or distressed: δαίεταί μοι ἦτορ Od. 1.48.
†δάκνω 3 sing. aor. δάκε Il. 5.493. Infin. δακέειν Il. 17.572, Il. 18.585. To bite. Of dogs Il. 18.585. Of a fly Il. 17.572. Fig.: δάκε φρένας μῦθος Il. 5.493 (cf. θυμοδακής).

δάκρυ τό [cf. δάκρυον.] 1 A tear: δεύοντο δάκρυσι κόλποι Il. 9.570. Cf. Il. 23.16, Il. 24.162: Od. 7.260, Od. 17.103 = Od. 19.596.–(κατὰ) δ. χέειν, to shed a tear, to weepIl. 1.357, 413, Il. 3.142, Il. 6.405, Il. 9.14, etc.: Od. 2.24, Od. 4.556, Od. 11.5, Od. 12.12, Od. 14.280, etc. Sim. in various expressions: βαλέειν ἀπὸ δ. παρειῶν Od. 4.198. Cf. Od. 4.114, 223, Od. 17.490.– ἔκπεσέ οἱ δ. Il. 2.266: Od. 16.16.– κατείβετο δ. Il. 24.794: τί δ. κατείβετον; Od. 21.86.–δ. ἀπομόρξασθαι, to wipe away one's tears Il. 2.269: Od. 17.304.– δ. ἔδευε παρειάς (his tears) Od. 8.522. 2 As the visible feature of weeping; hence, in pl., tears, weeping: δάκρυσι θυμὸν ἐρέχθων Od. 5.83 = 157.

δακρυόεις -εντος. Fem. -εσσα. [δάκρυον.] 1 Shedding tears, weeping Il. 6.455, Il. 16.10, Il. 18.66, Il. 21.493, 496, 506, Il. 22.499: Od. 10.415. In neut. δακρυόεν as adv.: γελάσας (smiling through her tears) Il. 6.484. 2 Accompanied by tears: γόοιο Od. 4.801, Od. 17.8, Od. 24.323. 3 Causing tears, bringing misery: πόλεμον Il. 5.737 = Il. 8.388, Il. 17.512. Cf. Il. 11.601, Il. 13.765, Il. 16.436.

δάκρυον τό [cf. δάκρυ.] Dat. pl. δᾶκρύοισι Od. 18.173. Instrumental δακρυόφι Il. 17.696, Il. 23.397: Od. 4.705, Od. 10.248, Od. 19.472, Od. 20.349. This form as ablative Od. 5.152. 1 A tear: ὄσσε δακρυόφι πλῆσθεν (with tears) Il. 17.696 = Il. 23.397: = Od. 4.705 = Od. 19.472, οὐδέ ποτʼ ὄσσε δακρυόφιν τέρσοντο (were free of tears) Od. 5.152, δάκρυα κεῦθεν Od. 19.212. Cf. Od. 10.248 = Od. 20.349, Od. 18.173.–δάκρυα χέειν, to shed tears, to weepIl. 7.426, Il. 16.3, Il. 18.17, 235: Od. 24.46.– χύτο δάκρυα Il. 23.385: δάκρυα χέοντο Od. 4.523. Sim. in varous expressions: δάκρυʼ ἀναπρήσας Il. 9.433: Od. 2.81.–(κατὰ) δάκρυον εἴβειν, to shed a tear, to weepIl. 16.11, Il. 19.323', Il. 24.9: Od. 4.153, Od. 8.531, Od. 11.391, Od. 16.219, 332, Od. 24.234, 280.– δάκρυα λείβειν Il. 13.88, 658, Il. 18.32: Od. 5.84 = 158, Od. 8.86, 93 = 532, Od. 16.214.– δάκρυʼ ἔκβαλεν Od. 19.362.– δάκρυον ἧκεν Od. 16.191, Od. 23.33.– δάκρυα πίπτει Od. 14.129.– δάκρυα ῥέεν Il. 17.437: Od. 19.204.– δάκρυʼ ὀμόργνυσθαι (ὀμόρξασθαι) Il. 18.124: Od. 8.88, Od. 11.527, 530. 2 As the visible feature of weeping: τείσειαν Δαναοὶ ἐμὰ δάκρυα (my weeping, i.e. the cause thereof, my wrongs) Il. 1.42.
δακρυπλώω (ᾱ) [δάκρυ + πλώω in sense to flow. Cf. L. pluo.] To flow with tears, be maudlin Od. 19.122.

δακρύω [δάκρυον.] 2 sing. pf. pass. δεδάκρυσαι Il. 16.7. 3 pl. δεδάκρυνται Il. 22.491: Od. 20.204, 353. 1 To shed tears, weep: δακρύσας ἕζετο (with a burst of tears) Il. 1.349. Cf. Il. 10.377. Il. 19.229: δάκρυσα ἰδών Od. 11.55 = 395, 87. Cf. Od. 1.336, Od. 17.33, 38, Od. 21.82, Od. 23.207. 2 In pf. pass., to be in tears: τίπτε δεδάκρυσαι; Il. 16.7. To be covered or filled with tears: δεδάκρυνται παρειαί Il. 22.491. Cf. Od. 20.204, 353.
δαλός -οῦ, ὁ. 1 A piece of ignited material for communicating fire, a fire-brand Il. 13.320, Il. 15.421: Od. 5.488. 2 A brand snatched from the fire or from a brazier Od. 19.69.

†δαμάζω 3 sing. fut. δαμάᾳ Il. 22.271. δαμᾷ Il. 1.61. 3 pl. δαμόωσι Il. 6.368. Aor. ἐδάμασσα Il. 5.191. 2 sing. δάμασσας Il. 21.90. 3 sing. ἐδάμασσε Il. 6.159, Il. 13.434, Il. 14.316, etc.: Od. 11.171, Od. 22.246, Od. 24.109, etc. δάμασε Il. 16.543, Il. 22.446: Od. 23.310. δάμασσε Il. 5.106, Il. 9.118, Il. 11.98, etc. 3 pl. δάμασσαν Il. 16.845: Od. 14.367. Subj. δαμάσσω Il. 16.438. 3 sing. δαμάσῃ Od. 5.468, Od. 19.488, 496, Od. 21.213. δαμάσσῃ Il. 5.138: Od. 17.24, Od. 18.57. 1 pl. δαμάσσομεν Il. 22.176. Imp. δάμασον Il. 9.496: Od. 11.562. δάμασσον Il. 3.352. Pple. δαμάσσας Od. 4.244. Nom. pl. δαμάσαντες Il. 18.113, Il. 19.66: Od. 9.59. Mid. 3 sing. aor. (ἐ)δαμάσσατο Il. 5.278: Od. 9.516. 3 pl. δαμάσαντο Il. 10.210, 411. 3 sing. subj. δαμάσσεται Il. 11.478, Il. 21.226. Opt. δαμασαίμην Od. 4.637. 1 pl. δαμασαίμεθα Il. 16.561. 3 pl. δαμασαίατο Od. 16.105. Pple. δαμασσάμενος, -ου Il. 15.476: Od. 9.454. Infin. δαμάσασθαι Il. 22.379, Il. 23.655. Pass. Aor. ἐδαμάσθην Od. 8.231. 3 sing. δαμασθείς Il. 19.9. Pple. δαμασθείς Il. 16.816, Il. 22.55. Aor. pass. δάμην Il. 20.94 [ἦ κʼ ἐδάμην Allen]. 3 sing. (ἐ)δάμη Il. 2.860, 874, Il. 9.545, Il. 21.383: Od. 1.237, Od. 3.90, Od. 4.499. 1 pl. ἐδάμημεν Il. 13.812. 3 pl. δάμεν Il. 8.344, Il. 12.14, Il. 15.2, Il. 18.103: Od. 4.495. Subj. δαμείω Od. 18.54. 2 sing. δαμήῃς Il. 3.436. 3 sing. δαμήῃ Il. 22.246. 2 pl. δαμήετε Il. 7.72. 3 sing. opt. δαμείη Il. 5.564, Il. 12.403: Od. 4.790, Od. 17.252. 3 pl. δαμεῖεν Il. 3.301. Pple. δαμείς, -έντος Il. 3.429, Il. 5.653, Il. 6.74, Il. 16.420, etc.: Od. 3.410, Od. 6.11, Od. 24.100. Infin. δαμήμεναι Il. 10.403, Il. 17.77, Il. 20.266, 312, Il. 21.291. δαμῆναι Il. 13.98, Il. 15.522, Il. 16.434, Il. 21.578, etc.: Od. 3.269, Od. 3.369, Od. 4.397, Od. 18.156. 3 sing. aor. imp. δμηθήτω Il. 9.158. Acc. sing. masc. pple. δμηθέντα Il. 4.99, Il. 5.646. 1 pl. pf. δεδμήμεσθα Il. 5.878. Plupf. δεδμήμην Od. 11.622. 3 sing. δέδμητο Od. 3.305, Od. 5.454. 3 pl. δεδμήατο Il. 3.183. Pple. δεδμημένος, -ου Il. 10.2, Il. 14.482, Il. 24.678: Od. 7.318, Od. 13.119, Od. 14.318, Od. 15.6, Od. 18.237. 1 To break in, tame. In mid.: ἡμίονον, ἥ τʼ ἀλγίστη δαμάσασθαι Il. 23.655. Cf. Od. 4.637. To control (horses) Il. 10.403 = Il. 17.77. Fig.: Διὸς μάστιγι δαμέντες Il. 12.37. Cf. Il. 13.812. 2 To bring into subjection: σοὶ δεδμήμεσθα Il. 5.878. Cf. Od. 11.622. Of political subjection Il. 3.183, Il. 6.159: Od. 3.305. To subject (to a man) in marriage: ἀνδρί με δάμασσεν Il. 18.432. To subject (a woman to the discretion of a victor): ἄλοχοι δʼ ἄλλοισι δαμεῖεν Il. 3.301. 3 Of feelings, sleep, etc., to overcome: ἔρος μʼ ἐδάμασσεν Il. 14.316. Cf. Il. 10.2 = Il. 24.678, Il. 14.353: δεδμημένος ὕπνῳ Od. 7.318. Cf. Od. 13.119, Od. 15.6. Of natural agencies, to have an overpowering effect upon, wear out, exhaust: ἁλὶ δέδμητο Od. 5.454. Cf. Od. 8.231, Od. 14.318. 4 To curb or restrain (one's spirit): δάμασον θυμὸν μέγαν Il. 9.496. Cf. Il. 18.113 = Il. 19.66: Od. 11.562. In pass., to be appeased or placated: δμηθήτω Il. 9.158. 5 To overpower, get the better of, master: ἐπεὶ ξάνθοιο δάμη μένος Il. 21.383. Cf. Il. 16.816: Od. 4.397. In mid.: δαμασσάμενος οἴνῳ Od. 9.454. Cf. Od. 9.516. To defeat, rout, put to flight: κλῖναν δαμάσαντες Ἀχαιούς Od. 9.59. Cf. Il. 6.74 = Il. 17.320, Il. 10.310 = 397, Il. 13.98, Il. 16.420, Il. 17.337, Il. 20.143: Od. 23.310. In mid. Il. 10.210 = 411, Il. 15.476. 6 To put an end to, destroy, kill, slay: εἰ πόλεμος δαμᾷ Ἀχαιούς Il. 1.61, μὴ ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ δουρὶ δαμήῃς (by him with his spear) Il. 3.436, σοὶ δαμῆναι (by thee) Il. 13.603. Cf. Il. 2.860, Il. 4.479, Il. 5.106, Il. 11.98, Il. 14.482, Il. 19.203, etc.: μοῖρʼ ἐπέδησε δαμῆναι Od. 3.269 (app. referring to Aegisthus as fate-bound to (ultimate) ruin; or perh. to Clytaemnestra as yielding to passion (sense (3))), μή με στίβη δαμάσῃ Od. 5.468. Cf. Od. 1.237, Od. 3.90, 410, Od. 4.495, Od. 11.171, Od. 18.54, etc. In mid. Il. 5.278, Il. 11.478, Il. 16.561, Il. 21.226, Il. 22.379: Od. 16.105. Of a shield, in pass., to be unable to resist a blow, be pierced Il. 20.266. To do violence to, disfigure (oneself): αὐτόν μιν πληγῇσι δαμάσσας Od. 4.244. 7 To subject to a foe, cause to be defeated Il. 9.118. 8 To cause to be slain by a foe: ἐμῇς ὑπὸ χερσὶ δάμασσον [Ἀλέξανδρον] Il. 3.352. Cf. Il. 6.368, Il. 13.434, Il. 16.543, 845, Il. 18.119, Il. 22.446, etc.: τούσδε μοῖρʼ ἐδάμασσεν Od. 22.413. Cf. Od. 14.367, Od. 18.57, Od. 19.488 = Od. 21.213, Od. 19.496.
δάμαρ -αρτος, ἡ [δαμ-, δαμάζω.] A wife Il. 3.122, Il. 14.503: Od. 4.126, Od. 20.290, Od. 24.125.
δάμασε δάμασσε 3 sing. aor. δαμάζω.
δάμη 3 sing. aor. pass. δαμάζω.

δάμνημι [cf. δαμάζω.] From δαμνάω 3 sing. δαμνᾷ Od. 11.221. 3 sing. impf. (ἐ)δάμνα Il. 5.391, Il. 14.439, Il. 16.103, Il. 21.52, 270. 2 sing. pres. mid. δαμνᾷ Il. 14.199. (ὑπο-.) 1 To control, keep in order: Ἥρην ἐπέεσσιν Il. 5.893. 2 To overcome by troubling the senses. In mid.: φιλότητα καὶ ἵμερον, ᾧ τε σὺ πάντας δαμνᾷ Il. 14.199. 3 To have an overpowering effect upon, wear out, exhaust: δεσμός ἑ ἐδάμνα Il. 5.391. Cf. Il. 14.439, Il. 21.52, 270. In mid. Od. 14.488. 4 To overpower, master Il. 16.103. 5 To defeat, rout, put to flight: Ἀχαιοὺς Τρωσὶν δαμναμένους (by the Trojans) Il. 13.16 = 353. Cf. Il. 5.746 = Il. 8.390: = Od. 1.100. 6 To kill, slay: Τρώεσσιν δάμνασθαι (by the Trojans) Il. 8.244 = Il. 15.376. Cf. Il. 11.309. To destroy, consume: σάρκας πυρὸς μένος δαμνᾷ Od. 11.221. To pierce, rend (a shield) Il. 21.401.

data.quote: φιλότητα καὶ ἵμερον, ᾧ τε σὺ πάντας δαμνᾷ

definition: δαμόωσι 3 pl. fut. δαμάζω.
δανός [δαίω1.] Dried, dry: ξύλα Od. 15.322.
δάος τό [cf. δαΐς.] A torch: δ. μετὰ χερσὶν ἔχουσα Od. 23.294. Collectively, torches: δ. μετὰ χερσὶν ἔχουσαι Il. 24.647: = Od. 4.300 = Od. 7.339 = Od. 22.497.

δάπεδον -ου, τό [δα- (app. referring to the work of levelling, stamping, etc.) + πέδον, the ground.] 1 A levelled and prepared surface: ἐν τυκτῷ δαπέδῳ Od. 4.627 = Od. 17.169. 2 A floor of a house Il. 4.2: Od. 10.227, Od. 11.420, Od. 22.188, 309 = Od. 24.185, Od. 22.455. Of the under surface of the realm of Hades Od. 11.577.

δάπτω 3 sing. fut. δάψει Il. 13.831. 2 sing. aor. ἔδαψας Il. 21.398. 3 sing. ἔδαψε Il. 5.858. (κατα-.) 1 To devour. Of wild beasts Il. 11.481, Il. 16.159. Fig. of fire Il. 23.183. 2 Of rending flesh Il. 5.831, Il. 13.831, Il. 21.398.
δαρδάπτω [lengthened fr. δάπτω.] To devour. Of wild beasts Il. 11.479. Fig.: κτήματα δαρδάπτουσιν Od. 14.92 = Od. 16.315.
†δαρθάνω 3 sing. aor. ἔδραθε. (κατα-, παρα-) To sleep, go to sleep, take one's rest Od. 20.143.
δάσασθαι aor. infin. δατέομαι.
δασάσκετο 3 sing. pa. iterative δατέομαι.
δάσκιος -ον [δα- + σκιή.] Thickly shaded, with thick shades: ὕλη Il. 15.273: ὕλην Od. 5.470.
δασμός ὁ [δασ-, δατέομαι.] A division or apportionment: ἤν ποτε δασμὸς ἵκηται Il. 1.166.
δάσονται 3 pl. fut. δατέομαι.
δασπλῆτις [prob. fr. δασ- (= δεσ-, house, as in δέσποινα) + πλη-, πελάζω. Cf. τειχεσιπλήτης.] Thus, that approaches houses (with hostile intent), smiter of houses: Ἐρινύς Od. 15.234.
δάσσαντο 3 pl. aor. δατέομαι.
δασύμαλλος [δασύς + μαλλός, a lock of wool.] With thick fleece: ἄρσενες ὄϊες Od. 9.425.
δασύς -εῖα, -ύ. Thick with hair, hairy Od. 14.51. App., spread so as to lie thickly: ῥῶπας Od. 14.49.

δατέομαι [δα-, δαίω2.] 3 sing. impf. δατεῦντο Il. 23.121: Od. 1.112. 3 sing. pa. iterative δασάσκετο Il. 9.333. 3 pl. fut. δάσονται Il. 22.354: Od. 2.368. 3 sing. aor. ἐδάσσατο Od. 6.10. 1 pl. δασσάμεθα Od. 9.42, 549. 3 pl. ἐδάσαντο Od. 14.208. δάσσαντο Il. 1.368: Od. 19.423. 3 pl. subj. δάσωνται Od. 17.80. 1 pl. opt. δασαίμεθα Od. 2.335. Pl. pple. δασσάμενοι Od. 3.66, 316, Od. 15.13, Od. 16.385, Od. 20.280. Infin. δάσασθαι Il. 18.511, Il. 22.120, Il. 23.21: Od. 18.87, Od. 22.476. δάσσασθαι Od. 20.216. 3 sing. pf. pass. δέδασται Il. 1.125, Il. 15.189: Od. 15.412. (ἀπο-.) 1 To divide among themselves, make mutual apportionment of: χηρωσταὶ διὰ κτῆσιν δατέοντο Il. 5.158. Cf. Il. 1.368, Il. 9.138 = 280: τάδε δʼ αὐτοὶ δάσονται Od. 2.368. Cf. Od. 2.335, Od. 3.316 = Od. 15.13, Od. 9.42, 549, Od. 14.208, Od. 16.385, Od. 17.80, Od. 20.216. Fig.: μένος Ἄρηος δατέονται (app., share between them, are alike filled with) Il. 18.264. 2 To divide, apportion: διὰ παῦρα δασάσκετο Il. 9.333. Cf. Il. 1.125, Il. 15.189, Il. 18.511, Il. 22.120: Od. 3.66 = Od. 20.280, Od. 6.10, Od. 15.412, Od. 19.423. To divide into portions: κρέα Od. 1.112. 3 To divide among themselves as prey, to tear (and devour). Of dogs, etc. Il. 22.354, Il. 23.21: Od. 18.87, Od. 22.476. 4 To cut in pieces Il. 20.394–To cut up (the ground) Il. 23.121.
δάφνη -ης, ἡ. The laurel Od. 9.183.
δαφοινεός [= δαφοινός.] Red (with blood) Il. 18.538.
δαφοινός [δα- + φοινός.] Red or tawny: δράκων Il. 2.308, δέρμα λέοντος Il. 10.23, θῶες Il. 11.474.
δάψει 3 sing. fut. δάπτω.

*†δάω 2 sing. fut. in mid. form δαήσεαι Od. 3.187, Od. 19.325. Aor. ἐδάην Il. 3.208: Od. 4.267. Subj. δαείω Il. 10.425, Il. 16.423, Il. 21.61: Od. 9.280. 1 pl. δαῶμεν Il. 2.299. Infin. δαήμεναι Il. 6.150, Il. 20.213, Il. 21.487: Od. 13.335, Od. 23.262. δαῆναι Od. 4.493. 2 sing. pf. δεδάηκας Od. 8.146, 3 δεδάηκε Od. 8.134. Pple. δεδαώς Od. 17.519. Pl. δεδαηκότες Od. 2.61. 3 sing. redup. aor. δέδαε Od. 6.233, Od. 8.448, Od. 20.72, Od. 23.160. From this tense is formed infin. mid. δεδάασθαι (for δεδαέσθαι) Od. 16.316. (προ-.) 1 To get to know, know, learn: ἀμφοτέρων φυήν Il. 3.208, πολέμοιο δαήμεναι (about war) Il. 21.487. Cf. Il. 6.150 = Il. 20.213: Od. 3.187, Od. 4.267, 493. With dependent clause: ἢ . . . ἦε . . . Il. 2.299. Cf. Il. 16.423, Il. 21.61: πῶς ἐμεῦ δαήσεαι εἰ . . . ; (about me) Od. 19.325. Absol.: ὄφρα δαείω Il. 10.425: Od. 9.280. Cf. Od. 13.335, Od. 23.262. 2 To acquire practical knowledge of or skill in. In pf., to have such knowledge of or skill in: εἴ τινʼ ἄεθλον δεδάηκεν Od. 8.134. Cf. Od. 2.61, Od. 8.146, Od. 17.519. 3 In redup. aor., to teach (something): ἔργα δʼ Ἀθηναίη δέδαεν Od. 20.72. With double acc. of person and thing: ὃν Ἥφαιστος δέδαεν τέχνην παντοίην Od. 6.233 = Od. 23.160. Cf. Od. 8.448. In mid., to have oneself taught; hence, to get to know, acquire knowledge of: γυναῖκας δεδάασθαι, αἵ τε . . . καὶ αἳ . . . Od. 16.316.

data.quote: γυναῖκας δεδάασθαι, αἵ τε . . . καὶ αἳ . . .

definition: δέ 1 Adversative particle, but, yet, on the other hand, while Il. 1.29, 83, 108, 137, 167, etc.: Od. 1.13, 19, 33, 75, 212, etc. 2 Particle of continuation, often introducing a subordinate statement or a parenthesis: πολλὰς δὲ ψυχὰς Ἄϊδι προΐαψεν Il. 1.3, νοῦσον ὦρσεν, ὀλέκοντο δὲ λαοί 10, μύδωνα βάλεν–ὁ δʼ ὑπέστρεφε ἵππους–χερμαδίῳ Il. 5.581. Cf. Il. 1.19, 25, 33, 34, 35, etc.: Od. 1.3, 51, 53, 71, 93, etc. 3 Giving a reason or explanation, for: πίθεσθʼ. ἄμφω δὲ νεωτέρω ἐστὸν ἐμεῖο Il. 1.259, ἐμέθεν ξύνες. Διὸς δέ τοι ἄγγελός εἰμι Il. 2.26, μή τι ῥέξῃ κακόν. θυμὸς δὲ μέγας ἐστὶ βασιλήων 196. Cf. Il. 1.271, Il. 3.410, Il. 4.438, 478, Il. 7.259, etc.: Od. 1.168, 433, Od. 2.36, 41, Od. 3.48, etc. 4 Introducing a principal clause after a relative, temporal or conditional protasis: οἱ δʼ ἐπεὶ οὖν ἤγερθεν . . . τοῖσι δὲ μετέφη Il. 1.58, εἰ δέ κε μὴ δώωσιν, ἐγὼ δέ κεν αὐτὸς ἕλωμαι 137, ὅν τινα βασιλῆα κιχείη, τὸν ἀγανοῖς ἐπέεσσιν ἐρητύσασκεν Il. 2.189. Cf. Il. 2.322, Il. 4.262, Il. 5.261, 439, Il. 7.314, Il. 9.167, etc.: Od. 5.425, Od. 7.109, Od. 8.25, Od. 10.366, Od. 11.148, Od. 16.274, etc. Introducing without antecedent clause Il. 2.802, Il. 3.229, etc.: Od. 4.400, Od. 5.428, Il. 3.229, etc.: Od. 4.400, Od. 5.428, etc. 5 Introducing a question: τίς δὲ σύ ἐσσι; Il. 6.123, τίς δʼ οἶδʼ εἰ . . . ; Il. 15.403. Cf. Il. 6.55, Il. 10.82, Il. 11.792, Il. 14.264, Il. 15.244, etc.: Od. 2.332, 363, Od. 4.312, 681, Od. 6.276, etc. 6 Before an imp. or a subj. as imp.: σὺ δὲ παῦε τεὸν μένος Il. 1.282. Cf. Il. 2.344, etc.: τῶν δὲ βοῶν ἀπεχώμεθα Od. 12.321. Cf. Od. 3.247, Od. 5.346, Od. 16.130, Od. 22.312, etc.

data.quote: πίθεσθʼ. ἄμφω δὲ νεωτέρω ἐστὸν ἐμεῖο
ἐμέθεν ξύνες. Διὸς δέ τοι ἄγγελός εἰμι
οἱ δʼ ἐπεὶ οὖν ἤγερθεν . . . τοῖσι δὲ μετέφη
ὅν τινα βασιλῆα κιχείη, τὸν ἀγανοῖς ἐπέεσσιν ἐρητύσασκεν

definition: δέατο 3 sing. sing. impf. To seem, appear Od. 6.242.
δέγμενος pf. pple. δέχομαι.
δεδάασθαι redup. aor. infin. mid. δάω.
δέδαε 3 sing. redup. aor. δάω.
δεδάηκε 3 sing. pf. δάω.
δεδαίαται 3 pl. pf. pass. δαίω2.
δεδαϊγμένος pf. pple. pass. δαΐζω.
δεδάκρυνται 3 pl. pf. pass. δακρύω.
δέδασται 3 sing. pf. pass. δατέομαι.
δεδαώς pf. pple. δάω.
δεδεγμένος pf. pple. δέχομαι.
δεδειπνήκει 3 sing. plupf. δειπνέω.
δέδεξο pf. imp. δέχομαι.
δεδέξομαι fut. pf. δέχομαι.
δέδετο 3 sing. plupf. pass. δέω.
δέδηε 3 sing. pf. δαίω1.
δεδίασι 3 pl. pf. See δείδοικα.
δεδιδάχθαι pf. infin. pass. διδάσκω.
δεδίσκομαι = δειδίσκομαι 1 Od. 15.150.
δεδμημένος1, pf. pple. pass. δαμάζω.
δεδμημένος2, pf. pple. pass. δέμω.
δεδμήμεσθα 1 pl. pf. pass. δαμάζω.
δεδμήμην, δέδμητο1,δεδμήατο 1 and 3 sing. and 3 pl. plupf. pass. δαμάζω.
δέδμητο2, 3 sing. plupf. pass δέμω.
δεδοκημένος pf. pple. δέχομαι.
δέδορκε 3 sing. pf. δέρκομαι.
δέδοται 3 sing. pf. pass. δίδωμι.
δεδουπότος genit. sing. masc. pf. pple. δουπέω.
δεδραγμένος pf. pple. δράσσομαι.
δέδυκε 3 sing. pf. δύω.
δέελος [app. for δήελος = δῆλος.] Thus, conspicuous, easy to be distinguished: σῆμα Il. 10.466.
δεῖ [prob. fr. δέω.] It is binding on (one), behoves (one). With acc. and infin.: τί δεῖ πολεμιζέμεναι Τρώεσσιν Ἀργείους; Il. 9.337.
δείδεκτο 3 sing. plupf. mid. δείκνυμι.
δειδέχαται 3 pl. pf. mid. δείκνυμι.
δειδήμων -ονος [δείδοικα.] Fearful, timid Il. 3.56.
δείδια pf. See δείδοικα.
δείδιε1, 3 sing. pf. See δείδοικα.
δείδιε2, 3 sing. plupf. See δείδοικα.
δείδιθι pf. imp. See δείδοικα.
δείδιμεν 1 pl. pf. See δείδοικα.
δειδίμεν pf. infin. See δείδοικα.
δειδίξεσθαι fut. infin. δειδίσσομαι.
δείδισαν 3 pl. plupf. See δείδοικα.
δειδίσκομαι [app. redup. fr. δικ-, δείκνυμι. Cf. δεικανάομαι.] 1 To pledge in drinking = δείκνυμι 5: δέπαϊ Od. 18.121. 2 To welcome, greet Od. 3.41, Od. 20.197.

δειδίσσομαι [redup. fr. δικ-, δείδοικα.] Fut. infin. δειδίξεσθαι Il. 20.201, 432. Aor. infin. δειδίξασθαι Il. 18.164. 1 To frighten, alarm, scare Il. 4.184, Il. 12.52, Il. 13.810 (try to . . .), Il. 20.201 = 432. To scare (away from something): Ἕκτορʼ ἀπὸ νεκροῦ Il. 18.164. 2 To use threats to, threaten Il. 2.190, Il. 15.196.

†δείδοικα (δέδϝοικα). pf. with pres. sense. 1 sing. δείδοικα Il. 1.555, Il. 9.244, Il. 10.538, Il. 18.261, Il. 24.435: Od. 8.230, Od. 24.353. 2 sing. -ας Il. 12.244. 3 sing. -ε Il. 21.198. Also 1 sing. δείδια (δέδϝια) Il. 13.49, 481, Il. 21.536: Od. 4.820, Od. 6.168, Od. 17.188. 2 sing. -ας Od. 18.80. 3 sing. -ε Od. 16.306. 1 pl. δείδιμεν Il. 7.196, Il. 9.230: Od. 2.199. 3 pl. δεδίασι Il. 24.663. 3 sing. plupf. (with impf. sense) δείδιε (with secondary person-ending) Il. 18.34, Il. 24.358. 1 pl. ἐδείδιμεν Il. 6.99. 3 pl. (ἐ)δείδισαν Il. 5.790, Il. 7.151, Il. 15.652. Imp. δείδιθι Il. 5.827, Il. 14.342: Od. 4.825, Od. 18.63. Pl. δείδιτε Il. 20.366. Pple. δειδιώς, -ότος Il. 3.242, Il. 4.431, Il. 6.137, Il. 12.39, Il. 15.628, Il. 20.45, Il. 21.24, Il. 24.384: Od. 14.60, Od. 18.77. Infin. δειδίμεν Od. 9.274, Od. 10.381. Also δείδω (app. for δείδοα (δέδϝοα)) Il. 10.39, Il. 11.470, Il. 13.745, Il. 14.44, Il. 19.24, Il. 20.30, Il. 22.455: Od. 5.300, 419, 473, Od. 12.122. 3 sing. fut. in mid. form δείσεται Il. 20.130. Infin. δείσεσθαι Il. 15.299. 2 sing. aor. ἔδεισας (ἔδϝεισας) Il. 22.19, Il. 24.364. 3 sing. ἔδεισε Il. 1.33, 568, Il. 3.418, Il. 10.240, Il. 20.61, Il. 23.425, Il. 24.571, 689: Od. 10.448. δεῖσε Il. 5.623, Il. 8.138, Il. 13.163. 2 pl. ἐδείσατε Il. 13.624. 3 pl. ἔδεισαν Od. 10.219, Od. 13.184. δεῖσαν Il. 7.93. 3 sing. subj. δείσῃ Il. 24.116. 2 pl. δείσῃητε Il. 24.779. 3 sing. opt. δείσειε Il. 7.456, Il. 24.672. Pple. δείσας, -αντος Il. 3.37, Il. 5.863, Il. 8.136, Il. 21.248, etc.: Od. 4.792, Od. 9.72, Od. 12.203, Od. 18.396, etc. Fem. δείσασα Od. 16.331. (περιδείδια, ὑποδείδια.) 1 To be afraid, feel fear: ἔδεισεν ὁ γέρων Il. 1.33 = Il. 24.571. Cf. Il. 1.568, Il. 5.233, Il. 6.137, Il. 7.151, Il. 9.230, Il. 10.240, etc.: υὴ δείδιθι Od. 4.825. Cf. Od. 4.792, Od. 7.305, Od. 9.236, 396, Od. 10.219, 381, Od. 12.203, 224, Od. 13.184, Od. 14.60, Od. 16.331, Od. 18.77, Od. 21.367, Od. 24.534. 2 With dependent clause. a In reference to the fut. with υή and subj. (or after secondary tenses opt.) : υὴ ἐρυσαίατο νεκρόν Il. 5.298, μὴ τελέσῃ ἔπος Il. 18.44. Cf. Il. 10.39, Il. 11.470, Il. 13.745, Il. 18.34, Il. 19.24, Il. 20.30, 62, Od. 21.536, Il. 22.455: Od. 4.820, Od. 5.419, 473, Od. 8.230, Od. 12.122, Od. 21.286, Od. 24.353. b In reference to the past with μή and indic.: μὴ πάντα νημερτέα εἷπεν Od. 5.300. In virtual reference to the past with μή and subj.: μή σε παρείπῃ (that she may prove to have..., i.e. that she has . . .) Il. 1.555. Cf. Il. 10.538. c With infin., to be afraid to do something, shrink from doing it: ὑποδέχθαι Il. 7.93. Cf. Il. 15.299: Od. 6.168. 3 To be afraid of, fear, be in fear of, dread, to anticipate with fear, shrink from: αἴσχεα Il. 3.242, μήτε σύ γʼ Ἄρηα τό γε δείδιθι Il. 5.827 (τό γε, for that matter), Ζηνὸς μῆνιν Il. 13.624. Cf. Il. 5.790, Il. 6.99, Il. 12.39, Il. 13.49, Il. 18.261, Il. 22.19, etc. : οὔτινα Od. 2.199, ἐμὴν ἐνιπήν Od. 10.448. Cf. Od. 9.72, 257, Od. 10.130, Od. 12.244, Od. 17.577, Od. 18.63, 80, 396. With complementary infin.: οὐ δείσαντες νέμεσιν ἔσεσθαι Od. 22.39. Cf. Il. 18.342 (τό γε as in Il. 5.827 above). In double construction with acc. and μή with subj.: ταῦτα δείδοικα, μή οἱ ἀπειλὰς ἐκτελέσωσι θεοί, ἡμῖν δʼ αἴσιμον εἴη . . . Il. 9.244 (here also with opt. of remoter consequence). Cf. Od. 17.188. 4 To stand in awe of, reverence, hold in awe or due respect: σημάντορας Il. 4.431. Cf. Il. 24.116, 435: Od. 9.274, Od. 14.389, Od. 16.306, Od. 22.39.

data.quote: μήτε σύ γʼ Ἄρηα τό γε δείδιθι
ταῦτα δείδοικα, μή οἱ ἀπειλὰς ἐκτελέσωσι θεοί, ἡμῖν δʼ αἴσιμον εἴη . . .

definition: δείδω See δείδοικα
δειελιάω [δείελος. 'To act as befits the evening'.] Hence, app., to sup: ἔρχεο δειελιήσας Od. 17.599.
δείελος ὁ [cf. δείλη.] 1 The setting sun, the evening: δ. ὀψὲ δύων Il. 21.232. 2 As adj.: δείελον ἦμαρ (evening) Od. 17.606.
†δεικανάομαι [δείκνυμι.] 3 pl. imp. δεικανόωντο. 1 To pledge in drinking = δείκνυμι 5 Il. 15.86. 2 To welcome, greet Od. 18.111, Od. 24.410.

†δείκνυμι Pres. pple. δεικνύς Il. 13.244. Fut. δείξω Od. 6.194, Od. 7.29, Od. 12.25, Od. 13.344, Od. 21.217. 3 sing. aor. ἔδειξε Od. 10.303, Od. 14.323, Od. 19.293, Od. 24.147. δεῖξε Il. 5.870, Il. 7.184, Il. 10.476: Od. 3.174, Od. 5.241. 2 sing. opt. δείξειας Il. 19.332. 3 sing. -ειε Od. 6.144. Imp. δεῖξον Od. 6.178. Infin. δεῖξαι Il. 3.452, Il. 6.170. Mid. Pres. pple. δεικνύμενος Il. 9.196, Il. 23.701: Od. 4.59. 3 pl. pf. (with pres. sense) δειδέχαται Od. 7.72. 3 sing. plupf. (with impf. sense) δείδεκτο Il. 9.224. 3 pl. δειδέχατο Il. 4.4, Il. 9.671, Il. 22.435. (ἐν-,) 1 To manifest, exhibit, display: σῆμα βροτοῖσιν Il. 13.244. Cf. Od. 3.174. 2 To show, bring forward or exhibit to be looked at: αἷμα καταρρέον Il. 5.870. Cf. Il. 6.170, Il. 7.184, Il. 19.332: Od. 14.323 = Od. 19.293, Od. 21.217, Od. 24.147. In mid. Il. 23.701. 3 To show, point out: Ἀλέξανδρον Il. 3.452. Cf. Il. 10.476: πόλιν Od. 6.144. Cf. Od. 6.178, 194, Od. 7.29, Od. 13.344. With dependent clause: ὅθι δένδρεα πεφύκει Od. 5.241. 4 To point out in words, tell, explain Od. 10.303, Od. 12.25. 5 In mid., to pledge in drinking (app. from a custom of pointing to the person whose health was to be drunk): δείδεκτʼ Ἀχιλῆα Il. 9.224. Cf. Il. 4.4, Il. 9.671. 6 In mid., to welcome, greet: τὼ δεικνύενος Il. 9.196. Cf. Il. 22.435: Od. 4.59, Od. 7.72.
δείλη ἡ [cf. δείελος.] Evening Il. 21.111.
δείλομαι [δείλη.] Of the sun, to decline towards evening: δείλετʼ ἠέλιος Od. 7.289.

δειλός -ή [δϝι-, δείδοικα.] 1 Cowardly, craven Il. 1.293, Il. 13.278. 2 Sorry, worthless: δειλαὶ δειλῶν ἐγγύαι (given by worthless fellows) Od. 8.351. 3 a Luckless, wretched, poor (in a tone of compassion or self-pity): δειλοῖσί σφι γόου κατάπαυμα Il. 17.38. Cf. Il. 5.574, Il. 17.670, Il. 19.287, Il. 21.464, Il. 22.31, 76, Il. 23.65, 105, 221, 223, Il. 24.525: ἐμοὶ δειλῷ κακὰ μήδετο Od. 14.243. Cf. Od. 9.65, Od. 11.19, Od. 12.341, Od. 15.408, Od. 20.115. In voc.: ἆ δειλέ Il. 17.201, Il. 24.518: Od. 11.618, Od. 14.361.mdash; ἆ δειλώ Il. 17.443.– ἆ δειλοί Il. 11.816: Od. 10.431, Od. 20.351. Sim.: ὤ μοι ἐγὼ δειλή Il. 18.54. Cf. Il. 22.431: Od. 5.299. b Tinged with hostility or contempt: ἆ δειλέ Il. 11.441, 452, Il. 16.837: Od. 18.389, Od. 21.288.– ἆ δειλώ Od. 21.86.
δεῖμα τό [δϝι-, δείδοικα.] Fear, terror Il. 5.682.
δείματο 3 sing. aor. mid. δέμω.
δεῖμος ὁ [δεῖμα.] Fear personified Il. 4.440, Il. 11.37, Il. 15.119.

δεινός -ή, -όν [δϝι-, δείδοικα.] 1 Causing, or such as to cause, fear, fearful, terrible, aweinspiring, dread, dire Il. 1.200, Il. 2.321, Il. 5.739, Il. 8.135, Il. 11.418, etc.: Od. 3.145, Od. 5.52, Od. 11.157, Od. 12.94, Od. 22.405, etc. With complementary infin.: δεινὸν γένος βασιλήϊόν ἐστι κτείνειν Od. 16.401. Of noises, troubling the hearers, terrible, dreadful: καναχήν Il. 16.104. Cf. Il. 1.49, Il. 23.688. Of something said, calculated to trouble the hearer, out of place, unseemly: ἔπος Od. 8.409, Od. 21.169. 2 In neut. δεινόν as adv., so as to cause fear, fearfully, terribly, dreadfully: δ. δερκόμενοι Il. 3.342. Cf. Il. 3.337, Il. 4.420, Il. 6.182, Il. 8.133, Il. 11.10, etc.: κῦμα δ. ἐπεσσύμενον Od. 5.314. Cf. Od. 5.403, Od. 11.608, Od. 12.85, 106, 236, Od. 22.124, etc. So in pl. δεινά Il. 5.439, Il. 15.13, Il. 16.706 = Il. 20.448. 3 Troubling with excessive wonder, marvellous, strange: θαῦμα Il. 13.100. Exciting wonder, wonderful: πελώρου Od. 10.168. 4 To be regarded or treated with awe, reverence or respect: ὅρκου Il. 2.755, θεός Il. 4.514. Cf. Il. 3.172, Il. 5.839, Il. 6.380 = 385, Il. 18.394, Il. 21.25: Od. 7.41, 246, 255, Od. 8.22, Od. 10.136 = Od. 11.8 = Od. 12.150, Od. 12.322, 449, Od. 14.234. In superl. δεινότατος Il. 15.38: = Od. 5.186. 5 Of armour, with notion of great power of resistance, proof against blows, stout: σάκος Il. 7.245, 266. Cf. Il. 10.254, 272, Il. 20.259. 6 Feeling fear: ἀγορὴ δεινὴ τετρηχυῖα (in fear and disorder) Il. 7.346.
δείξω fut. δείκνυμι.
δείους genit. δέος.

δειπνέω [δεῖπνον.] 3 sing. plupf. δεδειπνήκετ Od. 17.359. to take δεῖπνον 1 a In sense 1.a Il. 19.304: Od. 9.312, Od. 15.397. b In sense 1.b Od. 15.79. c In sense 1.f Od. 4.685, Od. 17.359, 506, Od. 20.119. d In sense 1.g Od. 9.155. 2 Of the meal taken by Hermes on arriving at Calypso's island Od. 5.95. Of that taken by the disguised Odysseus on arriving at Eumaeus's hut Od. 14.111.
δείπνηστος ὁ [δεῖπνον.] The time for δεῖπνον: ὅτε δ. ἔην Od. 17.170 (here in sense 1.f).
†δειπνίζω [δεῖπνον.] Aor. pple. δειπνίσσας. To entertain at δεῖπνον: κατέπεφνε δειπνίσσας Od. 4.535 = Od. 11.411 (app. in sense 1.f, but the time is not determined).

δεῖπνον -ου, τό. 1 The principal meal of the day. a Taken before beginning the day's work, whether of fighting or of a peaceful occupation Il. 2.381 = Il. 19.275, Il. 2.399, Il. 8.53, Il. 19.171, 316, 346: Od. 9.311. b Taken by travellers before setting out Od. 15.77 = 94. c Taken in an interval of occupation Il. 11.86, Il. 18.560: Od. 6.97. d Taken after work Il. 23.158. e Taken on returning from a nocturnal expedition Il. 10.578. f The regular principal meal, taken in the late morning or about mid-day Od. 1.124, 134, Od. 17.176, Od. 19.321, 419, Od. 20.390, Od. 24.215, 360, 386, 394, 412.– g A meal taken on shore by a ship's company Od. 9.86 = Od. 10.57, Od. 10.155, Od. 15.500.– h A meal taken in the evening (Od. 3.497) by travellers arriving at a house and finding a marriage-feast in progress Od. 4.61 (the same meal called δόρπον 213; and cf. μεταδόρπιος 194).– i Of an ἔρανος on the day after a marriage-feast Od. 4.624. 2 Simply, a meal Od. 10.116, Od. 15.316. 3 The material for a meal: αἷγας Od. 17.214 = Od. 20.175. 4 A feed for horses Il. 2.383.

data.ref: Od. 3.497) by travellers arriving at a house and finding a marriage-feast in progress

definition: δείραντας acc. pl. masc. aor. pple. δέρω.

δειρή -ῆς, ἡ. 1 The neck or throat Il. 3.371, 396, Il. 13.202, Il. 14.412, Il. 18.177, Il. 19.285: Od. 22.472, Od. 23.208, 240. Of the necks of Scylla Od. 12.90. Of an eagle's neck Il. 12.204: Od. 2.153. 2 The neck-opening of a θώρηξ Il. 11.26.
δειροτομέω [δειρή + τομ-, τάμνω.] (ἀπο-.) To cut the throat of, to slay thus; or simply, to slay Il. 21.89, 555, Il. 23.174: Od. 22.349.
δεῖσε 3 sing. aor. See δείδοικα.
δείσεται 3 sing. fut. See δείδοικα.
δεκάκις [δέκα.] 1 Ten times Il. 9.379. 2 Ten times the normal, tenfold: ἄποινα Il. 22.349.
δεκάς -άδος, ἡ [δέκα.] A body or company of ten: εἴ κʼ ἐς δεκάδας διακοσμηθεῖμεν Il. 2.126. Cf. Il. 2.128: Od. 16.245.

δέκατος -η, -ον [δέκα.] 1 The tenth: Ἠώς Il. 6.175, ὲς δεκάτους ἐνιαυτούς (app. for ἐς δέκα ἐνιαυτούς by confusion with ἐς δέκατον ἐνιαυτόν) Od. 8.404 = 418. Cf. Il. 2.329, Il. 9.474, Il. 12.15, Il. 24.785: Od. 5.107, Od. 7.253 = Od. 14.314, Od. 12.447, Od. 14.241, 325 = Od. 19.294, Od. 16.18, Od. 19.192. 2 δεκάτη (sc. ἡμέρη), the tenth day: δεκάτῃ (on the tenth day) Od. 9.83. So τῇ δεκάτῃ Il. 1.54, Il. 24.612, 665: Od. 10.29.
δεκάχιλοι [δέκα + χίλιοι.] Ten thousand Il. 5.860 = Il. 14.148.
δέκτης ὁ [δεκ-, δέχομαι.] A beggar Od. 4.248.
δέκτο 3 sing. aor. δέχομαι.
δελφίς -ῖνος, ὁ. A dolphin Il. 21.22: Od. 12.96.

δέμας τό [δέμω.] 1 One's bodily frame or build: οὐ δέμας οὐδὲ φυήν (the two words difficult to distinguish) Il. 1.115, μικρὸς δέμας Il. 5.801 (here app. stature), δέμας ἐϊκυῖα θεῇσιν Il. 8.305. Cf. Il. 13.45, Il. 17.323, 555, Il. 21.285, Il. 22.227, Il. 24.376: δέμας ἀθανάτοισιν ὁμοῖος Od. 3.468. Cf. Od. 2.268 = 401 = Od. 22.206 = Od. 24.503 = 548, Od. 4.796, Od. 5.212, 213, Od. 7.210, Od. 8.14, 116, 194, Od. 11.469 = Od. 24.17, Od. 13.222, 288, Od. 14.177, Od. 16.157, 174, Od. 18.251, Od. 19.124, 381, Od. 20.31, 194, Od. 23.163. Of animals: συῶν δέμας Od. 10.240. Cf. Od. 17.307, 313. 2 In advbl. acc. with genit., in the build of, after the similitude of, like (as our like has developed fr. orig. Teutonic *liko-, body, form): πυρός Il. 11.596 = Il. 13.673 = Il. 18.1, Il. 17.366.

δέμνια τά [δέμω.] A bedstead, a bed. (In Il. 24.644 two beds are referred to. See 648. So perh. also in Od. 4.297, 301; but from Od. 15.45 it would rather appear that Telemachus and Peisistratus were then sleeping together): δέμνιʼ ὑπʼ αἰθούσῃ θέμεναι Il. 24.644: = Od. 4.297 = Od. 7.336, δέμνια κούρης Od. 6.20. Cf. Od. 4.301, Od. 8.277, 282, 296, 314, Od. 11.189, Od. 19.318, 599, Od. 20.139.

data.ref: Il. 24.644 two beds are referred to. See
Od. 15.45 it would rather appear that Telemachus and Peisistratus were then sleeping together):

definition: δέμω [cf. δόμος.] Aor. ἔδειμα Il. 21.446. 3 sing. -ε Il. 9.349. 3 pl. -αν Il. 7.436, Il. 14.32. 1 pl. subj. δείμομεν Il. 7.337. 3 sing. aor. mid. (ἐ)δείματο Od. 6.9, Od. 14.8. 3 sing. plupf. pass. (ἐ)δέδμητο Il. 13.683: Od. 1.426, Od. 9.185, Od. 14.6. Pl. pple. δεδμημένοι Il. 6.245, 249. to construct, build, form: πύργους Il. 7.337. Cf. Il. 6.245, 249, Il. 7.436, Il. 9.349, Il. 13.683, Il. 14.32, Il. 21.446; ὅθι οἱ θάλαμος δέδμητο (was in the state of having been built, i.e., simply, stood) Od. 1.426, θάλαμον Od. 23.192. Cf. Od. 9.185, Od. 14.6. In mid. Od. 6.9, Od. 14.8.
δενδίλλω App., to turn the eyes, give meaning looks: ἐς ἕκαστον Il. 9.180.
δενδρήεις -εσσα [δένδρεον.] Abounding in trees: νῆσος Od. 1.51, ἄλσεϊ Od. 9.200.
δέξατο 3 sing. aor. δέχομαι.

δεξιός -ή, -όν. Locative δεξιόφιν Il. 13.308. 1 That is on the right side, the right ...: ὦμον Il. 5.46 = Il. 16.343, Il. 5.98, 189, Il. 11.507, Il. 14.450, Il. 16.289, 468, Il. 22.133: Od. 17.462, 504, Od. 18.95, Od. 19.452. Cf. Il. 4.481, Il. 5.66, Il. 11.584, Il. 13.651. The right-hand . . . : ἵππον Il. 23.336. 2 ἐπὶ δεξιά, to the right : νωμῆσαι βῶν Il. 7.238, εἴτʼ ἐπὶ δ. ἴωσιν (from left to right of a spectator, i.e. in the lucky direction) Il. 12.239.–ἐπὶ δεξιόφιν on the right of. With genit.: παντὸς στρατοῦ Il. 13.308. 3 Of a bird of omen, passing as in Il. 12.239 above, boding well: δεξιὸν ἧκεν ἐρωδιόν Il. 10.274. Cf. Il. 13.821, Il. 24.294 = 312, 320: Od. 2.154, Od. 15.160 = 525, 531, Od. 15.164, Od. 24.312. 4 In fem. δεξιή (sc. χείρ), the right hand: δεξιῇ ἠσπάζοντο Il. 10.542. A grasp or clasp of the right hand as the sign of a pledge Il. 2.341 = Il. 4.159.

δεξιτερός -ή, -όν [in form comp. of δεξιός. with changed accent.] Fem. instrumental δεξιτερῆφι Od. 19.480. This form as locative Il. 24.284: Od. 15.148. 1 That is on the right side, the right . . . : κνήμην Il. 4.519. Cf. Il. 5.393, Il. 7.108, Il. 10.373, Il. 11.377, Il. 14.137, Il. 21.167, Il. 24.284, 672: Od. 1.121, Od. 15.148, Od. 18.258, 397, Od. 19.480, Od. 20.197, Od. 21.410. The right-hand part of, the part of on the right: γναθμὸν δεξιτερόν Il. 16.405. 2 In fem. δεξιτερή (sc. χείρ), the right hand: δεξιτερῇ ἑλοῦσα Il. 1.501. Cf. Il. 21.490, Il. 22.320.
δέξο aor. imp. δέχομαι.
δέξομαι fut. δέχομαι.

δέος τό (δϝέος) [δϝι-, δείδοικα.] Genit. δείους Il. 10.376, Il. 15.4. 1 Fear, terror, affright, apprehension Il. 4.421, Il. 5.812, 817, Il. 7.479, Il. 8.77, Il. 10.376, Il. 13.224, Il. 14.387, Il. 15.4, 658, Il. 17.67, 625: Od. 6.140, Od. 11.43, 633, Od. 12.243, Od. 14.88, Od. 22.42, Od. 24.450, 533. 2 Reason or cause for fear or apprehension: οὔ τοι ἔπι δ. Il. 1.515. With complementary infin.: σοὶ οὐ δ. ἔστʼ ἀπολέσθαι Il. 12.246. Cf. Od. 5.347, Od. 8.563.

δέπας τό. Dat. δέπαϊ Il. 23.196, Il. 24.285: Od. 3.41, Od. 15.149, Od. 18.121, Od. 20.261. δέᾳ Od. 10.316. Pl. δέπα (for δέπαα) Od. 15.466, Od. 19.62, Od. 20.153. Genit. δεπάων Il. 7.480. Dat. δεπάεσσι Il. 1.471, Il. 3.295, Il. 8.162, etc.: Od. 3.340, Od. 7.137, Od. 18.418, etc. δέπασσι Il. 15.86. A drinking-cup: ἐπαρξάμενοι δεπάεσσιν (locative dat., into the . . .) Il. 1.471 = Il. 9.176, ἀμφικύπελλον Il. 1.584. Cf. Il. 3.295, Il. 4.3, 262, Il. 7.480, Il. 9.203, etc.: Od. 3.41, Od. 7.137, Od. 9.10, Od. 18.152, Od. 19.62, etc.

δέρκομαι 3 sing. pa. iterative δερκέσκετο Od. 5.84, 158. Aor. ἔδρακον Od. 10.197. 3 sing. pf. (in press. sense) δέδορκε Il. 22.95. Pple. δεδορκώς Od. 19.446. (ἀνα-, δια-, ἐσ-, κατα-, προσ-,) 1 To see, behold, look upon: Τρῶας Il. 13.86. Cf. Il. 14.141. 2 To have the power of sight as being alive: ἐμεῦ (ἐμέθεν) ἐπὶ χθονὶ δερκομένοιο Il. 1.88: Od. 16.439. 3 To descry, make out: καπνόν Od. 10.197. Absol.: ὀξύτατον δέρκεσθαι Il. 17.675. 4 To direct the sight, look: ἐπὶ πόντον Od. 5.84 = Od. 5.158. 5 To look, glance: δεινόν Il. 3.342, Il. 11.37, Il. 23.815. Cf. Il. 22.95, Il. 23.477. Fig., with cognate acc.: πῦρ ὀφθαλμοῖσι δεδορκώς Od. 19.446.

δέρμα -ατος, τό [δέρω.] 1 A hide or skin stripped from a beast: συός Il. 9.548. Cf. Od. 4.436, 440, Od. 22.362. 2 The prepared skin of a beast: λέοντος Il. 10.23, 177. Cf. Od. 13.436, Od. 14.50, 519. 3 A piece of leather: βόειον Od. 14.24. Used as = ἄντυξ 2 Il. 6.117. A leathern bag: πυκινοῖσιν Od. 2.291. 4 The human skin: ἔσχεθε δʼ οἷον δέρμα (the strip of skin not severed) Il. 16.341. Cf. Od. 13.431.
δερμάτινος [δερματ-, δέρμα.] Leathern: τροποῖς Od. 4.782 = Od. 8.53.
δέρτρον τό [δέρω.] The membrane enclosing the intestines: γῦπε δ. ἔσω δύνοντες Od. 11.579.

δέρω 3 pl. aor. ἔδειραν Il. 1.459, Il. 2.422: Od. 12.359. Acc. pl. masc. pple. δείραντας Od. 10.533, Od. 11.46. (ἐκ-,) To flay (a beast) Il. 7.316, Il. 23.167, Il. 24.622: Od. 8.61, Od. 10.533 = Od. 11.46, Od. 19.421. Absol. Il. 1.459 = Il. 2.422: Od. 12.359.

δεσμός ὁ [δεσ-, δέω.] Pl. δέσματα Od. 1.204. Acc. δέσματα Il. 22.468: Od. 8.278. 1 Any means of securing a person, a bond, bonds: δῆσαν κρατερῷ ἐνὶ δεσμῷ Il. 5.386. Cf. Il. 5.391, Il. 10.443, Il. 15.19: δεσμὸν ἀνέγναμψαν Od. 14.348. Cf. Od. 8.317, 353, 359, 360, Od. 12.160, Od. 15.232, 444, Od. 22.189, 200. In pl. (app., except where the idea of number is involved, used indifferently with the sing.): ὑπελύσαο δεσμῶν Il. 1.401: ἐνὶ πλεόνεσσι δεσμοῖσι διδέντων Od. 12.54. Cf. Od. 1.204, Od. 8.274, 278, 296, 336, 340, Od. 11.293, Od. 12.164, 196, 200. 2 A halter for a horse Il. 6.507 = Il. 15.264. 3 A ship's mooring-cable Od. 13.100. 4 A knot (in a cord put round a chest to secure the lid) Od. 8.443, 447. 5 A means of securing a gate: ἐπὶ δεσμὸν ἰῆλαι [θύραις] Od. 21.241 (app. not referring to a regular fastening. The gate is in fact secured with a ὅπλον νεός. See 390). 6 A rivet Il. 18.379. 7 In pl., articles of head-dress in gen.: δέσματα σιγαλόεντα Il. 22.468 (the particular articles being specified in the next line).

δέσποινα -ης, ἡ [δεσ-, house + a second element conn. with πόσις1 Cf. δεσπότης, master, πότνια; also δασπλῆτις.] The lady of a house, a mistress Od. 7.53, Od. 14.9 = 451, Od. 14.127, Od. 15.374, 377, Od. 19.83, Od. 23.2. Joined with ἄλοχος Od. 3.403. With γυνή Od. 7.347.
δετή -ῆς, ἡ [δέω.] A faggot Il. 11.554 = Il. 17.663.
δευήσεαι 2 sing. fut. δεύομαι. See δεύω2.

δεῦρο In form δεύρω Il. 3.240 (v.l. δεῦρο). Hither. 1 With vbs. of motion: ἤλυθον Il. 1.153. Cf. Il. 2.138, Il. 3.240, Il. 6.426, Il. 10.406, Il. 22.12, Il. 23.21, etc.: μολόντες Od. 3.44. Cf. Od. 8.424, Od. 15.213, Od. 16.132, Od. 17.53, Od. 24.299, etc. With imp. : δ. ἴθι Il. 3.130. Cf. Il. 3.390, Il. 7.75, Il. 13.235. In pregnant sense: δ. παρέστης Il. 3.405. Elliptically (withἄγε): ἄγε δ., ὄφρα. . . Il. 17.685. Cf. Od. 9.517, Od. 11.561. 2 With other vbs.: κάλεσσον Il. 4.193, ὁρόωντες Il. 17.637. Cf. Il. 24.106: Od. 17.529. 3 With imp. (with or without ἄγε), come ! ἄγε δ. παρʼ ἔμʼ ἵστασο Il. 11.314, Il. 17.179. Cf. Il. 23.581: δ. ὄρσο Od. 22.395. Cf. Od. 8.145, 205, Od. 12.184, Od. 22.233. 4 With 1 pl. subj. (with or without ἄγε), come ! let us ...: δ. ἐς τοὺς φύλακας καταβήομεν Il. 10.97. Cf. Il. 17.120, Il. 22.254, Il. 23.485: Od. 8.292.
δεύτατος [superl. to δεύτερος.] Last, the last: ἦλθεν Il. 19.51: Od. 1.286, τοῦτο δεύτατον εἶπεν ἔπος Od. 23.342.

δεῦτε = δεῦρο. Used in dual and pl. contexts. 1 = δεῦρο 1 elliptically: δ. καί μʼ ἀμύνετε Il. 13.481. Cf. Od. 8.307. 2 = δεῦρο 3: δ. δύω μοι ἕπεσθον Il. 22.450. With ἄγε Od. 8.11. 3 = δεῦρο 4 (with or without ἄγετε): δ. ἴομεν Il. 14.128. Cf. Il. 7.350: Od. 2.410, Od. 8.133.

δεύτερος [prob. fr. δεύω2.] 1 Coming second in a contest: γνώσεσθʼ ἵππους οἳ δεύτεροι οἵ τε πάροιθεν Il. 23.498. With ellipse of sb.: τῷ δευτέρῳ ἵππον ἔθηκεν Il. 23.265. Cf. Il. 23.750. In neut. pl. δεύτερα, the prize for the secondIl. 23.538. 2 Coming second in gaining estimation, taking a second place: ἵνα μὴ δ. ἔλθοι Il. 10.368. Cf. Il. 22.207. 3 (except in Il. 17.45, Il. 21.596 strengthened by αὖτε) a Second in doing something, following another in doing it: ἠρᾶτο Il. 10.283. Cf. Il. 23.729, 841. b In fighting, coming in with one's throw or stroke after an opponent: προΐει ἔγχος Il. 7.248, Il. 20.273. Cf. Il. 5.855, Il. 7.268, Il. 17.45, Il. 21.169, 596. 4 With genit.: ἐμεῖο δεύτεροι (left behind or surviving me) Il. 23.248. 5 In neut. δεύτερον as adv. a In the second place. With αὖ: δ. αὖ θώρηκʼ ἔδυνεν Il. 3.332 = Il. 11.19 = Il. 16.133 = Il. 19.371. Cf. Il. 6.184. b A second time, again: ὁρμηθείς Il. 16.402. With αὖτε Il. 3.191. With αὖτις Il. 1.513: Od. 3.161, Od. 19.65 (cf. Od. 18.321), Od. 22.69. Sim.: ᾔτεέ με δ. αὖτις (asked for a second supply) Od. 9.354. c Another time, for the future. With αὖτε: δ. αὖτʼ ἀλέασθαι ἀμείνονας ἠπεροπεύειν Il. 23.605. Again, in the future: οὔ μʼ ἔτι δ. ὦδε ἵξετʼ ἄχος Il. 23.46. Cf. Od. 18.24. d So as to come in as in 3.b: ὁρμηθείς Il. 16.467. Cf. Il. 3.349.

data.quote: γνώσεσθʼ ἵππους οἳ δεύτεροι οἵ τε πάροιθεν
οὔ μʼ ἔτι δ. ὦδε ἵξετʼ ἄχος

definition: δεύω2 (δέϝω). 3 sing. aor. ἐδεύησε Od. 9.483, 540. Also in form δῆσε Il. 18.100. Except in these forms as deponent δεύομαι. 2 sing. fut. δευήσεαι Od. 6.192, Od. 14.510. Infin. -εσθαι Il. 13.786: Od. 23.128. (ἐπιδεύομαι.) 1 To lack, be without, want, not to have. With genit.: ἡγεμόνος Il. 2.709. Cf. Il. 2.128, Il. 4.48 = Il. 24.69, Il. 5.202, Il. 8.127, Il. 13.786, Il. 18.100: ἐσθῆτος Od. 6.192, Od. 14.510. Cf. Od. 7.73, Od. 8.137, Od. 23.128. Absol.: ἧσθαι δευόμενον (with empty hands) Il. 1.134, μηδέ τι θυμῷ δευέσθω (fail) Il. 20.122, δευόμενος (in his need) Il. 22.492. To be in the state of having (something) fail one, be deprived of, lose. With genit.: θυμοῦ Il. 3.294, Il. 20.472. 2 To fall short of (a person). With genit.: Ἀργείων Il. 23.484. Cf. Od. 1.254, Od. 4.264. To be unequal to, unfitted for. With genit.: πολέμοιο Il. 13.310. Cf. Il. 17.142. 3 To suffer want or be stinted in the matter of. With genit.: δαιτός Il. 1.468 = 602 = Il. 2.431 = Il. 7.320 = Il. 23.56: = Od. 16.479 = Od. 19.425. 4 To fail to do something. With infin.: ἐδεύησεν οἰήϊον ἄκρον ἱκέσθαι Od. 9.483 = 540.

δέχομαι Fut. δέξομαι Il. 18.115, Il. 22.365. 3 sing. -εται Il. 17.208, Il. 18.331. Fut. pf. δεδέξομαι Il. 5.238. 3 sing. aor. (ἐ)δέξατο Il. 1.446, Il. 2.186, Il. 5.158, Il. 6.483, Il. 9.633, etc.: Od. 1.121, Od. 5.462, Od. 8.483, Od. 11.327, Od. 21.82, etc. Imp. δέξαι Il. 5.227, Il. 6.46, Il. 11.131, Il. 17.480, Il. 24.137, 429, 555. Pple. δεξάμενος, -ου Il. 9.333, 636, Il. 14.203, Il. 17.391, Il. 23.89: Od. 8.419, Od. 13.72, Od. 15.132, Od. 17.110. Fem. -η Od. 14.128, Od. 19.355. Infin. δέξασθαι Il. 1.112: Od. 18.287. 3 sing. aor. δέκτο Il. 2.420, Il. 15.88: Od. 9.353. Imp. δέξο Il. 19.10. Infin. δέχθαι Il. 1.23, 377. 3 pl. pf. δέχαται Il. 12.147. Imp. δέδεξο Il. 5.228, Il. 20.377, Il. 22.340. Pple. δεδεγμένος, -ου Il. 4.107, Il. 8.296, Il. 10.62, Il. 11.124, Il. 15.745, Il. 23.273. δέγμενος, -ου Il. 2.794, Il. 9.191, Il. 18.524: Od. 20.385. Also pf. pple. δεδοκημένος Il. 15.730. Plupf. ἐδέγμην Od. 9.513, Od. 12.230. (ἀνα-, ἀπο-, ἐκ-, παρα-, ποτι-, ὑπο-.) 1 To receive or take something offered, given, handed over, etc., to accept: ἄποινα Il. 1.20, παιδὸς κύπελλον (from him) Il. 1.596, σκῆπτρόν οἱ (from him) Il. 2.186, χαλκὸν δέδεξο (app., be minded to accept) Il. 22.340. Cf. Il. 1.446, Il. 5.227, Il. 6.483, Il. 9.633, Il. 17.391, etc.: κρήδεμνον Od. 5.462, δῶρα (for custody) Od. 8.419, χρυσὸν ἀνδρός (as the price of the betrayal of . . .) Od. 11.327, ἔγχος οἱ (relieved him of . . .) Od. 15.282 = Od. 16.40. Cf. Od. 1.121, Od. 8.483, Od. 9.353, Od. 17.356, Od. 19.355, etc. Of a god, to accept (a sacrifice) Il. 2.420. 2 To receive (a child) for nurture Il. 14.203. To receive and undertake the charge of (a person) Il. 23.89. To receive, welcome Il. 5.158, Il. 18.238, 331. To receive hospitably, entertain Od. 14.128, Od. 17.110, Od. 19.316. 3 To accept, resign oneself to: κῆρα Il. 18.115, Il. 22.365. To accept, put up with, make the best of: μῦθον Od. 20.271. 4 In pf. and plupf. a To expect, look for: χρυσὸν Ἀλεξάνδροιο (from...) Il. 11.124. With acc. and infin.: φῶτα μέγαν ἐδέγμην ἐλεύσεσθαι Od. 9.513. Cf. Od. 12.230. b To wait. With dependent clause: ὁππότʼ ἀφορμηθεῖεν (watching for the time when...)
