Il. 2.794, εἰς ὅ κεν ἔλθῃς Il. 10.62. Cf. Il. 18.524: Od. 20.385. To await. With dependent clause: Αἰακίδην ὁπότε λήξειεν Il. 9.191. Of things: ίππῆας ἄεθλα δεδεγμένα Il. 23.273. Absol.: δεδεγμένος (on the watch) Il. 4.107. c To await the attack of, stand up to, be ready for: Ἀχιλλῆα Il. 20.377. Cf. Il. 5.228, 238, Il. 12.147, Il. 15.745. Absol. Il. 8.296, Il. 15.730. 5 App., to succeed, come next: δέχεταί μοι κακὸν ἐκ κακοῦ Il. 19.290.
†δέψω Aor. pple. δεψήσας. To work or knead with the hands in order to soften: κηρόν Od. 12.48.

δέω 3 sing. pa. iterative mid. δησάσκετο Il. 24.15. 3 sing. plupf. pass. δέδεντο Il. 5.387, Il. 23.866: Od. 15.232, Od. 24.229. 3 pl. δέδεντο Il. 10.475: Od. 9.443, Od. 10.92. (ἐκ-, ἐν-, ἐπι-, κατα-, συν-.) 1 To tie or secure in its place, fasten: δῆσε ζυγόν Il. 5.730. Cf. Il. 24.190, 267: Od. 2.425 = Od. 15.290. In mid. Od. 8.37. 2 To tie into a bundle, bind together. In mid.: δράγματα δέοντο Il. 18.553. 3 To tie or attach by a cord, a strap, etc.: ἐκ δίφροιο ἔδησεν [Ἕκτορα] Il. 22.398, ποδός (by the foot) Il. 23.854. Cf. Il. 23.866: Od. 9.443. In mid. Il. 24.15. To tie round (with a fastening). In mid., [πόδα] δησάμενος τελαμῶνι Il. 17.290. 4 To moor (a ship) Od. 10.92. 5 To tie or secure (a rope): πρυμνήσια Il. 1.436. Cf. Il. 24.273: Od. 10.96, Od. 15.498. In mid. Od. 8.26: Od. 2.430. 6 To tie or secure (a person's feet, etc.): πόδας καὶ χεῖρας Od. 21.454. Cf. Od. 21.30: Od. 22.189. 7 To bind or secure (a person), put (him) in bonds: δῆσαν κρατερῷ ἐνὶ δεσμῷ Il. 5.386. Cf. Il. 1.406, Il. 2.231, Il. 5.387, Il. 10.443: Od. 8.352, Od. 9.99, Od. 12.50, 161, 178, 196, Od. 15.232. Fig.: ἡμέτερον μένος Il. 14.73: κελεύθου με (hinders from . . . ) Od. 4.380 = 469. Cf. Od. 14.61. To halter or secure (a horse or an ox) Od. 8.544, Il. 10.475, Il. 13.572. 8 To bind up (a wound) Od. 19.457. 9 In mid., to tie on to one's person: ἐδήσατο πέδιλα Il. 24.340, Il. 2.44 = Il. 10.22 = 132 = Il. 14.186: = Od. 2.4 = Od. 4.309 = Od. 20.126, Od. 1.96, Od. 5.44, Od. 15.550, Od. 16.155, Od. 17.2. Sim. in pass.: περὶ κνήμῃσι κνημῖδας δέδετο (had them bound about his legs) Od. 24.229.

δή 1 Temporal particle. a α By or before this (or that) time, by now, now, already, ere this: ἐννέα δὴ βεβάασιν ἐνιαυτοί Il. 2.134. Cf. Il. 1.394, 503, Il. 2.117, Il. 3.150, Il. 5.383, Il. 8.297, etc.: ὃς δὴ γήραϊ κυφὸς ἔην Od. 2.16. Cf. Od. 1.26, 161, Od. 3.245, Od. 4.373, Od. 7.152, Od. 13.10, etc. β Indicating the arrival of a point of time, arrival at a result: ἐξ οὗ δὴ διαστήτην (from the time when the quarrel came to the point of braaking out) Il. 1.6, εἰδὴ ὁμοῦ πόλεμός τε δαμᾷ καὶ λοιμὸς Ἀχαιούς (if it has come to this that . . . ) Il. 1.61, νημερτὲς μὲν δή μοι ὑπόσχεο (you must now decide) 514. Cf. Il. 1.161, 574, Il. 8.34, Il. 9.202, 309, 434, Il. 19.9, Il. 20.115, etc.: ἦ μάλα δή με θέσφαθʼ ἱκάνει Od. 13.172, ὅππως δὴ μνηστῆρσι χεῖρας ἐφήσει (at this crisis of his fate) Od. 20.29, αἲ γὰρ δὴ θεοὶ τισαίατο λώβην (to such a pitch of insolence have they come) 169. Cf. Od. 14.333, 379, Od. 19.510, Od. 22.395, Od. 23.43, etc. With ἄγε, ἄγετε. See ἄγε.–With ἄγρει Od. 21.176. b Now, at this (or that ) time: καὶ δὴ τάχʼ ἔμελλε . . . Il. 6.52. Cf. Il. 1.388, Il. 2.436, Il. 9.245, Il. 11.126, 441, Il. 17.261, etc.: ὃς δή σφι σχεδόν ἐστιν Od. 2.284. Cf. Od. 4.551, 770, Od. 5.401, 409, Od. 10.549, Od. 16.280, etc. c Joined with, and emphasizing or defining, other temporal words: αἰεὶ δή Il. 12.323, δὴ αὖ Il. 1.540, δὴ αὖτε Il. 1.340, ἐπεὶ δή Il. 4.124, ἐπὴν δή Il. 16.453, καί νυ δή Il. 7.273, νῦν δή Od. 2.284, ὁππότε δή Il. 16.53, ὅτε δή Il. 1.432, ὀψὲ δή Il. 7.94, τάχα δή Il. 13.120, τῆμος δή Od. 12.441, τότε δή Il. 1.92, etc. 2 As affirmative or emphasizing particle: μὴ δὴ οὕτως κλέπτε νόῳ Il. 1.131. Cf. Il. 1.286, 295, Il. 2.158, 301, Il. 6.476, Il. 8.491, Il. 11.314, Il. 13.260, Il. 18.364, etc.: εἰ δὴ ἐξ αὐτοῖο τόσος πάϊς εἰς Ὀδυσῆος Od. 1.207. Cf. Od. 1.253, 384, Od. 3.352, 357, Od. 4.819, Od. 5.23, Od. 11.348, Od. 14.282, etc. Giving a touch of scorn, forsooth, to be sure: ὡς δὴ τοῦδʼ ἕνεκά σφιν ἑκηβόλος ἄλγεα τεύχει Il. 1.110. Cf. Il. 3.403, Il. 8.177, Il. 14.88, etc.: Od. 21.170. Emphasizing superlatives: κάρτιστοι δὴ κεῖνοι τράφεν Il. 1.266. Cf. Il. 6.98, Il. 7.155, Il. 10.436, Il. 22.76, etc.: οἴκτιστον δὴ κεῖνο ἴδον Od. 12.258. Cf. Od. 8.519, Od. 11.309, etc.

data.quote: ἦ μάλα δή με θέσφαθʼ ἱκάνει
εἰ δὴ ἐξ αὐτοῖο τόσος πάϊς εἰς Ὀδυσῆος
ὡς δὴ τοῦδʼ ἕνεκά σφιν ἑκηβόλος ἄλγεα τεύχει

definition: †δήεις 2sing. 1 pl. δήομεν 2 pl pl. δήετε. [Subjunctives with strong stem answering to δᾶ- in ἐδάην, etc. See δάω. The -εις of 2 sing. app. a trace of an older inflexion, -ω, -εις, -ει, answering to -ομεν, -ετε.] To find, to light or come upon: δούρατα δήεις (will find) Il. 13.260. Cf. Od. 6.291, Od. 7.49, Od. 13.407. Of immaterial things: ἐν πήματα οἴκῳ Od. 11.115. To find, get: ἄλλοθι ἕδρην Od. 16.44. To find out by experience: τέκμωρ Ἰλίου Il. 9.418 = 685. To attain to, bring about: ἄνυσιν Od. 4.544.

δηθά [δήν.] For a long time, for long, long: μηκέτι δ. λεγώμεθα Il. 2.435, ποταμῷ δ ἱερεύετε ταύρους . . . καθίετε ἵππους (the vbs. to be taken as presents, have long been sacrificing . . . ) Il. 21.131. Cf. Il. 5.104, 587, Il. 10.52, Il. 14.110, Il. 15.512: δ. πήματα πάσχει (has been suffering) Od. 1.49, δ. θύρῃσιν ἐφεστάμεν 120. Cf. Od. 2.255, 404, Od. 3.313, 336, Od. 4.373, 466, Od. 7.152, Od. 8.411, Od. 12.351, Od. 16.313, Od. 22.177.
δηθύνω [δηθά.] To tarry, delay, loiter Il. 1.27, Il. 6.503, 519: Od. 12.121, Od. 17.278.

δήϊος1 -ον (the first syllable scanned ⏑) [conn. with δαίω1. Perh. orig. δά̆ϝιος. Cf. θεσπιδαής.] Epithet of fire, blazing, consuming Il. 2.415, Il. 6.331, Il. 8.181, Il. 9.347, 674, Il. 11.667, Il. 16.127, 301, Il. 18.13.

δήϊος2 (The first syllable scanned ⏑ when followed by ⏑–.) 1 Hostile, enemy: ἄνδρα Il. 6.481. Cf. Il. 9.317 = Il. 17.148, Il. 10.358, Il. 12.57, Il. 15.533, Il. 22.84, Il. 24.684. Epithet of πόλεμος, destructive, deadlyIl. 4.281, Il. 5.117, Il. 7.119 = 174, Il. 17.189, Il. 19.73, Il. 21.422. Of Ares Il. 7.241. 2 As sb., an enemy, a foe: δηΐοισι μάχεσθαι Il. 4.373. Cf. Il. 2.544, Il. 6.82, Il. 9.76, Il. 10.206, Il. 11.190 = 205, Il. 12.264, 276, Il. 13.395, 556, Il. 15.548, Il. 16.591, Il. 17.167, 272, 667, Il. 18.208, 220.

δηϊοτής -ῆτος, ἡ [δήϊος2.] 1 Battle, warfare, strife, struggle Il. 3.20, Il. 5.348, Il. 7.29, Il. 12.248, Il. 14.129, Il. 16.815, Il. 20.245, etc.: Od. 6.203, Od. 11.516, Od. 12.257, Od. 22.229. 2 In concrete sense, the fighters, the fighting throng: θέων ἀνὰ δηϊοτῆτα Il. 15.584, Il. 17.257.

†δηϊόω [δήϊος2.] 3 pl. opt. δηϊόῳεν Od. 4.226. Pple. δηϊόων Il. 17.566, Il. 18.195, Il. 23.176. Pl. δηϊόωντες Il. 11.153. 3 pl. impf. pass. δηϊόωντο Il. 13.675. Contr. forms. Pres. pple. δῃῶν Il. 17.65. 3 pl. impf. δῄουν Il. 5.452, Il. 11.71, Il. 12.425, Il. 15.708, Il. 16.771. Fut. infin. δῃώσειν Il. 9.243. 3 sing. aor. subj. δῃώσῃ Il. 16.650. 3 pl. -ωσι Il. 4.416, Il. 12.227. Pple. δῃώσας, -αντος Il. 8.534, Il. 14.518, Il. 16.158, Il. 18.83, Il. 22.218. Aor. pple. pass. δῃωθείς, -έντος Il. 4.417: Od. 9.66. 1 To treat as a foe, to wound, kill, slay Il. 8.534, Il. 11.71 = Il. 16.771, Il. 11.153, Il. 12.227, Il. 15.708, Il. 16.650, Il. 17.566, Il. 18.83, 195, Il. 22.218, Il. 23.176: Od. 4.226, Od. 9.66. To inflict slaughter upon (a hostile force): Τρῶας Il. 4.416. Cf. Il. 4.417, Il. 9.243, Il. 13.675. 2 To rend or tear: βοείας Il. 5.452 = Il. 12.425. Cf. Il. 14.518. Of beasts tearing their prey Il. 16.158, Il. 17.65.

δηλέομαι 3 sing. aor. subj. δηλήσηται Il. 3.107. (δια-.) 1 To do harm or mischief to, hurt, injure: μή πως ἀμφοτέρους δηλήσεαι Il. 23.428. Absol. Od. 8.444, Od. 13.124. Of warlike action Il. 4.67 = 72: Od. 10.459, Od. 11.401, 408, Od. 22.368, Od. 24.111. Absol. Il. 4.236, 271. –Of a weapon: ῥινὸν δηλήσατο χαλκός Od. 22.278. Also, absol., to do harm, lead to mischief: σή κε βουλἡ δηλήσεται Il. 14.102. 2 To ravage, destroy: καρπόν Il. 1.156. 3 To violate (a treaty) Il. 3.107.
δήλημα -ατος, τό [δηλέομαι.] Something that brings harm, a bane: δηλήματα νηῶν Od. 12.286.
δηλήμων -ονος [δηλέομαι]. Working mischief, baneful Il. 24.33. As sb., a bane Od. 18.85 = 116 = Od. 21.308.
δῆλος Clear, plain, manifest Od. 20.333.
δημιοεργός ὁ [δήμιος + ἔργον.] One who works for the common weal, not for himself or for a private employer Od. 17.383, Od. 19.135.

δήμιος -ον [δῆμος.] 1 Belonging to the community, public: οἶκος Od. 20.264. 2 Relating to the public interests, public: πρῆξις Od. 3.82. Absol.: ἦέ τι δήμιον πιφαύσκεται; Od. 2.32. Cf. Od. 2.44, Od. 4.314. 3 Discharging public functions: αἰσυμνῆται Od. 8.259. 4 In neut. pl. δήμια as adv., at the public cost (cf. δημόθεν): πίνουσιν Il. 17.250.
δημοβόρος [δῆμος 1 + βορ-, βι-βρώσκω.] (καταδημοβορέω.) That devours the common stock: βασιλεύς Il. 1.231.
δημογέρων -οντος [δῆμος + γέρων.] = γέρων 4 Il. 3.149, Il. 11.372.
δημόθεν [δῆμος 1 + -θεν 1.] From the common stock: δ. ἄλφιτα δῶκα Od. 19.197.

δῆμος -ου, ὁ. 1 The common stock or store: ἐς δῆμον ἔδωκεν Il. 11.704. 2 A district, country, land, realm: Ἐρεχθῆος Il. 2.547. Cf. Il. 2.828, Il. 3.201, Il. 5.710, Il. 6.158, 225, Il. 9.634, Il. 16.437, 455, 514, 673, 683, Il. 19.324, Il. 20.385, Il. 24.481: Ἰθάκης Od. 1.103. Cf. Od. 1.237, Od. 2.317, Od. 3.100, Od. 6.3, Od. 8.555, Od. 13.233, Od. 20.210, Od. 21.307, Od. 24.12, etc. 3 A community or people: παντὶ δήμῳ Il. 3.50, Il. 24.706, θεὸς ὣς τίετο δήμῳ (in the . . . , among the . . . ) Il. 5.78, Il. 10.33, Il. 11.58, Il. 13.218, Il. 16.605. Cf. Il. 9.460, Il. 11.328, Il. 12.447, Il. 17.577, Il. 18.295, 500, Il. 20.166: κατὰ δῆμον Od. 2.101, δήμου ἡγήτορες Od. 13.186. Cf. Od. 2.239, 291, Od. 4.691, Od. 7.11, 150, Od. 14.205, 239, Od. 16.114, 425, etc. 4 A body or force of men: ἑτεραλκέα δῆμον Il. 15.738. Cf. Il. 17.330. App., a multitude: ἐπὶ δʼ ἔστενε δ. ἀπείρων Il. 24.776. 5 The common people: δήμου ἄνδρα Il. 2.198. App., one of the common people: δῆμον ἐόντα Il. 12.213.

δήν (δϝήν). For a long time, for long, long: ἀκέων δ. ἧστο Il. 1.512. Cf. Il. 1.416, Il. 5.412, Il. 6.131, 139, Il. 8.126, Il. 9.30 = 695, Il. 13.573, Il. 16.736, Il. 17.695, Il. 20.426, Il. 23.690: δ. ἀπεών (having been long . . .) Od. 13.189, ὀϊζὺν δ. ἔχομεν (have long been suffering . . .) Od. 14.416. Cf. Od. 1.281, Od. 2.36, Od. 4.494, Od. 5.127, Od. 6.33, Od. 20.155, Od. 22.473, etc.
δηναιός [δήν.] Long-lived Il. 5.407.
δήνεα τά [app. fr. δάω.] 1 Arts, wiles: ὀλοφώϊα Od. 10.289. 2 What one has in one's mind, thougts, counsels: ἤπια δήνεα οἶδεν Il. 4.361 (see ἤπιος 1): θεῶν Od. 23.82.
δῄουν 3 pl. contr. impf. δηϊόω.

†δηριάομαι [δῆρις.] 3 dual δηριάασθον Il. 12.421. 3 pl. imp. δηριαάσθων Il. 21.467. Infin. δηριάασθαι Il. 16.96, Il. 17.734. 3 pl. impf. δηριόωντο Od. 8.78. To strive, contend, struggle, in passages cited.
†δηρίομαι [as δηριάομαι.] 3 pl. aor. δηρίσαντο Od. 8.76. 3 dual aor. δηρινθήτην Il. 16.756. = δηριάομαι.
δῆρις ἡ. Strife, contention Il. 17.158: Od. 24.515.

δηρός [δήν.] 1 Of time, long Il. 14.206 = 305. Absol.: ἐπὶ δηρόν Il. 9.415. 2 In neut. sing. δηρόν as adv., for a long time, for long, long: μένειν Il. 2.298. Cf. Il. 5.120, Il. 10.371, Il. 13.151, Il. 16.852, Il. 19.64, etc.: ἐσκοπίαζον Od. 10.260. Cf. Od. 1.203, Od. 2.285, Od. 5.396, Od. 16.171, Od. 21.112, etc.
δησάσκετο 3 sing. pa. iterative mid. δέω.
δῆσε1, 3 sing. aor. δέω.
δῆσε2, 3 sing. aor. δεύω2.
δῃωθείς contr. aor. pple. pass. δηϊόω.
δῃῶν contr. pres. pple. δηϊόω.
δῃώσειν contr. fut. infin. δηϊόω.

διά I Adv. 1 Through: διὰ δʼ ἔπτατʼ ὀϊστός Il. 5.99: διὰ τάφρον ὀρύξας (i.e. stretching in a line) Od. 21.120. Sim. κλέος διὰ ξεῖνοι φορέουσιν (through the lands they traverse) Od. 19.333. With ἀμπερές. See ἀμπερές. 2 Severing, sundering, splitting, dividing: διὰ κτῆσιν δατέοντο Il. 5.158. Cf. Il. 2.655, Il. 9.333, Il. 17.522, Il. 20.280, etc.: διὰ ξύλα κεάσσαι Od. 15.322. Cf. Od. 9.157, 291, etc. 3 Intensive: διὰ χρόα ἔδαψεν Il. 5.858. Cf. Il. 12.308, Il. 13.507, Il. 19.90, etc.: ἐπὴν σχεδίην διὰ κῦμα τινάξῃ Od. 5.363. II Prep. (sometimes, without anastrophe, following the case). 1 With genit. a Through, passing through, piercing: πέλεκυς, ὅς εἶσιν διὰ δουρός Il. 3.61. Cf. Il. 3.357, Il. 4.135, 481, Il. 5.113, etc.: κόρυθος διά Od. 24.523. Cf. Od. 22.16. With a form in -φι: διὰ στήθεσφιν Il. 22.284, Il. 5.41 = 57 = Il. 8.259 = Il. 11.448: = Od. 22.93. In reference to pain: ὀδύνη διὰ χροὸς ἦλθεν Il. 11.398. b Through, traversing or passing through (a space, a passage, a throng, or the like): αἰθέρος Il. 2.458, σκαιῶν Il. 3.263, προμάχων Il. 4.495. Cf. Il. 5.250, 503, Il. 6.226, Il. 7.340, Il. 9.478, etc.: Ὠκεανοῖο Od. 10.508, νηός Od. 12.206. Cf. Od. 10.118, 391, Od. 11.581, Od. 12.335, etc. With a form in -φι: διʼ ὄρεσφιν Il. 10.185. Of extension: σύες (ὕες) τανύοντο διὰ φλογός Il. 9.468 = Il. 23.33. Cf. Od. 9.298. Among: ἔπρεπε καὶ διὰ πάντων Il. 12.104. 2 With acc. a Through, passing through, piercing: ἔντεα Il. 23.806. Cf. Il. 7.247, Il. 20.269. b Through, traversing or passing through (a space, a passage, a throng, or the like) or among (objects): δώματα Il. 1.600, ἔντεα Il. 10.298, στόμα 375. Cf. Il. 8.343, Il. 11.118, Il. 12.62, Il. 17.283, Il. 23.122, etc.: σφέας Od. 7.40, ἄκριας Od. 10.281. Cf. Od. 2.154, Od. 6.50, Od. 9.447, Od. 10.150, etc. In reference to night regarded as a space: νύκτα διʼ ὀρφναίην Il. 10.83. Cf. Il. 2.57, Il. 8.510, Il. 24.363, 653, etc.: Od. 9.143, 404, Od. 12.284, etc. During (the night): διὰ νύκτα μάχεσθαι Il. 10.101. Cf. Od. 15.8, Od. 19.66. Of extension: διὰ κρατερὰς ὑσμίνας Il. 2.40. Cf. Od. 9.400. Among: πολέας διὰ κοιρανέοντα Il. 4.230. c Through, by means of, by virtue of, by the help or working of: μαντοσύνην Il. 1.72, ἰότητα Il. 15.41. Cf. Il. 10.497, Il. 15.71: βουλάς Od. 8.82, Ἀθήνην 520. Cf. Od. 11.276, 437, Od. 13.121, Od. 19.154, 523. d On account of, because of: κάλλος Od. 11.282, ἀτασθαλίας Od. 23.67.

διαβαίνω [δια- 3.] Aor. pple. διαβάς Il. 12.458. Infin. διαβήμεναι Od. 4.635. To pass over, cross. With acc.: τάφρον Il. 12.50. Absol., to cross over: ἐς Ἤλιδα Od. 4.635.–εὖ διαβάς, with the legs set well apartIl. 12.458.
διαγιγνώσκω [δια- 7.] Aor. infin. διαγνῶναι Il. 7.424. To distinguish, discern: ἄνδρα ἕκαστον Il. 7.424. Cf. Il. 23.240. Absol. Il. 23.470.
†διαγλάφω [δια- 10 + γλάφω = γλύφω, to cut out, carve. Cf. γλυφίς, γλαφυρός.] Fem. aor. pple. διαγλάψασα. To hollow out, form: εὐνὰς ἐν ψαμάθοισιν Od. 4.438.
†διάγω [δι-, δια- 3.] 3 pl. aor. διήγαγον. To convey across a strait: πορθμῆες Od. 20.187.
†διαδέρκομαι [δια- 10.] 3 sing. aor. opt. διαδράκοι. To catch sight of, see Il. 14.344.
διαδηλέομαι [δια- 10.] To do sore hurt to Od. 14.37.
διαδράκοι 3 sing. aor. opt. διαδέρκομαι.
διαδράμοι 3 sing. aor. opt. διατρέχω.

διαείδω [δια- 7.] 3 sing. fut. in mid. form διαείσεται Il. 8.535. 1 To distinguish, discern. In pass.: ἀρετὴ διαείδεται ἀνδρῶν Il. 13.277. 2 To learn the value of, know. With acc. and dependent clause: ἣν ἀρετήν, εἰ . . . (whether . . .) Il. 8.535.
διαεῖπον [δια- 9.] Contr. imp. δίειπε Il. 10.425. 1 To go through in talk: μῦθοι ἔσονται διαειπέμεν ἀλλήλοισιν Od. 4.215. 2 To tell fully, declare. Absol. Il. 10.425.
†διάημι [δι-, δια- 1.] 3 sing. impf. διάη. To blow through. With acc.: θάμνους Od. 5.478, λόχμην Od. 19.440.
διαθειόω [δια- 10 + θειόω = θεειόω.] To fumigate thoroughly with sulphur: μέγαρον Od. 22.494.
†διαθρύπτω [δια- 5 + θρύπτω, to break.] Nom. sing. neut. aor. pple. pass. διατρυφέν. To break in pieces, shiver: ξίφος διατρυφὲν ἔκπεσε χειρός Il. 3.363.
διαίνω 3 sing. aor. ἐδίηνε Il. 22.495. To wet, moisten Il. 13.30, Il. 21.202, Il. 22.495.
†διακείρω [δια- 10.] Aor. infin. διακέρσαι. To thwart, frustrate: ἐμὸν ἔπος Il. 8.8.
†διακλάω [δια- 5.] Aor. pple. διακλάσσας. To break in two: τόξα Il. 5.216.

διακοσμέω [δια- 6 10.] 1 To separate out and form into suitable bodies, marshal Il. 2.476. To divide up and form (into bodies): ἐς δεκάδας Il. 2.126. 2 To put in due order. In mid.: ἐπεὶ μέγαρον διεκοσμήσαντο Od. 22.457.
διακριδόν [διακρίνω.] Clearly, without doubt: δ. εἶναι ἄριστοι (ἄριστος) Il. 12.103, Il. 15.108.

†διακρίνω [δια- 6, δια- 7.] 3 sing. fut. διακρινέει Il. 2.387. 3 sing. aor. διέκρινε Od. 4.179. 3 pl. -αν Il. 17.531. 3 sing. subj. διακρίνῃ Il. 7.292, 378, 397. 3 pl. -ωσι Il. 2.475. 3 sing. opt. διακρίνειε Od. 8.195. Pass. Fut. infin. διακρινέεσθαι Od. 18.149, Od. 20.180. 3 pl. aor. διέκριθεν Il. 2.815. 2 pl. subj. διακρινθῆτε Od. 24.532. 2 pl. opt. διακρινθεῖτε Il. 3.102. Pple. διακρινθείς, -έντος Il. 7.306, Il. 20.141, 212. Infin. διακρινθήμεναι Il. 3.98. Nom. pl. fem. pf. pple. διακεκριμέναι Od. 9.220. 1 To separate out and form into suitable bodies, marshal Il. 2.815. To separate out, sort out: αἰπόλια αἰγῶν Il. 2.475. Cf. Od. 9.220. 2 To separate, part: ἡμέας Od. 4.179. Of combatants Il. 3.98, 102, Il. 7.292 = 378 = 397, Il. 7.306, Il. 17.531, Il. 20.141, 212: Od. 18.149, Od. 20.180, Od. 24.532. Sim.: μένος ἀνδρῶν Il. 2.387. 3 To distinguish, make out: τὸ σῆμα Od. 8.195.

διάκτορος -ου, ὁ [perh. fr. διακ-, lengthened fr. δι-α-, δι-, to run, as in δίεμαι.] Thus, the runner. Epithet or a name of Hermes Il. 2.103, Il. 21.497, Il. 24.339, 378 = 389 = 410 = 432, 445: Od. 1.84, Od. 5.43, 75, 94, 145, Od. 8.335, 338, Od. 12.390, Od. 15.319, Od. 24.99.
†διαλέγομαι [δια- 9 + λέγομαι, λέγω2.] 3 sing. aor. διελέξατο. To go through, debate: ταῦτα Il. 11.407 = Il. 17.97 = Il. 21.562 = Il. 22.122 = 385.
διαμάω (ᾰ) [app. fr. δια- 5 + ἀμάω1.] To cut through: διάμησε χιτῶνα Il. 3.359 = Il. 7.253.
διαμετρέω [δια- 10.] To measure off Il. 3.315.
διαμετρητός [διαμετρέω.] Measured off Il. 3.344.
διαμοιράομαι [δια- 10 + μοιράω, to divide, fr. μοῖρα.] To divide, apportion: ἕπταχα πάντα Od. 14.434.

διαμπερές [δι-, δια- 1 + ἀμπερές.] 1 Right through: βέλος ἐξέρυσε Il. 5.112 (i.e. in the direction of the arrow so as not to pull against the barbs), αἰχμὴ ἦλθεν 658. Cf. Il. 5.284, Il. 13.547. With genit.: ἀσπίδος Il. 12.429. Cf. Il. 20.362. Right through so as to make itself felt: οὐκ ὄμβρος περάασκεν Od. 5.480, Od. 19.442. 2 Continuously, without break or interval: πέτρη τετύχηκεν Od. 10.88. Cf. Il. 16.640: Od. 5.256–Continuously, all the way: θρόνοι ἐρηρέδατο Od. 7.96–Right round: σταυροὺς ἔλασσεν Od. 14.11. Cf. Il. 18.563. Right on: ἡγεμόνευε Od. 17.194. Cf. Il. 10.325. All together, in a mass Il. 12.398. Right through a company, in turn Il. 7.171. So as to meet, thoroughly: πόδας χεῖράς τε ἀποστρέψαντε Od. 22.190. 3 Of time, continuously, without intermission, break or interval Il. 10.89, 331, Il. 15.70, Il. 16.499, Il. 19.272, Il. 22.264: Od. 4.209, Od. 8.245, Od. 11.558, Od. 13.59, Od. 15.196, Od. 20.47, Od. 23.151. In intensive sense: ἔγχος κέ σε κατέπαυσε δ. (for good) Il. 16.618.
διάνδιχα [δι-, δια- 10 + ἄνδιχα.] 1 By halves Il. 9.37. 2 With divided mind: μερμήριξεν (was in two minds) Il. 1.189, Il. 13.455, (had half a mind) Il. 8.167.
†διανύω [δι-, δια- 10.] 3 sing. aor. διήνῦσε. To make an end. With pple.: κακότητʼ ἀγορεύων Od. 17.517.

†διαπέρθω [δια- 10.] 3 sing. aor. διέπερσε Od. 9.265. 1 pl. -αμεν Od. 3.130, Od. 11.533, Od. 13.316. 1 pl. subj. διαπέρσομεν Il. 9.46. Infin. διαπέρσαι Il. 4.53, 55. 1 pl. aor. διεπράθομεν Il. 1.367. 3 pl. -ον Od. 8.514. Infin. διαπραθέειν Il. 7.32, Il. 9.532, Il. 18.511. 3 sing. aor. pass. διεπράθετο Od. 15.384. To sack or ravage (a town) Il. 1.367, Il. 4.53, 55, Il. 7.32, Il. 9.46, 532, Il. 18.511: Od. 3.130 = Od. 13.316, Od. 8.514, Od. 9.265, Od. 11.533, Od. 15.384.
†διαπέτομαι [δια- 2.] 3 sing. aor. διέπτατο. 1 To traverse a space by flight Il. 15.83, 172. 2 To fly away through some opening Od. 1.320.
διαπλήσσω [δια- 5.] Aor. infin. διαπλῆξαι Od. 8.507. To split: δρῦς Il. 23.120. To split in pieces Od. 8.507.
διαπορθέω [δια- 10.] = διαπέρθω Il. 2.691.
διαπραθέειν aor. infin. διαπέρθω.

διαπρήσσω [δια- 10.] Aor. opt. διαπρήξαιμι Od. 14.197. 1 To traverse a space, pass, advance, make one's way: πεδίοιο (local genit., along the . . .) Il. 2.785 = Il. 3.14, Il. 23.364. To accomplish (a journey) Il. 1.483: = Od. 2.429, Od. 2.213. 2 To pass or spend (time) Il. 9.326. 3 To make an end. With pple.: λέγων ἐμὰ κήδεα Od. 14.197.

διαπρό [διά strengthened by πρό.] 1 Right through: ἤλυθʼ ἀκωκή Il. 5.66. Cf. Il. 5.538, Il. 7.260, Il. 12.184, Il. 13.388, Il. 20.276, Il. 21.164, etc.: Od. 22.295, Od. 24.524. With genit.: μίτρης Il. 4.138. Cf. Il. 5.281, Il. 14.494. 2 Through the whole extent: τάνυται Il. 17.393.
διαπρύσιον [app. conn. with διαμπερές.] 1 Of shouting, piercingly Il. 8.227 = Il. 11.275 = 586 = Il. 17.247, Il. 12.439 = Il. 13.149. 2 Without a break: πεδίοιο τετυχηκώς (on the . . .) Il. 17.748.
διαπτοιέω [δια- 10.] To terrify, scare Od. 18.340.
διαρπάζω [δι-, δια- 10.] To make prey of Il. 16.355.

διαρραίω [δια- 5.] Fut. infin. pass. διαρραίσεσθαι Il. 24.355. To dash in pieces, destroy, make an end of, bring to nought Il. 2.473, Il. 9.78, Il. 11.713, 733, Il. 17.727, Il. 24.355: Od. 1.251 = Od. 16.128, Od. 2.49, Od. 12.290.
†διαρρίπτω [δια- 1.] 3 sing. pa. iterative διαρρίπτασκε. To shoot (an arrow) through something Od. 19.575.

†διασεύω [δια- 1, δια- 2 3.] 3 sing. aor. mid. διέσσυτο. To speed or pass quickly through or across. With genit.: τάφροιο Il. 10.194: μεγάροιο Il. 22.460: Od. 4.37. Of a piercing weapon Il. 15.542. With acc.: λαόν Il. 2.450. Absol., of a weapon Il. 5.661.

†διασκεδάννυμι [δια- 4.] 3 sing. aor. διεσκέδασε Od. 5.369, 370, Od. 7.275. 3 sing. opt. διασκεδάσειε Od. 17.244. To scatter, disperse Od. 5.369, 370. To break up into its component parts and disperse these: σχεδίην Od. 7.275. To scatter to the winds, make an end of: ἀγλαΐας Od. 17.244.
διασκίδνημι = διασκεδάννυμι. To scatter, disperse: νέφεα Il. 5.526.
διασκοπιάομαι [δια- 7 10 + σκοπιάομαι fr. σκοπιή.] 1 To spy out Il. 10.388. 2 To distinguish, discern Il. 17.252.
διαστήτην 3 dual aor. διίστημι.
†διασχίζω [δια- 5.] 3 sing. aor. διέσχισε Od. 9.71. 3 sing. aor. pass. διεσχίσθη Il. 16.316. 1 To sever, rend: νεῦρα διεσχίσθη Il. 16.316. 2 To tear in pieces: ἱστία Od. 9.71.

†διατμήγω [δια- 5, δια- 6.] Aor. pple. διατμήξας Il. 21.3: Od. 3.291, Od. 5.409, Od. 12.174. Aor. διέτμαγον Od. 7.276. 3 pl. aor. pass. διέτμαγεν Il. 1.531, Il. 7.302, Il. 12.461, Il. 16.354: Od. 13.439. 1 To divide into two, sever Il. 21.3 (i.e. severing the fugitives into two bodies). So of ships sailing together and severed into two bodies by a storm Od. 3.291. 2 To cleave (the sea), traverse (it) Od. 5.409, Od. 7.276. 3 In pass., of two persons, to leave one another, part: ἐν φιλότητι διέτμαγεν Il. 7.302. Cf. Il. 1.531: = Od. 13.439. 4 To cut in pieces Od. 12.173. In pass., of the boards of a gate coming apart Il. 12.461. Of a scattered flock Il. 16.354.

data.ref: Il. 21.3 (i.e. severing the fugitives into two bodies).

definition: †διατρέχω [δια- 2.] 3 pl. aor. διέδραμον Od. 3.177. 3 sing. opt. διαδράμοι Od. 5.100. To run over, traverse. With acc.: κέλευθα Od. 3.177. Cf. Od. 5.100.
†διατρέω [δια- 4.] 3 pl. aor. διέτρεσαν. To flee in all directions: θῶες Il. 11.481, ἄλλυδις ἄλλος 486.

διατρίβω [δια- 10.] 1 To rub down into small fragments, crumble Il. 11.847. 2 To throw obstacles in the way of, put off, delay Od. 2.265, Od. 20.341. To thwart, oppose: τὸν ἐμὸν χόλον Il. 4.42. 3 To put off (a person). With double acc. of the person and of what is delayed: Ἀχαιοὺς ὃν γάμον Od. 2.204. 4 To put off time, loiter, delay Il. 19.150. With genit., to hold back from, delay in undertaking: ὁδοῖο Od. 2.404.
διατρύγιος [δια- 8 + τρύγη. See τρυγάω.] Bearing fruit through the seasons, never failing Od. 24.342.
διατρυφέν nom. sing. neut. aor. pple. pass. διαθρύπτω.
διαφαίνω [δια- 1 10.] In pass. 1 To appear or be seen through. With genit.: ὅθι νεκύων διεφαίνετο χῶρος Il. 8.491 = Il. 10.199. 2 To glow Od. 9.379.
†διαφθείρω [δια- 10.] 3 sing. fut. διαφθέρσει Il. 13.625. 2 sing. pf. διέφθορας Il. 15.128. 1 To destroy utterly: πόλιν Il. 13.625. 2 In pf., to have lost one's wits, be beside oneself Il. 15.128.
†διαφράζω [δια- 9.] 3 sing. aor. διεπέφραδε. To go through, say, tell Il. 20.340: Od. 17.590. Absol. Il. 18.9: Od. 6.47.
διαφύσσω [δι-, δια- 8 10.] 3 sing. aor. διήφυσε Od. 19.450. 1 To draw off (wine) in large quantities or constantly Od. 16.110. 2 To lay open or rend (flesh) (as if to draw off the life) Od. 19.450.
†διαχέω [δια- 5.] 3 pl. aor. διέχευαν. To dismember or divide into joints (a sacrificial victim) Il. 7.316: = Od. 19.421, Od. 3.456, Od. 14.427.

διδάσκω [redup. fr. δα-, δάω.] 3 sing. aor. (ἐ)δίδαξε Il. 5.51, Il. 11.832: Od. 8.481, 488. 1 pl. διδάξαμεν Od. 22.422. 3 pl. ἐδίδαξαν Il. 23.307. Pf. infin. pass. δεδιδάχθαι Il. 11.831. 1 To teach, instruct (a person) Il. 11.832, Il. 23.308: Od. 8.488. 2 To teach, impart knowledge of (something) Il. 9.442, Il. 23.307: Od. 22.422 (ἐργάζεσθαι complementary). 3 With double acc. of person and thing: σφέας οἴμας Od. 8.481. With infin. of what is taught: βάλλειν ἄγρια πάντα Il. 5.51. With acc. of person and this infin.: ὑψαγόρην σʼ ἔμεναι Od. 1.384. 4 In pass., to gain knowledge of, learn: φάρμακα δεδιδάχθαι (i.e. their properties) Il. 11.831. With genit.: διδασκόμενος πολέμοιο (concerning war, i.e. the art of war) Il. 16.811.
δίδημι [redup. fr. δε-, δέω.] = δέω 7 Il. 11.105: Od. 12.54.
διδυμάων [as δίδυμος.] Only in dual and pl. Twin: διδυμάονε παῖδε Il. 5.548, Il. 6.26.– (The) twins: Ὕπνῳ καὶ Θανάτῳ διδυμάοσιν Il. 16.672 = 682.
δίδυμος [redup. fr. δύο.] 1 Two, two (to one) Il. 23.641. 2 Double; αὐλοῖσιν Od. 19.227.

†δίδωμι [redup. fr. δο-.] 1 sing. pres. δίδωμι Il. 23.620: Od. 15.125, Od. 20.342. 2 sing. διδοῖς Il. 9.164. διδοῖσθα Il. 19.270. 3 sing. δίδωσι Il. 9.261, Il. 20.299, Il. 24.528: Od. 1.348, Od. 17.287, 474. διδοῖ Il. 9.519: Od. 4.237, Od. 17.350. 1 pl. δίδομεν Il. 2.228, Il. 21.297. 3 pl. διδοῦσι Il. 2.255, Il. 19.265: Od. 1.313, Od. 8.167, Od. 17.450, Od. 18.279. 2 pl. opt. διδοῖτε Od. 11.357. 3 pl. διδοῖεν Od. 18.142. 2 sing. impf. ἐδίδους Od. 19.367. 3 sing. (ἐ)δίδου Il. 5.165, Il. 6.192, Il. 7.305, etc.: Od. 8.63, 64, Od. 11.289, Od. 18.191, 323, Od. 22.236. 1 pl. δίδομεν Od. 8.545. 3 pl. δίδοσαν Od. 4.585, Od. 14.286, etc. Imp. δίδωθι Od. 3.380. δίδου Od. 3.58. Pple. διδούς, -όντος Il. 9.699: Od. 1.390, Od. 11.117, Od. 13.378. Infin. διδοῦναι Il. 24.425. Pa. iterative δόσκον Il. 9.331: Od. 17.420, Od. 19.76. 3 sing. δόσκε Il. 18.546. 3 pl. δόσκον Il. 14.382. Fut. δώσω Il. 8.166, Il. 14.238, Il. 19.144, etc.: Od. 2.223, Od. 4.589, Od. 16.80, etc. 2 sing. -εις Od. 19.167. 3 sing. -ει Il. 1.96, Il. 8.143, Il. 9.270, etc: Od. 2.135, Od. 14.444, Od. 17.11, etc. 3 pl. -ουσι Il. 1.123, 135, Il. 9.255, Il. 10.215, Il. 22.341: Od. 4.480, Od. 23.358. 1 pl. διδώσομεν Od. 13.358. Infin. δωσέμεναι Il. 10.393, Il. 13.369: Od. 4.7. -έμεν Il. 10.323, Il. 22.117. -ειν Il. 5.654, Il. 6.53, Il. 19.195, etc.: Od. 24.342. διδώσειν Od. 24.314. Aor. ἔδωκα Od. 9.361, Od. 15.373. δῶκα Il. 4.43: Od. 4.649, Od. 13.273, Od. 19.185, etc. 2 sing. ἔδωκας Il. 5.285, Il. 21.473, Il. 24.685: Od. 22.290, Od. 24.337. δῶκας Od. 4.647, Od. 8.415, Od. 24.340. 3 sing. ἔδωκε Il. 8.216, Il. 15.719, Il. 18.456, etc.: Od. 1.67, Od. 7.150, Od. 14.63, etc. δῶκε Il. 1.347, Il. 6.193, Il. 13.727, etc.: Od. 3.40, Od. 9.203, Od. 10.19, etc. 3 pl. ἔδωκαν Il. 13.303, Il. 22.379, Il. 23.745: Od. 8.440, Od. 13.369. δῶκαν Od. 6.215. 1 pl. aor. ἔδομεν Od. 24.65. δόμεν Il. 17.443. 3 pl. ἔδοσαν Il. 19.291: Od. 13.135, Od. 14.216, Od. 17.148, etc. δόσαν Il. 1.162, Il. 4.320, Il. 16.867, etc.: Od. 7.242, Od. 9.93, Od. 14.39, etc. Subj. δῶ Od. 9.356, Od. 20.296. 2 sing. δῷς Il. 7.27. 3 sing. δώῃσι Il. 1.324, Il. 12.275. δώῃ Il. 6.527, Il. 8.287, Il. 16.88, etc.: Od. 12.216, Od. 18.87, Od. 21.338, etc. δῷσι Il. 1.129: Od. 1.379, Od. 2.144. 1 pl. δώομεν Il. 7.299, 351: Od. 16.184. δῶμεν Il. 23.537: Od. 8.389, Od. 13.13. 3 pl. δώωσι Il. 1.137, Il. 9.136, 278. δῶσι Il. 3.66. Opt. δοίην Od. 7.314, Od. 15.449, Od. 18.361. 2 sing. δοίης Il. 16.625: Od. 4.600, Od. 9.268, Od. 17.223, 455. 3 sing. δοίη Il. 9.379, 385, Il. 17.127, 562, etc.: Od. 2.54, Od. 6.144, Od. 9.229, etc. 1 pl. δοῖμεν Il. 13.378: Od. 2.336, Od. 16.386. 3 pl. δοῖεν Il. 1.18, Il. 19.264, Il. 23.650, Il. 24.686: Od. 6.180, Od. 7.148, Od. 8.411, 413, Od. 15.316, Od. 24.402. Imp. δός Il. 1.338, Il. 5.359, Il. 16.524, etc.: Od. 3.46, Od. 6.178, Od. 9.355, etc. 3 sing. δότω Il. 2.383, Il. 11.798, Il. 14.377, Il. 18.301: Od. 7.166. 2 pl. δότε Il. 6.476: Od. 2.212, Od. 6.209, Od. 21.281, etc. Fem. pple. δοῦσα Od. 15.369. Nom. pl. masc. δόντες Il. 1.299: Od. 5.38, Od. 23.341. Infin. δόμεναι Il. 1.98, Il. 4.380, Il. 9.120, etc.: Od. 1.317, Od. 9.518, Od. 17.417, etc. δόμεν Il. 4.379, Il. 9.571, Il. 18.458, 508: Od. 17.404. δοῦναι Il. 11.319, Il. 15.216, Il. 23.593: Od. 1.292, 316. 3 sing. aor. opt. pass. δοθείη Od. 2.78. 3 sing. pf. δέδοται Il. 5.428. (ἀπο-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, περι-.) 1 To make another the owner of, give, present: τόξον ἔδωκεν Il. 2.827, δῶρα δίδωσι (offers) Il. 9.261. Cf. Il. 2.102, Il. 5.272, Il. 6.219, Il. 7.299, etc.: τάλαρον ἔδωκεν Od. 4.125, ἕδνα διδόντες (offering) Od. 11.117. Cf. Od. 1.313, 316, Od. 2.336, etc. In reference to something immaterial: τιμῆς ἥμισυ Il. 6.193. To assign (a share of spoil) Il. 1.162, Il. 2.228, Il. 9.334, etc. To make over one's rights in: ἑπτὰ πτολίεθρα Il. 9.149, 291. 2 To give as a reward or prize: δύω χρυσοῖο τάλαντα Il. 18.508. Cf. Il. 10.305, Il. 23.537, 551, 560, 616, 620, 807, etc. 3 To offer (a sacrifice): θεοῖς ἑκατόμβας Il. 7.450 = Il. 12.6. Cf. Od. 1.67, Od. 16.184, Od. 19.367. Sim. δῶρα θεοῖσιν Il. 20.299. Cf. Il. 24.425: Od. 13.358. 4 To give (food or drink), put (food or drink) before a person: δέπας οἴνου Il. 18.546: ξεινήϊα Od. 3.490. Cf. Od. 6.209, Od. 7.166, Od. 9.93, etc. To see to the due providing of (a meal): δεῖπνον ἑταίροισιν Od. 10.155. Of feeding horses Il. 2.383. Of an eagle feeding its young Il. 12.222. 5 To pay (a price) Od. 1.431, Od. 15.388 = 429, 449. To pay (ransom) Il. 21.41, 42, Il. 22.341, Il. 23.746, Il. 24.594, 685, 686. To make over (as compensation): ἵππους υἶος ποινήν Il. 5.266. To pay as bride-price Il. 11.243, 244. To give (μείλια) Il. 9.147, 289. 6 To give in marriage: θυγατέρα ἥν Il. 6.192 = Il. 11.226. Cf. Il. 13.369, 378, Il. 14.268, 275, Il. 19.291: Od. 1.292, Od. 2.54, 223, Od. 4.7, Od. 11.289, Od. 15.367. 7 To give or confer (something immaterial): μέγʼ εὖχος Il. 5.285: γέρας Od. 7.150. Cf. Il. 5.654 = Il. 11.445, Il. 16.625, Il. 21.473. Sim.: δαίμονά τοι δώσω (will deal thee . . .) Il. 8.166: γαστὴρ πολλὰ κακὰ δίδωσιν Od. 17.287, 474. To give or utter (an oath) Od. 19.302. 8 To resign one's claims to: ἵππον Il. 23.553, 592, 610. 9 To give the use of, lend: φάσγανον Il. 10.255. Cf. Il. 5.359, 363, Il. 10.260, Il. 11.798, etc.: νῆα Od. 2.212 = Od. 4.669. Cf. Od. 3.369, Od. 4.647, 649, Od. 5.234, 237, Od. 6.144, 178, etc. To give the services of: ἐπικούρους Il. 4.379, 380: Od. 2.212 = Od. 4.669. To give as a servant or slave Od. 17.223, 442. 10 To give, commit, hand over, for some purpose: σάκος χείρονι φωτί Il. 14.377. Cf. Il. 1.324, Il. 2.205, Il. 9.331, Il. 15.455, Il. 17.127, Il. 21.84, etc.: ἄλεισον Od. 3.50. Cf. Od. 3.40, 437, Od. 5.351, Od. 10.33, Od. 14.112, Od. 21.233, etc. Sim.: ὀδύνῃσί μιν (μʼ) ἔδωκεν Il. 5.397: Od. 17.567, ἀχέεσσί με δώσεις Od. 19.167. With infin. expressing the purpose: δός σφωϊν [κούρην] ἄγειν Il. 1.338. Cf. Il. 5.26, Il. 6.53, Il. 7.471, Il. 11.704, Il. 16.40, etc.: δὸς τούτῳ δέπας σπεῖσαι Od. 3.46. Cf. Od. 18.87, Od. 20.78. To give (the hand) Il. 23.75. To commit (to the flames) Od. 24.65. 11 Of a divine power a To give, grant, bestow, as a boon or in answer to prayer: ναύτῃσιν οὖρον Il. 7.4. Cf. Il. 1.178, Il. 3.66, Il. 4.320, Il. 9.38, etc.: ἐπιφροσύνην Od. 5.437. Cf. Od. 2.116, Od. 3.58, Od. 4.237, Od. 7.148, Od. 8.44, etc. b To send or afflict with (something evil): ἄλγεα Il. 1.96. Cf. Il. 2.375, Il. 9.571, Il. 19.264, 270, Il. 24.241, etc.: ἄτην Od. 4.262. Cf. Od. 2.135, Od. 4.237, Od. 7.242, Od. 14.39, etc. c With infin., to empower or permit to do something, grant a person's doing it or its being done: ἐκπέρσαι πόλιν Il. 1.18, τὸν δῦναι δόμον Ἄϊδος Il. 3.322. Cf. Il. 1.129, Il. 5.118, Il. 6.307, Il. 7.203, Il. 17.646, etc.: παλίντιτα ἔργα γενέσθαι Od. 1.379, ἄλοχον ἰδέειν Od. 8.411. Cf. Od. 3.60, Od. 6.327, Od. 7.110, Od. 12.216, Od. 22.253, etc. To appoint as one's lot: τολυπεύειν πολέμους Il. 14.86. d Absol.: διάνδιχα δῶκε κρόνου πάϊς Il. 9.37. Cf. Il. 22.285, Il. 24.529: Διός γε διδόντος Od. 1.390. Cf. Od. 1.348, Od. 7.35, Od. 19.396. 12 Absol., to accede to one's wishes: σοὶ δῶκα ἑκὼν ἀέκοντί γε θυμῷ Il. 4.43. 13 To restore (cf. 14.a 14.b): κτήματα Il. 7.364. Cf. Il. 7.391, 393, Il. 11.125, Il. 22.117. 14 Uses with adverbs. a With ἀπό, to restore(cf. (13)): πρίν γʼ ἀπὸ πατρὶ δόμεναι κούρην Il. 1.98. To make up for, give compensation for: πρίν γʼ ἀπὸ πᾶσαν ἐμοὶ δόμεναι λώβην Il. 9.387. Cf. Od. 2.78. b With πάλιν, to restore(cf. (13)) Il. 1.116, Il. 7.79 = Il. 22.342, Il. 22.259.

data.quote: σοὶ δῶκα ἑκὼν ἀέκοντί γε θυμῷ
πρίν γʼ ἀπὸ πατρὶ δόμεναι κούρην
πρίν γʼ ἀπὸ πᾶσαν ἐμοὶ δόμεναι λώβην

definition: διέδραμον 3 pl. aor. διατρέχω.
διεέργω [δι-, δια- 6.] To keep apart, separate Il. 12.424.
δίειπε contr. imp. διαεῖπον.
διείπομεν 1 pl. impf. διέπω.
διείρομαι [δι-, δια- 9.] To ask about at length; or simply, to ask about Il. 1.550. With double acc. (cf. εἴρομαι 4): ταῦτά με Il. 15.93: Od. 4.492, Od. 11.463, Od. 24.478.

διέκ [διά strengthened by ἐκ.] Right through; or simply, through. With genit.: προθύρου Il. 15.124. Cf. Od. 10.388, Od. 17.61, 460, Od. 18.101, 185 = Od. 19.503 = Od. 22.433, Od. 18.386, Od. 19.47 = Od. 20.144, Od. 21.299.
διέκριθεν 3 pl. aor. pass. διακρίνω.

†διελαύνω [δι-, δια- 1, δια- 3] 3 sing. aor. διήλασε. 1 To drive (horses, etc.) across something Il. 12.120 (across the ditch). To drive them across. With genit.: τάφροιο Il. 10.564. 2 To drive or thrust (a weapon) through. With genit.: λαπάρης ἔγχος Il. 16.318. To drive or thrust a weapon through. With genit.: ἀσπίδος Il. 13.161.
διελέξατο 3 sing. aor. διαλέγομαι.
διελεύσεσθαι fut. infin. διέρχομαι.
διελθέμεν aor. infin. διέρχομαι.

δίεμαι [cf. δίον2, διώκω.] Aor. sub. δίωμαι Od. 21.370. 3 sing. δίηται Il. 7.197, Il. 15.681, Il. 16.246, Il. 22.189, 456. 3 pl. δίωνται Il. 17.110. 3 sing. opt. δίοιτο Od. 17.317. (ἀπο-, ἐνδίημι.) 1 To chase, pursue Il. 22.189: Od. 17.317 2 To chase away, drive off or away: λῖν Il. 17.110. Cf. Il. 12.276, Il. 18.162, Il. 22.456: Od. 21.370. Sim.: ἀπὸ ναῦφι μάχην Il. 16.246. To cause to retire, put to flight Il. 7.197. 3 To send or chase away, dismiss: ξεῖνον ἀπὸ μεγάροιο Od. 17.398. Cf. Od. 20.343. 4 To drive (horses) Il. 15.681. 5 As pass. a To be driven off or away Il. 12.304. b Of horses, to be driven, race Il. 23.475.
†διέξειμι [δι-, δια- 1 + ἐξ- 1 + εἶμι.] Infin. (in fut. sense) διεξίμεναι. To pass through and emerge from something: πύλας, τῇ ἔμελλε διεξίμεναι πεδίονδε Il. 6.393.
διεξερέομαι [δι-, δια- 9, ἐξ- 9.] To question closely about. With double acc.: ἐμὲ ταῦτα Il. 10.432.
διεξίμεναι infin. διέξειμι.
διέπερσε 3 sing. aor. διαπέρθω.
διεπέφραδε 3 sing. aor. διαφράζω.
διέπραθον 3 pl. aor. διαπέρθω.
διέπτατο 3 sing. aor. διαπέτομαι.

διέπω [δι-, δια- 10 + ἕπω1.] 1 To bring into order or under control: στρατόν Il. 2.207. Cf. Il. 24.247. 2 To carry on, manage Il. 1.166. To attend to, carry through: τὰ ἕκαστα Od. 12.16. To attend to, arrange, settle Il. 11.706.
†διερέσσω [δι-, δια- 2.] Aor. διήρεσ(σ)α. To row or propel oneself in the water through a space Od. 12.444 (through the strait), Od. 14.351 (through the water between the ship and the shore).
διερός 1 App., living: βροτός Od. 6.201. 2 App., nimble: ποδί Od. 9.43.

διέρχομαι [δι-, δια- 1, δια- 2.] Fut. infin. διελεύσεσθαι Il. 13.144, Il. 20.263. 3 sing. aor. διῆλθε Il. 23.876: Od. 19.453. 3 pl. opt. διέλθοιεν Il. 10.492. Infin. διελθέμεν Il. 20.100, Il. 24.716: Od. 6.304. 1 Of a weapon, to pierce its way Il. 20.263, Il. 23.876: Od. 19.453. To pierce or pass through. With genit.: χροός Il. 20.100. 2 To pass through or traverse a space: ὅπως ἵπποι ῥεῖα διέλθοιεν Il. 10.492. Cf. Il. 24.716. To pass through or traverse. With genit.: μεγάροιο Od. 6.304. With acc.: ἄστυ Il. 6.392. Cf. Il. 3.198, Il. 13.144.
διεσκέδασε 3 sing. aor. διασκεδάννυμι.
διέσσυτο 3 sing. aor. mid. διασεύω.
διέσταμεν 1 pl. pf. διίστημι.
διέστησαν 3 pl. aor. διίστημι.
διέσχε 3 sing. aor. διέχω.
διέσχισε 3 sing. aor. διεσχίσθη, 3 sing. aor. pass. διασχίζω.
διέτμαγον aor. διατμήγω.
διέτρεσαν 3 pl. aor. διατρέω.
διέφθορας 2 sing. pf. διαφθείρω.
διέχευαν 3 pl. aor. διαχέω.
†διέχω [δι-, δια- 1.] 3 sing. aor. διέσχε. To pass through, hold its way: [ὀϊστός] Il. 5.100. Cf. Il. 11.253, Il. 20.416.

δίζημαι [prob. a non-thematic redup. pres. = ζητέω.] 2 sing. δίζηαι Od. 11.100. 1 pl. aor. subj. διζησόμεθα Od. 16.239. 1 To seek for, try to find (a person or a strayed animal): πάνδαρον Il. 4.88. Cf. Il. 5.168, Il. 10.84, Il. 13.760: ἵππους Od. 21.22. Cf. Od. 15.90. To seek out, try to get the help of: ἄλλους Od. 16.239. 2 To seek after, try to acquire or have: φάρμακον Od. 1.261. Cf. Il. 17.221. To strive after, seek to achieve: νόστον Od. 11.100, Od. 23.253. 3 To seek in marriage, woo Od. 16.391 = Od. 21.161.
δίζυξ -υγος [δι-, δισ- + ζυγόν.] Yoked, or meant to be yoked, in pairs: ἵπποι Il. 5.195, Il. 10.473.
δίζω [prob. thematic form answering to δίζημαι.] To be in doubt, hesitate: ἠὲ . . . ἦ . . . Il. 16.713.
διήγαγον 3 pl. aor. διάγω.
διηκόσιοι [δι-, δισ- + ἑκατόν.] Two hundred Il. 9.383. Absol. Il. 8.233.
διήλασε 3 sing. aor. διελαύνω.
διῆλθε 3 sing. aor. διέρχομαι.
διηνεκέως [adv. fr. διηνεκής.] Right through, at length: ἀγορεῦσαι Od. 7.241. Fully, plainly, in detail Od. 4.836, Od. 12.56.

διηνεκής [δι-, δια- 8 + ἐνεκ-. See φέρω.] Carried straight through, straight: ὦλκα Od. 18.375. Without break or obstruction: ἀτραπιτοί Od. 13.195. Continuous: νώτοισιν (slices cut the whole length of the back) Il. 7.321: Od. 14.437–Thrown out far, far-stretching: ῥίζῃσιν Il. 12.134. Carried right round: ῥάψε ῥάβδοισι διηνεκέσιν περὶ κύκλον Il. 12.297.
διήνυσε 3 sing. aor. διανύω.
διήρεσα (σσ) aor. διερέσσω.
δίηται 3 sing. aor. subj. δίεμαι.
διήφυσε 3 sing. aor. διαφύσσω.
†διικνέομαι [δι-, δια- 9.] Fut. διίξομαι Il. 9.61. 2 sing. aor. διίκεο Il. 19.186. To go through in speaking: πάντα Il. 9.61, Il. 19.186.

διιπετής [app. fr. διί, dat. of. Ζεύς + πε-, πίπτω.] Thus, falling in the sky, i.e. rain-fed; or poss., falling by the power or ordinance of Zeus. Epithet of rivers Il. 16.174, Il. 17.263, Il. 21.268, 326: Od. 4.477, 581, Od. 7.284.

διΐστημι [δι-, δια- 6.] 3 dual aor. διαστήτην Il. 1.6, Il. 16.470. 3 pl. διέστησαν Il. 24.718. Nom. pl. masc. pple. διαστάντες Il. 12.86, Il. 17.391. 1 pl. pf. διέσταμεν Il. 21.436. 1 In aor. and mid. a To stand apart or aside: διαστάντες (severing, parting, i.e. in order to form themselves into bodies) Il. 12.86, τὼ [ἵππω] διαστήτην (wheeled apart, i.e. with their hind quarters) Il. 16.470, διαστάντες (taking their stand at (regular) intervals) Il. 17.391, διέστησαν καὶ εἶξαν ἀπήνῃ (stood aside, parted this way and that) Il. 24.718. b Of the sea, to part, be cleft Il. 13.29. c To come into variance, quarrel Il. 1.6. 2 In pf., to have one's stand, stand, apart: τίη διέσταμεν; (why do we not come to close quarters ?) Il. 21.436.

διΐφιλος [Διί, dat. of Ζεύς + φίλος. Prob. better written thus than Διὶ φίλος. Cf. διιπετής, which is clearly a compound.] Dear to Zeus, favoured by Zeus Il. 1.74, 86, Il. 2.628, Il. 6.318, Il. 8.493, 517, Il. 9.168, Il. 10.49, 527, Il. 11.419, 473, 611, Il. 13.674, Il. 16.169, Il. 18.203, Il. 22.216, Il. 24.472.

δικάζω [δίκη.] Fut. δικάσω Il. 23.579. 3 pl. aor. δίκασαν Od. 11.547. Imp. pl. δικάσσατε Il. 23.574. 1 To pronounce judgment, give a decision Il. 18.506, Il. 23.574, 579: Od. 11.547. 2 To form a decision, come to a resolve Il. 1.542, Il. 8.431 (lay down the law for . . .). 3 In mid., to seek a judgment or decision, plead one's cause Od. 11.545, Od. 12.440.

δίκαιος [δίκη.] 1 Conforming to the traditional order of society, observing the usages common to civilized men, civilized Od. 6.120 = Od. 9.175 = Od. 13.201, Od. 8.575. In superl. δικαιότατος Il. 11.832, Il. 13.6. 2 Mindful of the usages of courtesy, well-bred Od. 3.52. 3 Acting with due regard to what is right, upright, honourable Od. 2.282, Od. 3.133, Od. 13.209. In comp. δικαιότερος Il. 19.181. 4 Absol. in neut. δίκαιον, something right or proper: ἐπὶ ῥηθέντι δικαίῳ (when the right word has been spoken) Od. 18.414 = Od. 20.322.–οὐ δ. with infin., (it is) not right or proper to: ἀτέμβειν Od. 20.294, Od. 21.312.
δικαίως [adv. fr. δίκαιος.] In due or proper wise Od. 14.90.
δικασπόλος [δίκας, acc. pl. of δίκη + -πολος, conn. with πολεύω.] Busied about judgments, administering justice Il. 1.238: Od. 11.186.

δίκη -ης, ἡ. 1 Custom, usage, way: βασιλήων Od. 4.691. Cf. Od. 18.275, Od. 19.43. With notion of privilege: γερόντων Od. 24.255. Applied to a mode of existence or action imposed from without: δμώων Od. 14.59. Cf. Od. 11.218. Something that always happens in specified circumstances Od. 19.168. 2 Right, justice Il. 16.388, Il. 19.180: Od. 14.84. In pl., rules of right, principles of justice: οὐ δίκας εἰδότα οὐδὲ θέμιστας (having no regard for justice or the usages of (civilized) men; see εἴδω III.12) Od. 9.215. Cf. Od. 3.244. 3 A judgement or doom: ὃς λυκίην εἴρυτο δίκῃσιν (by his (impartial) administration of justice) Il. 16.542. Cf. Il. 18.508. 4 A plea of right, a claim: δίκας εἴροντο (were asking questions about their . . ., seeking decisions in regard to them) Od. 11.570. Cf. Il. 23.542.
δικλίς -ίδος [δι-, δισ- + κλίνω.] Of gates or doors, double: πύλας δικλίδας Il. 12.455. Cf. Od. 2.345, Od. 17.268.
δίκτυον -ου, τό. A fishing-net Od. 22.386.

δινεύω [δίνη.] 3 sing. pa. iterative δινεύεσκε Il. 24.12. 1 To turn (one's team) this way and that Il. 18.543. 2 To whirl oneself about, spin round. Of acrobats Il. 18.606: = Od. 4.19. Of a bird, to circle or wheel in flight Il. 23.875. 3 To wander, rove, roam. Il. 4.541, Il. 24.12: Od. 19.67.

δινέω [as δινεύω.] (ἀμφι-, ἐπι-.) 1 To whirl round (before throwing): δόλον Il. 23.840. To cause to revolve: μοχλόν Od. 9.384, 388. 2 To whirl oneself about, spin round. Of dancers Il. 18.494. 3 In pass. a To go in a circle: πόλιν πέρι δινηθήτην Il. 22.165. b To wander, rove, roam Od. 9.153, Od. 16.63. c Of the eyes, to be turned in various directions, wander Il. 17.680.
δίνη -ης, ἡ. An eddy or whirlpool (in a river) Il. 21.11, 132, 213, 239, 246, 353: Od. 6.116.

δινήεις -εντος [δίνη.] Eddying, whirling. Epithet of rivers. Of the Lycian Xanthus Il. 2.877, Il. 5.479. Of the Trojan Xanthus (Scamander) Il. 8.490, Il. 14.434 = Il. 21.2 = Il. 24.693, Il. 21.125, 206, 332, Il. 22.148. Of other rivers Il. 20.392: Od. 6.89, Od. 11.242.

δινωτός -ή, -όν [δινόω fr. δῖνος = δίνη.] (Cf. ἀμφιδινέω.) 1 App., adorned with inlaid circles or spirals of a precious material Il. 3.391: Od. 19.56. 2 App., ornamented with rings or round pieces of specified materials Il. 13.407.

διογενής [Δι-ο-, fr. Δι- of oblique cases of Ζεύς + γεν-, γίγνομαι.] Sprung from Zeus. Epithet of heroes Il. 1.337, 489, Il. 2.173, Il. 4.489, Il. 9.106, Il. 11.810, Il. 23.294, etc. In Od. always of Odysseus Od. 2.352, Od. 5.203, Od. 8.3, Od. 10.443, etc.
Διόθεν [Δι-ο- as in διογενής. + -θεν 1.] 1 From, sent by, Zeus Il. 24.194, 561. 2 By his power or will Il. 15.489.

διοϊστεύω [δι-, δια- 1, δια- 2.] 1 To shoot an arrow through. With genit.: πελέκεων Od. 19.578 = Od. 21.76. Cf. Od. 19.587, Od. 21.97 = 127, Od. 21.114. 2 To shoot an arrow over an indicated space Od. 12.102.
δίοιτο 3 sing. aor. opt. δίεμαι.
†διόλλυμι [δι-, δια- 10.] 3 sing. pf. διόλωλε. To go to ruin: οἶκος ἐμὸς διόλωλε Od. 2.64.
δίον1, aor. [δϝι-, δείδοικα.] To be afraid Il. 5.566, Il. 9.433, Il. 11.557. With μή and opt. Il. 17.666: Od. 22.96.
δίον2 aor. [Cf. δίεμαι.] To flee, run Il. 22.251.
διοπτεύω [δι-, δια- 10 + ὀπτεύω fr. ὀπ-. See ὁράω.] (ἐποπτεύω.) To act the spy Il. 10.451.
διοπτήρ -ῆρος, ὁ [cf. διοπτεύω.] A spy Il. 10.562.

δῖος δῖα, δῖον [δι- of oblique cases of Zeus.] 1 Of Zeus: δῖον γένος Il. 9.538 (= Διὸς κούρη 536). 2 a Bright, shining. Of the sea Il. 1.141, Il. 2.152, Il. 14.76, etc.: Od. 3.153, Od. 4.577, Od. 5.261, etc. Of rivers (or perh. rather = διιπετής) Il. 2.522, Il. 12.21. Of the dawn Il. 9.240, Il. 11.723, Il. 18.255, etc.: Od. 9.151, Od. 11.375, Od. 16.368, etc. Of the αἰθήρ Il. 16.365: Od. 19.540. Of the earth Il. 14.347, Il. 24.532. b α Of goddesses, bright, resplendent, glorious Il. 2.820, Il. 3.389, 413, Il. 5.370, Il. 10.290 (here, of Athene, perh. rather in sense (1), = Διὸς τέκος 284): Od. 5.263, 321, 372, Od. 12.133, Od. 20.68, 73. Applied to Charybdis Od. 12.104, 235. β With superl. sense: δῖα θεάων, bright, etc., among goddesses(partitive genit.), brightest, etc., of goddesses (cf. 3.b.β) Il. 5.381, Il. 6.305, Il. 14.184, etc.: Od. 1.14, Od. 4.382, Od. 10.400, etc. 3 An epithet of general commendation. a Of men, noble, illustrious, goodly, or the like Il. 1.7, 145, Il. 2.57, 221, Il. 3.329, Il. 4.319, Il. 5.211, Il. 6.31, Il. 10.285, Il. 14.3, Il. 17.705, Il. 24.618, etc.: Od. 1.196, 284, 298, Od. 3.439, Od. 4.655, Od. 11.168, 522, Od. 14.3, Od. 21.240, etc. Sim. of peoples or bodies of men: Ἀχαιοί Il. 5.451. Cf. Il. 10.429, Il. 11.455, 504, Il. 18.241, Il. 20.354: Od. 3.116, Od. 19.177, 199. b α Of women, noble, queenly, or the like Il. 5.70, Il. 6.160, Il. 17.40: Od. 3.266. β With superl. sense: δῖα γυναικῶν, pearl of women(cf. 2.b.β) Il. 2.714, Il. 3.171, 228, 423: Od. 1.332, Od. 4.305, Od. 20.147, etc. c Of horses, noble, well-bred, or the like Il. 8.185, Il. 23.346 (here perh. rather in sense (1), divine ; cf. 347). d Of cities, etc., famed, rich, or the like Il. 2.615, 836, Il. 11.686, 698, Il. 21.43: Od. 3.326, Od. 4.313, 702 = Od. 5.20, Od. 13.275, 440, Od. 15.298, Od. 17.121, Od. 24.431.

data.ref: Il. 10.290 (here, of Athene, perh. rather in sense (1), =

definition: διοτρεφής [δι-ο- (cf. διογενής) + τρέφω.] Nourished or cherished by Zeus. Epithet of kings, chiefs, etc. Il. 1.176, Il. 2.660, Il. 5.463, Il. 7.109, Il. 11.648, etc.: Od. 3.480, Od. 4.26, Od. 5.378, Od. 7.49, Od. 22.136, etc. Absol. in voc. Il. 9.229, Il. 17.685, Il. 21.75, etc.: Od. 4.391, Od. 10.266, 419, Od. 15.155, 199, Od. 24.122.

δίπλαξ -ακος [δι-, δισ-. For the second element cf. διπλόος.] 1 Double, applied in two layers: δημῷ Il. 23.243. Cf. Il. 23.253. 2 As fem. sb., a χλαῖνα intended to be worn double Il. 3.126, Il. 22.441: Od. 19.241.

διπλόος [δι-, δισ-. For the second element cf. ἁ-πλοΐς and δίπλαξ.] Contr. acc. sing. fem. διπλῆν Il. 10.134: Od. 19.226. 1 Worn double: χλαῖναν Il. 10.134: Od. 19.226. 2 Of the θώρηξ, consisting of two plates: ὅθι ζωστῆρος ὀχῆες σύνεχον καὶ δ. ἤντετο θώρηξ Il. 4.133 = Il. 20.415 (i.e. where the two plates met (and overlapped) at the sides. But there is great confusion in these passages. The belt would naturally be fastened in front, not at the side; and in Il. 20 the wound is behind).

data.ref: Il. 20.415 (i.e. where the two plates met (and overlapped) at the sides. But there is great confusion in these passages. The belt would naturally be fastened in front, not at the side; and in

data.quote: ὅθι ζωστῆρος ὀχῆες σύνεχον καὶ δ. ἤντετο θώρηξ

definition: δίπτυχος -ον [δι-, δισ- + πτυχ-, πτύξ.] From δίπτυξ acc. sing. fem. δίπτυχα (cf. ὑπόβρυξ). 1 Worn double: δίπυχον λώπην Od. 13.224. 2 In a double fold: δίπτυχα [κνίσην] ποιήσαντες (i.e. folding it with a double fold so as to enclose the sacrificial joints) Il. 1.461 = Il. 2.424: = Od. 3.458 = Od. 12.361.
δίς [δύο.] Twice: δὶς τόσσον Od. 9.491.
δισθανής [δισ- + θαν-, θνῄσκω.] Dying twice Od. 12.22 (i.e. with a second death to face).

data.ref: Od. 12.22 (i.e. with a second death to face).

definition: δισκέω [δίσκος.] To engage in a contest of throwing the δίσκος: ἀλλήλοισιν (with . . . ) Od. 8.188.
δίσκος -ου, ὁ. A mass of stone for distance-throwing as a trial of strength or skill Il. 23.431, Il. 2.774: = Od. 4.626 = Od. 17.168, Od. 8.129, 186.
δίσκουρα τά Il. 23.523 = δίσκου οὖρα. See οὖρον 3.
διφάω To seek for, search for Il. 16.747.

δίφρος -ου, ὁ [contr. fr. διφόρος fr. δι-, δισ- + -φορος, φέρω. Something that carries two, i. e. (in war) the ἡνίοχος and the παραιβάτης.] 1 a A chariot, whether used in war, for racing, for travel or for conveyance in general (hardly to be distinguished from ἅρμα) Il. 3.262, 310, Il. 5.20, Il. 13.392, Il. 23.335, 370, Il. 24.322, etc.: Od. 3.324, 369, 481, 483, Od. 4.590, Od. 14.280. b The platform thereof, composed of straps plaited and strained tight Il. 5.727. 2 A seat (the notion of two app. lost) Il. 3.424, Il. 6.354, Il. 24.578: Od. 4.717, Od. 17.330, Od. 19.97, Od. 20.259, etc.

δίχα [δι-, δίς.] 1 In two: δ. ἑταίρους ἠρίθμεον (into two bodies) Od. 10.203, δ. δφισὶ πάντα δέδασται (between them) Od. 15.412. 2 In two ways: δ. σφισὶν ἥνδανε βουλή (they were divided in opinion) Il. 18.510: Od. 3.150, βάζομεν (in disagreement, at variance) Od. 3.127. So of favouring different sides, taking different parts: δ. θυμὸν ἔχοντες Il. 20.32. Cf. Il. 21.386. Of doubt or hesitation: δ. μερμήριζεν (was in two minds) Od. 22.333. Cf. Od. 16.73, Od. 19.524.
διχθά [as δίχα.] 1 = δίχα. (1) Od. 1.23 (into two tribes). 2 = δίχα. (2). Of doubt, etc. Il. 16.435.
διχθάδιος -η, -ον [διχθά.] 1 Two (and different): κῆρας Il. 9.411. 2 In neut. pl. διχθάδια as adv. = δίχα 2. Of doubt, etc. Il. 14.21.
διψάω [δίψα.] To be athirst: διψάων (in (his) thirst) Od. 11.584.
†διωθέω [δι-, δια- 5.] 3 sing. aor. διῶσε. To tear asunder, rend: κρημνὸν [πτελέη] διῶσεν Il. 21.244.

διώκω [cf. δίεμαι.] 3 dual impf. διώκετον Il. 10.364. 1 To chase, pursue Il. 5.65, 672, Il. 8.339, Il. 10.359, 364, Il. 13.64, Il. 16.598, Il. 17.463, Il. 21.3, 601, Il. 22.8, 157, 158, 168, 173, 199, 200, 230: Od. 15.278. In mid. Il. 21.602. Absol.: διωκέμεν ἠδὲ φέβεσθαι Il. 5.223 = Il. 8.107. 2 To send away, chase away Od. 18.409. In mid. Od. 18.8. 3 To pursue, seek to win: ἀκίχητα Il. 17.75. 4 To drive (a chariot) Il. 8.439. Absol. Il. 23.344, 424, 499, 547. 5 Of a wind, to drive (a vessel) Od. 5.332. 6 Of rowers, to propel (a vessel). Absol.: ῥίμφα διώκοντες Od. 12.182. In pass., of a vessel, to be propelled by any agency, course along: ῥίμφα διωκομένη Od. 13.162.
δίωμαι aor. subj. δίεμαι.
διῶσε 3 sing. aor. subj. διωθέω.
δμηθήτω 3 sing. aor. imp. pass. δαμάζω.
δμῆσις ἡ [δμη-, δαμάζω.] Control, handling Il. 17.476.
δμήτειρα ἡ [as δμῆσις.] The subduer (cf. πανδαμάτωρ): νὺξ δ. θεῶν καὶ ἀνδρῶν Il. 14.259.

δμῳή -ῆς, ἡ [δμ-, δαμάζω.] A bondwoman, a female servant (cf. ἀμφίπολος) Il. 6.375, 376, Il. 9.658, Il. 18.28, Il. 22.449, Il. 23.550, Il. 24.582, 587, 643: Od. 1.147, Od. 2.412, Od. 4.49, Od. 6.307, Od. 15.461, Od. 17.34, etc. Of Calypso's servants Od. 5.199. With γυνή. See γυνή 3.

δμώς -ωός, ὁ [as δμῳή.] Genit. pl. δμώων Od. 1.398, Od. 9.206, Od. 14.59, Od. 17.402, etc. Dat. δμώεσσι Od. 6.71, Od. 11.431, Od. 15.379, Od. 24.213, etc. δμωσί Od. 17.389. A bondman, a man-servant Il. 19.333: = Od. 7.225, Od. 4.644, Od. 6.69, Od. 11.190, Od. 17.299, Od. 24.210, etc. With ἀνήρ Od. 16.305.

δνοπαλίζω 2 sing. fut. δνοπαλίξεις Od. 14.512. App., to knock aside or about, or, to shake: ἀνὴρ ἄνδρʼ ἐδνοπάλιζεν Il. 4.472. Of clothes, app., metaphorically, to knock them about; or perh., to flutter or flaunt them: τὰ σὰ ῥάκεα δνοπαλίξεις Od. 14.512.
δνοφερός -ή, -όν [δνόφος, darkness.] 1 Dark, devoid of light Od. 13.269, Od. 15.50. 2 Dark in hue Il. 9.15 = Il. 16.4.

δοάσσατο 3 sing. sing. aor. [app. conn. with δοκέω.] 3 sing. subj. δοάσσεται Il. 23.339. To seem, appear. With infin.: ἄκρον ἱκέσθαι Il. 23.339. Impers.: κέρδιον εἶναι Il. 13.458 = Il. 14.23 = Il. 16.652: = Od. 15.204 = Od. 18.93 = Od. 22.338 = Od. 24.239, Od. 5.474 = Od. 6.145, Od. 10.153.
δοθείη 3 sing. aor. opt. pass. δίδωμι.
δοιή -ῆς, ἡ [δοιός.] Doubt Il. 9.230.
δοίην aor. opt. δίδωμι.
δοκεύω [δοκ-, δέχομαι.] To watch, keep an eye upon: μεταστρεφθέντα (for his turning away) Il. 13.545, Ὠρίωνα Il. 18.488: = Od. 5.274. Cf. Il. 8.340, Il. 16.313, Il. 23.325.

δοκέω 1 To seem, appear. With infin.: ὃς δοκέει χαριέστατος εἶναι Il. 6.90. Cf. Il. 23.459, 470: Od. 1.227, Od. 2.33, Od. 5.342, Od. 6.258, Od. 8.388, Od. 17.415, Od. 18.18, 125, Od. 20.93. Impers.: ὥς μοι δοκεῖ εἶναι ἄριστα Il. 9.103 = 314 = Il. 13.735. Cf. Il. 6.338, Il. 12.215: Od. 1.376 = Od. 2.141, Od. 5.360, Od. 13.154, Od. 18.354, Od. 23.130. 2 To seem likely to . . . With fut. infin.: οὔ μοι δοκέει μύθοιο τελευτὴ κρανέεσθαι Il. 9.625. 3 To seem or appear to oneself, think oneself. With infin.: δοκέεις τις μέγας ἔμμεναι Od. 18.382. 4 To think, suppose, fancy, imagine. With pres. infin.: δόκησε σφίσι θυμὸς ὣς ἔμεν ὡς εἰ . . . Od. 10.415. With fut. infin.: νικησέμεν Il. 7.192.

data.quote: οὔ μοι δοκέει μύθοιο τελευτὴ κρανέεσθαι
δόκησε σφίσι θυμὸς ὣς ἔμεν ὡς εἰ . . .

definition: δοκός ἡ [δοκ-, δέχομαι.] A beam supporting a roof Od. 19.38, Od. 22.176, 193. A piece of timber intended to be used as such a beam Il. 17.744.
δόλιος -η, -ον [δόλος.] 1 Characterized by or showing craft or guile Od. 4.455, 529, Od. 9.282. 2 Craftily and skilfully arranged: κύκλον Od. 4.792.
δολίχαυλος -ον [δολιχός + αὐλός 3.] With long αὐλός: αἰγανέας Od. 9.156 (meaning simply long ; the second element not to be pressed).
δολιχεγχής [δολιχός + ἔγχος.] With long spears Il. 21.155.
δολιχήρετμος -ον [δολιχός + ἐρετμόν.] With long oars. Epithet of the Phaeacians Od. 8.191 = 369 = Od. 13.166. Of ships Od. 4.499, Od. 19.339, Od. 23.176.

δολιχός -ή, -όν. 1 Long Il. 4.533, Il. 7.255, Il. 9.86, Il. 13.162, Il. 15.474, Il. 17.607: Od. 3.169, Od. 4.393, 483, Od. 17.426, Od. 19.448. Of time: νύκτα δολιχὴν σχέθεν (so as to be . . . ) Od. 23.243. Of a disease, long drawn-out, protracted Od. 11.172. 2 In neut. sing. δολιχόν as adv., for a long time, for long, long Il. 10.52.

δολιχόσκιος [doubtfully explained as fr. δολιχός + σκιή, casting a long shadow, long.] Epithet of spears: ἔγχος Il. 3.346, 355, Il. 5.15, Il. 6.44, Il. 7.213, Il. 13.509, Il. 16.801, Il. 20.262, Il. 21.139, Il. 23.798, etc.: Od. 19.438, Od. 22.95, 97, Od. 24.519, 522.
δολόεις -εσσα [δόλος.] 1 Crafty, wily Od. 7.245, Od. 9.32. 2 Craftily or cunningly made Od. 8.281.
δολομήτης -ου [δόλος + μῆτις.] Crafty of counsel, wily. Absol. in voc. δολομῆτα Il. 1.540.
δολόμητις [as δολομήτης.] = δολομήτης. Od. 1.300 = Od. 3.198 = 308, Od. 3.250, Od. 4.525, Od. 11.422.

δόλος -ου, ὁ. 1 Bait for catching fish Od. 12.252. 2 Any cunningly made contrivance for ensnaring or bringing into one's power. Of the bonds forged by Hephaestus Od. 8.276, 282, 317. Of the Trojan horse Od. 8.494. 3 Any cunning or crafty contrivance, a trick or stratagem Il. 3.202, Il. 4.339, Il. 6.187, Il. 11.430, Il. 15.14, Il. 18.526: Od. 2.93, Od. 3.119, 122, Od. 4.437, 453, Od. 5.356, Od. 9.19, 422, Od. 10.232, 258, 380, Od. 11.439, Od. 13.292, 293, Od. 19.137, Od. 24.128. 4 Guile, craft, cunning, trickery: ἔπεφνε δόλῳ Il. 7.142. Cf. Il. 21.599, 604, Il. 23.585: ἠὲ δόλῳ ἢ ἀμφαδόν Od. 1.296, Od. 11.120. Cf. Od. 2.106 = Od. 24.141, Od. 2.368, Od. 9.406, 408, Od. 19.212.– (The) contrivance or plotting: ὑπʼ Αἰγίσθοιο δόλῳ Od. 3.235. Cf. Od. 4.92. Craftiness, cunning: δόλου οὐ λήθετο Il. 23.725. Cf. Od. 23.321.
δολοφρονέω [δόλος + φρονέω.] To have guile in one's heart, plan trickery Il. 3.405, Il. 14.197, 300 = 329 = Il. 19.106: Od. 10.339, Od. 18.51 = Od. 21.274.
δολοφροσύνη -ης, ἡ [δολόφρων, fr. δόλος + φρήν.] Trickery, deceit Il. 19.112. In pl.: δολοφροσύνῃς ἀπάτησεν Il. 19.97.
δόμεν1, 1 pl. aor. δίδωμι.
δόμεν2,δόμεναι aor. infin. δίδωμι.

δόμονδε [acc. of δόμος + -δε 1.] 1 To the house Od. 22.479, Od. 24.220. 2 Home, to one's home Il. 24.717. So ὅνδε δόμονδε Il. 16.445: Od. 1.83 = Od. 14.424 = Od. 20.239 = Od. 21.204, Od. 3.272, Od. 17.527, Od. 20.329.

δόμος -ου, ὁ [δεμ-, δέμω. Cf. δῶμα, L. domus.] 1 A house or abode Il. 2.513, 701, Il. 9.382, Il. 10.267, Il. 18.290, Il. 24.673, etc.: Od. 1.126, Od. 4.43, Od. 6.302, Od. 16.274, Od. 18.8, Od. 20.361, etc. In pl. in the same sense: δόμοις ἔνι ποιητοῖσιν Il. 5.198. Cf. Il. 6.370, Il. 11.132, Il. 14.202, Il. 23.84, etc.: Od. 1.380, Od. 3.313, Od. 6.303, Od. 15.465, etc. 2 Of the house or realm of Hades: δόμον Ἄϊδος Il. 3.322. Cf. Il. 7.131, Il. 11.263, Il. 14.457, Il. 20.336, Il. 24.246: Od. 9.524, Od. 10.512, Od. 11.69, 150, 627, Od. 23.252, 322. So in pl.: Ἀΐδαο δόμοισιν Il. 22.52, 482, Il. 23.19 = 179, Il. 23.103: Od. 4.834 = Od. 24.264, Od. 10.175, 491 = 564, Od. 14.208, Od. 15.350, Od. 20.208, Od. 24.204. 3 A temple: Ἐρεχθῆος Od. 7.81. Cf. Il. 6.89. 4 Of a nest of wasps or bees Il. 12.169. Of a sheepfold Il. 12.301 = Od. 6.134. 5 With a distinguishing word: χαλκήϊον Od. 18.328 (see χαλκήϊος). 6 Applied to particular parts of a house. a To Penelope's quarters Od. 1.330, Od. 21.5. b To the μέγαρον (sometime difficult to say whether the word should be taken in this restricted sense): δόμον κάτα δαινυμένοισιν Od. 17.332. Cf. Od. 2.322, Od. 7.144, Od. 22.199, 291, 381, 440, 455.
δονακεύς [δόναξ.] A thicket of reeds Il. 18.576.
δόναξ -ακος, ὁ [δονέω.] 1 A reed Il. 10.467: Od. 14.474. 2 The shaft of an arrow: ἐκλάσθη δ. Il. 11.584.
δονέω 1 To shake, cause to quiver Il. 17.55. 2 To drive about, put in commotion: βόας οἶστρος Od. 22.300. Of the wind driving clouds Il. 12.157.
δόντες nom. pl. masc. aor. pple. δίδωμι.
δόξα -ης, ἡ [δοξ-, δοκέω.] What one expects: ἀπὸ δόξης (away from, i. e. such or so as to fall short of or disappoint, expectation) Il. 10.324: Od. 11.344.
δορός -οῦ, ὁ [δέρω.] A leathern bag Od. 2.354, 380.
δορπέω [δόρπον.] To take δόρπον Il. 23.11: Od. 7.215, Od. 8.539, Od. 15.302 (twice).

δόρυ τό. Genit. δουρός (for δορϝός) Il. 3.61, Il. 17.295, Il. 23.529, etc.: Od. 19.453. δούρατος Il. 11.357. Dat. δουρί Il. 1.303, Il. 15.420, Il. 22.246, etc.: Od. 8.229, Od. 16.441, Od. 22.92, etc. δούρατι Il. 13.77: Od. 5.371. Nom. dual δοῦρε Il. 10.76: Od. 18.377. Acc. δοῦρε Il. 3.18, Il. 12.298, Il. 21.145, etc.: Od. 1.256, Od. 12.228, Od. 16.295, Od. 22.101, 125. Nom. pl. δοῦρα Il. 2.135, Il. 11.571, Il. 19.361, etc.: Od. 12.441. δούρατα Il. 5.656, Il. 12.36, Il. 13.264: Od. 5.361. Genit. δούρων Il. 22.243: Od. 17.384. Dat. δούρεσσι Il. 12.303: Od. 8.528. δούρασι Il. 21.162. Acc. δοῦρα Il. 5.495, Il. 6.3, Il. 24.450, etc.: Od. 5.243, Od. 12.443, Od. 22.144, etc. δούρατα Il. 5.618, Il. 13.260, Il. 17.234, etc.: Od. 5.162, Od. 22.110, 251, etc. 1 A shoot or stem of a tree Od. 6.167. 2 A treetrunk, a piece of timber in the rough: δοῦρα κέρσαντες Il. 24.450. Cf. Il. 3.61: Od. 5.162, 243. 3 A beam, plank, or log: δοῦρα νεῶν Il. 2.135. Cf. Il. 12.36, Il. 15.410, Il. 17.744: τέκτονα δούρων Od. 17.384. Cf. Od. 5.361, 370, 371, Od. 9.384, 498, Od. 12.441, 443. Something made of beams or planks. Applied to the Trojan horse Od. 8.507. 4 The shaft of a spear: πῆλε κόλον δ. Il. 16.117 (perh. δ. in 114 should be taken in the same sense). 5 A spear Il. 2.382, Il. 4.490, Il. 8.258, Il. 13.130, Il. 17.355, Il. 21.145, etc.: Od. 1.256, Od. 8.229, Od. 11.532, Od. 14.277, Od. 16.295, Od. 22.101, etc. Used in hunting Il. 21.577: Od. 10.162, 164, Od. 19.448, 453. In guarding a sheepfold Il. 12.303. Personified: εἰ καὶ ἐμὸν δ. μαίνεται Il. 8.111. Fig.: δουρὶ δʼ ἐμῷ κτεάτισσα Il. 16.57. Cf. Il. 16.708, Il. 18.341.
δός aor. imp. δίδωμι.
δόσαν 3 pl. aor. δίδωμι.
δόσις ἡ [δο-, δίδωμι.] 1 A gift: δ. ὀλίγη τε φίλη τε (i.e. even a small gift is welcome) Od. 6.208. Cf. Il. 10.213: Od. 14.58, Od. 18.287. 2 A giving for use, a loan Od. 4.651.
δόσκον pa. iterative δίδωμι.
δότε aor. imp. pl. δίδωμι
δοτήρ -ῆρος, ὁ [δο-, δίδωμι.] One who gives out or distributes: ταμίαι, σίτοιο δοτῆρες Il. 19.44.
δότω 3 sing. aor. imp. δίδωμι.
δούλειος [δοῦλος, a slave. Cf. δούλη.] Of a slave: δούλειον ἐπιπρέπει (show like a slave's) Od. 24.252.
δούλη -ης, ἡ [cf. δούλειος.] A female slave: γέετʼ ἐκ δούλης (i.e. a captive) Od. 4.12. Cf. Il. 3.409.
δούλιος = δούλειος: δούλιον ἦμαρ. See ἦμαρ 4.c.
δουλιχόδειρος [δ(ο)ὐλιχός + δειρή.] Long-necked: κύκνων Il. 2.460 = Il. 15.692.
δουλοσύνη -ης, ἡ [as δούλειος.] Slavery Od. 22.423.
δοῦναι aor. infin. δίδωμι.

δουπέω (γδουπέω) [δοῦπος.] 3 pl. aor. ἐγδούπησαν Il. 11.45. Genit. sing. masc. pf. pple. δεδουπότος Il. 23.679 (app. formed direct fr. δοῦπος. Cf. ἀρημένος, κεκοπώς, πεφυζότες.) (ἐν-.) 1 To give forth a sound: δούπησε πεσών (fell with a thud) Il. 4.504 = Il. 5.42 = 540 = Il. 13.187 = Il. 17.50 = 311, Il. 5.617, Il. 11.449, Il. 13.373, 442, Il. 15.421, 524, 578, Il. 16.325, 401, 599, 822, Il. 17.580, Il. 20.388: Od. 22.94, Od. 24.525. App., to thunder Il. 11.45. 2 To fall in fight, be slain Il. 13.426. App., simply, to die: δεδουπότος οἰδιπόδαο Il. 23.679.

δοῦπος -ου, ὁ (γδοῦπος. Cf. ἐρίγδουπος). A sound or noise. Of the roaring of the sea Od. 5.401, Od. 12.202. Of the roar of rushing and meeting waters Il. 4.455. Of noise or din in battle: ἐς δοῦπον ἀκόντων (to where the sound is, i.e. to battle) Il. 11.364 = Il. 20.451, δοῦπον ἀκόντων (the whiz) Il. 16.361, τεῖχος ὕπερ δ. ὀρώρει Il. 12.289. Cf. Il. 9.573, Il. 16.635.– Of the sound of persons approaching or moving: ἐπερχομένων δ. Il. 23.234. Cf. Il. 10.354: Od. 10.556, Od. 16.10.

data.ref: Il. 16.635.– Of the sound of persons approaching or moving:

definition: δουράτεος [δουρατ-, δόρυ.] Made of beams or planks. Of the Trojan horse Od. 8.493, 512.
δούρατος genit. δόρυ.
δουρηνεκής [δουρ-, δόρυ + ἐνεκ-. See φέρω.] In neut. sing. δουρηνεκές as adv., as far as a spear carries, a spear-throw: ἄπεσαν Il. 10.357.

δουρικλειτός [δουρί, dat. of δόρυ + κλειτός.] Famous with, i.e., for, the spear, renowned in fight. Epithet of Menelaus Il. 5.55, 578, Il. 10.230, Il. 23.355: Od. 15.52, Od. 17.116, 147. Of Diomedes Il. 11.333.

δουρικλυτός [as δουρικλειτός. + κλυτός.] = δουρικλειτός. Epithet of Idomeneus Il. 2.645, 650, Il. 5.45, Il. 13.210, 467, 476.– Of Tlepolemus Il. 2.657. Of Meges Il. 5.72. Of Diomedes Il. 11.368.– Of Odysseus Il. 11.396, 401, 661 = Il. 16.26. Of the Lesser Aias Il. 14.446. Of Automedon Il. 16.472. Of Meriones Il. 16.619. Of Achilles Il. 21.233. Of Peiraeus Od. 15.544, Od. 17.71.
δουρικτητός -ή [as δουρικλυτός. + κτητός.] Won by the spear, a captive. Of Briseis Il. 9.343.
δουροδόκη -ης, ἡ [δουρ-, δόρυ + δοκ-, δέχομαι.] A rack or stand for holding spears Od. 1.128.
δουρός genit. δόρυ.
δοῦσα aor. pple. fem. δίδωμι.
δόχμιος = δοχμός. In neut. pl. δόχμια as adv., across-hill: ἄναντα κάταντα πάραντά τε δ. τε Il. 23.116 (hardly to be distinguished from πάραντα).

data.quote: ἄναντα κάταντα πάραντά τε δ. τε

definition: δοχμός (ἀποδοχμόω). Taking a slanting direction: ἀΐσσοντε (slantwise) Il. 12.148.
δράγμα -ατος, τό [δραγ-, δράσσομαι.] An armful; in reaping, the corn cut by a sweep of the sickle, a swath Il. 11.69, Il. 18.552.
δραγμεύω [as δράγμα.] In reaping, to pick up the cut corn in armfuls Il. 18.555.
δραίνω [desiderative fr. δράω.] To be for doing, be minded to do: εἴ τι δραίνεις Il. 10.96.
δράκων -οντος, ὁ [prob. fr. δρακ-, δέρκομαι.] (With fem. reference in Il. 6.181.) A serpent or snake Il. 2.308, Il. 3.33, Il. 6.181, Il. 11.26, 39, Il. 12.202 = 220, Il. 22.93: Od. 4.457.
δράμε 3 sing. aor. τρέχω.
†δράσσομαι Pf. pple. δεδραγμένος. To clutch at, grasp. With genit.: κόνιος δεδραγμένος Il. 13.393 = Il. 16.486.
δρατός [metathesis of δαρτός, fr. δέρω.] Skinned, flayed: σώματα Il. 23.169.
†δράω Opt. δρώοιμι. (παρα-, ὑπο-.) To do, accomplish: ἅσσʼ ἐθέλοιεν Od. 15.317.
δρεπάνη -ης, ἡ [δρέπω.] A sickle Il. 18.551.
δρέπανον -ου, τό [as δρεπάνη.] = δρεπάνη. Od. 18.368.
δρέπω To pluck, pick off. In mid. Od. 12.357.
δρήστειρα ἡ [fem. of δρηστήρ.] A female servant: αἳ δῶμα κάτα δρήστειραι ἔασιν Od. 19.345. Cf. Od. 10.349.
δρηστήρ -ῆρος, ὁ [agent-noun fr. δράω.] A manservant Od. 16.248, Od. 18.76, Od. 20.160.
δρηστοσύνη -ης, ἡ [δράω.] Domestic service, household work Od. 15.321.

δριμύς -εῖα, -ύ. Of the pains of child birth, sharp, piercing Il. 11.270. Of wrath, bitter, piercing Il. 18.322. Of fighting, bitter, keenly contested Il. 15.696. Applied to passion manifesting itself outwardly (and app. likened to smarting tears) Od. 24.319.
δρίος [δρῦς. For δρϝ-ος.] A coppice Od. 14.353.

δρόμος -ου, ὁ [δρομ-, δραμ-, τρέχω.] 1 Running Il. 18.281. A running: δρόμου ἰσχανόωσαν (for the race) Il. 23.300, ὡς μεμνέῳτο δρόμους 361 (app., the running of the various chariots. Not laps, as the course seems to be only out and home. V.l. δρόμου, the running simply), πύματον τέλεον δρόμον (the last part of the race, i.e. that from the turn home) 373, 768. Cf. Il. 23.375, 526, 758: Od. 8.121. 2 A race-course Il. 23.321. 3 A piece of ground suited to horses Od. 4.605.

data.ref: 361 (app., the running of the various chariots. Not

definition: δρύϊνος [δρῦς.] Oaken, or perh., wooden Od. 21.43.

δρυμά τά [δρῦς.] 1 Thickets, coppices (prob. not nec. of oak) Il. 11.118: Od. 10.251. 2 The pl. app. expressing vague mass or quantity rather than plurality: ἐείσατο καπνὸς διὰ δ. Od. 10.150. Cf. Od. 10.197.
δρύοχοι οἱ [δρῦς + ὀχ-, ἔχω.] Stays or trestles supporting the keel of a ship under construction Od. 19.574.

δρύπτω (ἀπο-, περι-) To tear away or strip off: ἀπό κε ῥινοὺς δρύφθη (would have had his skin stripped off) Od. 5.426. Cf. Il. 16.324. In mid. of reciprocal action Od. 2.153 (tearing each other's . . .).

δρῦς δρυός, ἡ [cognate with Eng. tree, doubtless the orig. sense. Cf. δρίος, δρύϊνος, δρυμά, δρύοχοι, δρυτόμος.] Pl. δρύες Il. 12.132. Acc. δρῦς Il. 11.494, Il. 23.118. 1 An oak Il. 11.494, Il. 12.132, Il. 13.389 = Il. 16.482, Il. 14.398, 414, Il. 18.558, Il. 23.118: Od. 12.357, Od. 14.328 = Od. 19.297. 2 A felled oak or a piece thereof: ξύλον δρυός Il. 23.328. Cf. Od. 9.186, Od. 14.12, 425. 3 In phrase οὐκ ἀπὸ δρυὸς οὐδʼ ἀπὸ πέτρης Il. 22.126: Od. 19.163, an obscure proverbial expression. In Il. 22. the sense seems to be giving utterance to thoughts from any source as they arise, with unconsidered or idle words. In Od. 19. the sense seems to be for you are sprung (from men) not from . . .

data.ref: Od. 19.163, an obscure proverbial expression. In Il. 22. the sense seems to be

data.quote: οὐκ ἀπὸ δρυὸς οὐδʼ ἀπὸ πέτρης

definition: δρυτόμος -ου, ὁ [δρῦς + τομ-, τάμνω.] A wood-cutter Il. 11.86, Il. 16.633, Il. 23.315.
δρώοιμι opt. δράω.
δῦ 3 sing. aor. δύω.
†δυάω [δύη.] 3 pl. δυόωσι. To afflict Od. 20.195.
δύη -ης, ἡ. Suffering, misery: δ. μʼ ἔχει Od. 14.215, δύης πῆμα (sorrow of suffering, sorrow and suffering) 338. Cf. Od. 18.53, 81.
δύη 3 sing. aor. opt. δύω.
δύῃ 3 sing. aor. subj. δύω.
δῦθι aor. imp. δύω.
δύμεναι δῦναι aor. infin. δύω.

δύναμαι 2 sing. subj. δύνηαι Il. 6.229. Opt. δυναίμην Il. 18.464: Od. 9.523. 2 sing. δύναιο Od. 4.388. 3 sing. δύναιτο Od. 4.644. Genit. sing. masc. pple. δυναμένοιο Od. 1.276, Od. 11.414. Fut. δυνήσομαι Il. 1.588. 2 sing. -εαι Il. 1.241, 562, Il. 13.729. 3 sing. -εται Il. 19.163: Od. 1.78, Od. 2.191, Od. 10.291, Od. 21.403. 3 sing. aor. (ἐ)δυνήσατο Il. 5.621, Il. 13.510, 607, 647, Il. 14.33, 423: Od. 17.303. 1 pl. subj. δυνησόμεθα Od. 16.238. 3 sing. aor. (ἐ)δυνάσθη Il. 23.465: Od. 5.319. 1 To be able, have the power, ability or strength, be in a position, to do something. With infin.: τεύχεʼ ὤμοιιν ἀφελέσθαι Il. 5.621. Cf. Il. 1.241, Il. 2.343, Il. 3.236, Il. 6.101, Il. 13.634, etc.: ἐριδαινέμεν οἶος Od. 1.78. Cf. Od. 2.191, Od. 3.89, Od. 4.374, Od. 18.230, Od. 21.171, etc. Of things: οὐδέ μοι αἷμα τερσῆναι δύναται (as if it was striving) Il. 16.519. Cf. Il. 14.33. With ellipse of infin.: δύναται ἅπαντα Od. 4.237. Cf. Il. 6.229: Od. 10.306, Od. 14.445. Absol.: εἰ δύνασαί γε Il. 1.393. Cf. Il. 20.360: μέγα δυναμένοιο (possessed of great power or influence) Od. 1.274, Od. 11.414, δύναμαι γάρ Od. 4.612, δύνασαι γάρ (thou well knowest how to do it) Od. 5.25. Cf. Od. 4.827, Od. 16.208. 2 Of moral possibility: τελευτὴν ποιῆσαι (cannot make up her mind to . . .) Od. 1.250 = Od. 16.127, προλιπεῖν δε (have not the heart to . . .) Od. 13.331.

δύναμις ἡ [δύναμαι.] 1 Power, strength, might: ὅση δ. γε πάρεστιν Il. 8.294, Il. 13.786. Cf. Il. 13.787, Il. 22.20, Il. 23.891: Od. 2.62, Od. 3.205, Od. 20.237 = Od. 21.202, Od. 23.128. 2 Power to do something: ἀκέσασθε: δ. γὰρ ἐν ὑμῖν Od. 10.69.
δυνάσθη 3 sing. aor. δύναμαι.
δύνηαι 2 sing. subj. δύναμαι.
δυνήσατο 3 sing. aor. δύναμαι.
δύντα acc. sing. masc. aor. pple. δύω.

δύο δύω indeclinable. (The forms about equally common. Used with both dual and pl.) Two Il. 1.16, 250, Il. 2.731, Il. 3.18, Il. 5.159, Il. 10.253, etc.: Od. 1.256, Od. 4.27, 496, Od. 5.388, Od. 8.312, Od. 10.515, etc. Absol.: δύω μοι ἕπεσθον Il. 22.450. Cf. Il. 2.346, Il. 10.224, Il. 20.271, Il. 23.174, etc.: Od. 2.22, Od. 6.63, Od. 14.74, etc. With other numerals: δύω καὶ εἴκοσι Il. 2.748: Od. 9.241, Od. 10.208.– δύω καὶ πεντήκοντα Od. 8.35, 48, Od. 16.247.

δυοκαίδεκα indeclinable [ = δυώδεκα, δώδεκα.] Twelve Il. 2.557, Il. 6.93 = 274, 308, Il. 10.560, Il. 11.228, Il. 20.225: Od. 8.59, Od. 14.13, Od. 18.293, Od. 19.578 = Od. 21.76. Absol.: δ. πάντες ἄριστοι Od. 16.251. Cf. Od. 9.195.
δυόωσι 3 pl. δυάω.
δυσαής [δυσ- 1 + ἄημι.] Genit. pl. δυσαήων Od. 13.99. Of winds, blowing with violence, stormy, blustering Il. 5.865, Il. 23.200: Od. 5.295, Od. 12.289, Od. 13.99.
δῦσαι aor. infin. δύω.
δυσάμμορος -ον [δυσ- 2 + ἄμμορος.] Dogged by persistent evil fate, most miserable Il. 19.315, Il. 22.428, 485, Il. 24.727.
δύσαντο 3 pl. aor. mid. δύω.
δυσαριστοτόκεια [δυσ- 1 + ἄριστος + τοκ-, τίκτω.] That bare the noblest of sons to an evil fate Il. 18.54.
δύσετο 3 sing. aor. mid. δύω.
δύσζηλος [δυσ- 2 + ζῆλος, jealousy.] Apt to put a bad construction on things, suspicious Od. 7.307.
δυσηλεγής [δυσ- 2 + ἀλεγ-, ἀλεγεινός.] Bringing much woe. Epithet of war Il. 20.154. Of death Od. 22.325.
δυσηχής [δυσ- 2 + ἄχος.] Bringing much woe. Epithet of war Il. 2.686, Il. 7.376 = 395, Il. 11.524, 590, Il. 13.535, Il. 18.307. Of death Il. 16.442 = Il. 22.180, Il. 18.464.
δυσθαλπής [δυσ- 1 + θάλπω.] Evil in the matter of heat, cold: χειμῶνος Il. 17.549.
δύσκε 3 sing. pa. iterative δύω.
δυσκέλαδος [δυσ- 1 + κέλαδος.] III-sounding, evil to the ears: φόβοιο Il. 16.357.
δυσκηδής [δυσ- 2 + κῆδος.] Bringing pain or discomfort: νύκτα Od. 5.466.
δυσκλεής [δυσ- 1 + κλέος.] Acc. δυσκλέα (for δυσκλεέα). With smirched fame Il. 2.115 = Il. 9.22.
δυσμενέων pres. pple. [δυσμενής.] Bearing ill-will, in enemy wise: εἰ δ. κάκʼ ἔρεξεν Od. 2.72. Cf. Od. 2.73, Od. 20.314.

δυσμενής [δυσ- 1 + μένος.] Dat. pl. δυσμενέεσσι Il. 5.488, Il. 10.193, Il. 22.403, etc.: Od. 3.90, Od. 14.218, Od. 17.289, etc. δυσμενέσι Il. 3.51. 1 Bearing ill-will, hostile, enemy Il. 5.488, Il. 6.453, Il. 10.40, 100, 221, 395, Il. 13.263, Il. 17.158, Il. 19.168, 232, Il. 24.288, 365: Od. 3.90, Od. 4.246, 319, Od. 6.200, Od. 8.217, Od. 14.221, Od. 15.387, Od. 22.234. 2 Absol. in pl., enemies, foes, the foe: μάχεσθαι δυσμενέεσσιν Il. 16.521. Cf. Il. 3.51, Il. 10.193, Il. 19.62, Il. 22.403: δυσμενέες καὶ ἀνάρσιοι (i.e. pirates) Od. 14.85. Cf. Od. 4.822, Od. 6.184, Od. 14.218, Od. 16.121, 234, Od. 17.289.
δυσμήτηρ [δυσ- 1 + μήτηρ.] In voc. δύσμητερ, mother of an ill sortOd. 23.97.
δύσμορος [δυσ- 1 + μόρος.] Doomed to an evil fate, ill-starred, unlucky Il. 22.60, 481: Od. 1.49, Od. 7.270, Od. 16.139, Od. 20.194, Od. 24.290, 311.
δύσομαι fut. mid. δύω.
δυσομένου genit. sing. masc. aor. pple. mid. δύω.
Δύσπαρις [δυσ- 1 + Πάρις.] In voc. δύσπαρι, Paris, thou wretchIl. 3.39 = Il. 13.769.
δυσπέμφελος [δυσ-. Second element obscure.] Stormy: [πόντος] Il. 16.748.
δυσπονής [δυσ- 2 + πόνος.] Distressing Od. 5.493.

δύστηνος -ον [δυσ-. Second element obscure.] Wretched, unhappy, miserable, unfortunate Il. 17.445, Il. 22.477: Od. 1.55, Od. 4.182, Od. 5.436, Od. 11.76, Od. 13.331, Od. 17.10, 483, 501, Od. 19.354, Od. 24.289. Absol.: δυστήνων παῖδες Il. 6.127 = Il. 21.151. Cf. Il. 22.59: Od. 6.206, Od. 7.223, 248, Od. 10.281, Od. 11.80, 93, Od. 20.224.
δυσχείμερος -ον [δυσ- 2 + χεῖμα.] Vexed by bitter weather, inclement. Of Dodona Il. 2.750, Il. 16.234.
δύσω fut. δύω.
δυσώνυμος -ον [δυσ- 1 + ὄνυμα, Aeolic form of ὄνομα.] Of ill name, accursed Il. 6.255, Il. 12.116: Od. 19.571.
†δυσωρέομαι [app. δυσ- 1 + ὥρη, care, concern.] 3 pl. aor. subj. δυσωρήσωνται (most MSS. -ονται, prob. the orig. form). To keep painful watch Il. 10.183.
δῦτε 2 pl. aor. imp. δύω.
δύω two. See δύο.

δύνω δύω 3 sing. pa. iterative δύσκε Il. 8.271. Fut. δύσω Il. 2.261. 3 pl. sigmatic aor. ἔδυσαν Od. 14.341. Infin. δῦσαι Il. 5.435, Il. 13.182. 3 sing. aor. ἔδυ Il. 3.36, Il. 11.63, Il. 18.241, etc.: Od. 3.329, Od. 13.35, Od. 16.220, etc. δῦ Il. 8.85, Il. 17.210, Il. 18.416, Il. 21.118. 3 dual ἐδύτην Il. 6.19, Il. 10.254, 272. 2 pl. ἔδυτε Od. 24.106. 3 pl. ἔδυσαν Il. 18.145. ἔδυν Il. 4.222, Il. 11.263. Subj. δύω Il. 6.340, Il. 7.193, Il. 17.186, Il. 18.192, Il. 21.559, Il. 22.99, 125. 2 sing. δύῃς Il. 9.604. 3 sing. δύῃ Il. 11.194, 209, Il. 17.455. 3 sing. opt. δύη (for δυίη) Od. 18.348, Od. 20.286. Imp. δῦθι Il. 16.64. 3 sing. δύτω Il. 14.377. Pl. δῦτε Il. 18.140. Acc. sing. masc. pple. δύντα Il. 19.308. Nom. dual δύντε Od. 22.201. Infin. δύμεναι Il. 6.185, 411, Il. 14.63, Il. 19.313. δῦναι Il. 2.413, Il. 3.322, Il. 7.131, Il. 10.221, Il. 11.537, Il. 20.76: Od. 13.30. 3 sing. pf. δέδυκε Il. 5.811, Il. 9.239: Od. 12.93. Mid. Fut. δύσομαι Od. 12.383. 2 sing. -εαι Il. 9.231. 3 pl. -ονται Il. 7.298. Infin. -εσθαι Od. 7.18. 3 pl. aor. δύσαντο Il. 23.739. 3 pl. opt. δυσαίατο Il. 18.376. 3 sing. aor. (ἐ)δύσετο Il. 2.578, Il. 3.328, Il. 7.465, Il. 15.120, Il. 19.368, Il. 21.515, etc.: Od. 2.388, Od. 4.425, Od. 5.352, Od. 6.321, Od. 17.336, Od. 23.366, etc. Imp. δύσεο Il. 16.129, Il. 19.36: Od. 17.276. Genit. sing. masc. pple. δυσομένου Od. 1.24. (ἀνα-, ἀπο-, ἐκ-, ἐνδύνω, ἐξανα-, ἐξαποδύνω, ἐσ-, κατα-, περι-, ὑπεξανα-, ὑπο-.) I In fut. and sigmatic aor. act., with adverbs indicating deprivation, to strip off (clothes, etc.): εἰ μὴ ἀφʼ εἵματα δύσω Il. 2.261. Cf. Il. 5.435, Il. 13.182: Od. 14.341. Sim. in pres. subj., to put off (one's armour): ἐπεί κʼ ἀπὸ τεύχεα δύω Il. 22.125. II In the tenses other than the fut. and sigmatic aor. act. 1 In act. and mid., to enter, go into, make one's way into: δῦναι δόμον Ἄϊδος Il. 3.322, Il. 7.131, δύοντο τεῖχος Il. 15.345. Cf. Il. 6.19, 411, Il. 11.263, Il. 21.515, Il. 22.99: δέρτρον δύνοντες (thrusting their beaks into it) Od. 11.579, ἐδύσετο δώματα Od. 17.336. Cf. Od. 7.18, 81, Od. 13.366, Od. 24.106. To plunge into (the sea): δῦνε πόντον Il. 15.219. Cf. Il. 18.140. Of the apparent motion of a star: ἔδυ νέφεα Il. 11.63. Absol., to take its inward way, pass: δύνει ἀλοιφή Il. 17.392. Cf. Il. 16.340, Il. 21.118. 2 In act. and mid. with preps., to go, make one's way, place oneself (into or under something): βέλος εἰς ἐγκέφαλον δῦ Il. 8.85. Cf. Il. 5.140, Il. 8.271, Il. 21.559: οὓς ὑπʼ Ὀδυσσεὺς δύσετο Od. 5.482, μέσση κατὰ σπείους δέδυκεν (stands waist-deep) Od. 12.93. Cf. Od. 12.383. So of plunging into the sea: δύσεθʼ ἁλὸς κατὰ κῦμα Il. 6.136, ὑπὸ κῦμʼ ἔδυσαν Il. 18.145: ἐς πόντον ἐδύσετο Od. 5.352. Cf. Od. 4.425, 570 = Od. 11.253. 3 In act. and mid., to enter, mingle with (a throng or company, etc.): δῦναι ὅμιλον Il. 11.537, Il. 20.76. Cf. Il. 6.185, Il. 7.298, Il. 9.604, Il. 10.221, Il. 14.63, Il. 16.729, Il. 17.552, Il. 18.376, Il. 19.313, Il. 20.379: δύσεο μνηστῆρας (go among them, mix with them) Od. 17.276. Sim. with a prep.: καθʼ ὅμιλον ἔδυ Il. 3.36. 4 In act. and mid., to get into, put on (armour or clothes): ἐδύσετο χαλκόν Il. 2.578, Il. 11.16, ἔντεʼ ἔδυνεν Il. 3.339, δύσαντο χιτῶνας Il. 23.739. Cf. Il. 3.328, 332 = Il. 11.19 = Il. 16.133 = Il. 19.371, Il. 6.340, Il. 7.193, Il. 8.43 = Il. 13.25, Il. 9.596, Il. 13.241, Il. 14.382, Il. 15.120, Il. 16.64, 129, Il. 17.186, 194, 202, Il. 18.192, 416, Il. 19.368: χιτῶνα δῦνεν Od. 15.61, δυέσθην τεύχεα Od. 22.114. Cf. Od. 22.113, Od. 23.366. Of putting on the cap of Hades Il. 5.845. Sim. with preps.: κατὰ τεύχεʼ ἔδυν Il. 4.222. Cf. Il. 10.254, 272, Il. 23.131: ἐν τεύχεσσι δύοντο Od. 24.496. Cf. Od. 22.201, Od. 24.498. So ἐν ἀσπίδι δύτω Il. 14.377. Fig.: δύσεο δʼ ἀλκήν Il. 19.36. Cf. Il. 9.231. 5 In act. and mid., of the sun, to enter Ocean, set: δύσετʼ ἠέλιος Il. 7.465, ἔδυ φάος Il. 8.487. Cf. Il. 2.413, Il. 11.194 = 209 = Il. 17.455, Il. 18.241, Il. 19.308, Il. 23.154: Αἰθίοπες δυσομένου Ὑπερίονος (dwelling in the west) Od. 1.24. Cf. Od. 2.388 = Od. 3.487 = 497 = Od. 11.12 = Od. 15.185 = 296 = 471, Od. 3.329 = Od. 5.225, Od. 6.321, Od. 8.417, Od. 13.30, 35, Od. 16.220 = Od. 21.226. So of a constellation: ὀψὲ δύοντα βοώτην Od. 5.272. Sim.: δείελος ὀψὲ δύων Il. 21.232. 6 In act., of feelings or physical or mental states, to come upon, befall: κάματος γυῖα δέδυκεν Il. 5.811, Μελέαγρον ἔδυ χόλος Il. 9.553. Cf. Il. 9.239, Il. 11.268, 272, Il. 19.16, 367, Il. 22.94: ὄφρʼ ἔτι μᾶλλον δύη ἄχος κραδίην Od. 18.348 = Od. 20.286. Of a god, to inspire: δῦ μιν Ἄρης Il. 17.210.

data.quote: ὄφρʼ ἔτι μᾶλλον δύη ἄχος κραδίην

definition: δυώδεκα indeclinable [ = δυοκαίδεκα, δώδεκα.] Twelve Il. 2.637, Il. 18.230, Il. 21.27: Od. 9.159, 204, Od. 12.89, Od. 19.199. Absol.: ὄφρα δ. ἔπεφνεν Il. 10.488.
δυωδεκάβοιος [δυώδεκα + βοῦς.] Of the value of twelve oxen: δυωδεκάβοιον τῖον (at . . .) Il. 23.703.

δυωδέκατος -η [δυώδεκα. Cf. δωδέκατος.] 1 The twelfth: ἠώς Il. 1.493 = Il. 24.31, Il. 21.81, Il. 24.413. 2 δυωδεκάτη (sc. ἡμέρη), the twelfth day: δυωδεκάτῃ (on the twelfth day) Il. 21.46: ἑνδεκάτη τε δυωδεκάτη τε Od. 2.374, Od. 4.588. So τῇ δυωδεκάτῃ Il. 24.667.
δυωκαιεικοσίμετρος [μέτρον.] Holding twenty-two measures: τρίποδα Il. 23.264.
δυωκαιεικοσίπηχυς -υ [πῆχυς in sense cubit.] Twenty-two cubits long: ξυστόν Il. 15.678.
δῶ aor. subj. δίδωμι.
δωδέκατος -η [ = δυωδέκατος.] 1 The twelfth: ἠώς Il. 24.781. 2 δωδεκάτη (sc. ἡμέρη), the twelfth day: δωδεκάτῃ (on the twelfth day) Il. 1.425: πρὶν δωδεκάτην γενέσθαι Od. 4.747.
δώῃ δώῃσι 3 sing. aor. subj. δίδωμι.
δῶκα aor. δίδωμι.

δῶμα -ατος, τό [cf. δόμος.] 1 A house or abode: ὑψερεφὲς μέγα δ. Il. 5.213, θάλαμον καὶ δ. καὶ αὐλήν Il. 6.316 (app. the house in gen., a particular part, the θ., being specially mentioned; cf. Od. 22.494). Cf. Il. 1.18, Il. 2.854, Il. 14.121, Il. 15.143, Il. 21.44, etc.: πρὸς δ. (home) Od. 2.298, Ἀλκινόοιο δ. Od. 8.13. Cf. Od. 3.368, Od. 5.208, Od. 16.276, Od. 20.192, Od. 23.50, etc. In pl. in the same sense: ἐν δώμασʼ ἐμοῖσιν Il. 6.221. Cf. Il. 1.222, Il. 11.77, Il. 16.190, Il. 23.89, etc.: Od. 1.116, Od. 3.355, Od. 17.479, Od. 19.194, etc. 2 Of the house or realm of Hades: δ. Ἀΐδαο Il. 15.251: Od. 12.21. 3 Applied to particular parts of a house. a To Penelope's quarters. In pl. Od. 18.314. b To the μέγαρον (sometimes difficult to say whether the word should be taken in this restricted sense. In Od. 22.494 μέγαρον and δ. are app. distinguished): βῆ διὰ δ. Od. 7.139. Cf. Il. 4.386, Il. 15.101: Od. 1.228, Od. 2.247, Od. 4.15, 44, 46, Od. 7.85, Od. 17.329, 501, 541, 566, Od. 18.153, 341, Od. 20.149, 178, Od. 21.378, Od. 22.23, 307, 360, Od. 23.146. So in pl.: φαίνοντες κατὰ δώματα δαιτυμόνεσσιν Od. 7.102. Cf. Il. 1.600: Od. 4.72, Od. 9.7, Od. 17.531, Od. 20.159, Od. 21.234, Od. 22.22, Od. 24.183.
δώομεν δῶμεν 1 pl. aor. subj. δίδωμι.
δωρέομαι [δῶρον.] To give Il. 10.557.
δωρητός [δωρέομαι.] Open to gifts, that may be appeased by gifts Il. 9.526.

δῶρον -ου, τό [δω-, δίδωμι.] 1 A gift or present Il. 1.213, Il. 7.299, Il. 9.164, Il. 19.3, Il. 23.745, etc.: Od. 1.311, Od. 4.130, Od. 8.397, Od. 15.18, Od. 17.76, etc. 2 Something given as a return or reward: δώρῳ ἔπι μεγάλῳ Il. 10.304. Cf. Il. 9.576, 598, Il. 11.124, Il. 14.238, etc.: πόρε μοι δῶρα Od. 9.201. Cf. Od. 2.186, Od. 11.521, Od. 15.247. Of a share of spoil Il. 1.230. Of ransom for a corpse Il. 22.341, Il. 24.76, 119 = 147 = 176 = 196, 447, 458. 3 Something given or devoted to a god: δ. Ἀθήνῃ Il. 6.293. Cf. Il. 1.390, Il. 8.203, Il. 20.299, Il. 24.68, 425: Od. 13.358, Od. 16.185. 4 Of what is bestowed by the gods on mortals. Of one's lot or fortune: δώρων οἶα δίδωσι [Ζεύς] Il. 24.528. Cf. Il. 24.534: Od. 18.142. Of personal qualities: δῶρʼ Ἀφροδίτης Il. 3.54, 64. Cf. Il. 3.65: Od. 18.191. Of sleep: ὕπνου δ. ἕλοντο Il. 7.482, Il. 9.713: Od. 16.481, Od. 19.427. 5 Gifts more or less voluntary, benevolences (cf. δωτίνη 2): δώροισι κατατρύχω λαούς Il. 17.225.
δῶσι 3 pl. aor. subj. δίδωμι.
δῷσι 3 sing. aor. subj. δίδωμι.
δώσω fut. δίδωμι.
δωτήρ -ῆρος [δω-, δίδωμι.] A bestower Od. 8.325.
